To address these limitations, we adapt d3-flash through low-rank fine-tuning on public EO training splits, producing EO-Jev. EO-Jev improves significantly over d3-flash on 26 of 30 settings and matches or exceeds specialist references on 20 of 28. It also achieves an average gain of 8.0 points across 12 held-out settings and lower expected calibration error than specialists on 21 of 28 settings. These improvements come at a modest cost of 1.8 points in general decision performance. Our results demonstrate the potential of adapting general decision models into competitive EO generalists while highlighting persistent challenges in quantitative perception, option-order consistency, and calibration under distribution shift.

items.title_en: Fuse To Align: Multimodal Representation Learning for Retrieval via Hypergraph Regularization
items.abstract_en: Multimodal retrieval must integrate complementary evidence from views that may be missing, noisy, or unequally informative. When a sample provides limited reliable evidence, learning from its views alone can hinder the acquisition of useful retrieval representations. Semantically related training samples may provide complementary observations, yet existing volume-based objectives jointly align modalities within each sample without explicitly enabling information exchange across samples. We therefore propose a training-time hypergraph fusion framework that connects observed modalities both within samples and across semantically related samples, allowing representation learning to draw on evidence beyond an individual sample while leaving the retrieval pipeline unchanged at inference. The framework includes HyVol as a special case and introduces two configurations: wHyVol learns view contribution weights and symmetric semantic affinities, whereas wRHG additionally models typed interactions and participant roles through relational propagation. Missing modalities are omitted rather than imputed, and the hypergraph is discarded after training, incurring no additional inference cost. Experiments on eleven zero-shot video-text and audio-text retrieval benchmarks demonstrate broad improvements with both GRAM and HyperGRAM. Across 17 video benchmark-modality settings evaluated in both retrieval directions, wRHG outperforms GRAM in all 34 comparisons and HyperGRAM in 33 of 34. Mean text-to-video R@1 increases from 63.4 to 68.2 with GRAM and from 64.8 to 68.4 with HyperGRAM, while the largest video-to-text gain reaches 13.3 percentage points on ActivityNet. Under missing-modality evaluation, both weighted configurations retain positive text-to-video gains over GRAM across seven benchmarks at every evaluated missingness rate, even when 90% of clips lack one modality.

items.title_en: Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry
items.title_zh: 每个像素皆可选：一种用于医学超声生物测量的System One模型
items.abstract_en: **Purpose:** Ultrasound biometry is widely used across various clinical applications, including prenatal and cardiac examinations, to obtain quantitative measurements by placing calipers at anatomical landmarks. However, these measurements remain subject to interoperator variability as they rely largely on manual caliper placement. Conventional methods often use specialized prediction heads for different ultrasound tasks, whereas vision-language models offer flexibility through text instructions. However, direct coordinate prediction does not explicitly model spatial likelihood distributions, limiting the representation of localization ambiguity. **Methods:** We propose Kev-Bio, a vision-language model that uses clinical measurement questions to guide ultrasound landmark detection. Inspired by System One decision models, Kev-Bio uses decision representations of the language model to generate queries for each caliper endpoint. These queries are matched against shared dense ultrasound features to produce spatial probability maps, from which landmark coordinates and clinical measurements are derived. The model is trained end-to-end using both landmark localization and clinical measurement losses. **Results:** On the nine-view FU/GU Biometry 2026 dataset, Kev-Bio achieves a mean radial error (MRE) of 22.50 pixels and a clinical measurement mean absolute error (MAE) of 15.38, outperforming the compared baselines in overall performance. **Conclusion:** These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Kev-Bio for ultrasound landmark detection and clinical measurement across different anatomical views. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/moeinheidari7829/Kev-Bio.

items.title_en: Air-Scan-Based Point-Spread-Function Estimation for Megavoltage CT with Flat-Panel Detectors
items.abstract_en: Accurate spatial-resolution characterization of flat-panel detectors at megavoltage energies is difficult due to long-tailed cross-talk. Conventional measurements at high energy using line-pair gauges or knife-edge phantoms require expensive, carefully fabricated objects and precise alignment, and despite these, scatter from the phantom, detector, and imaging room can further confound the measurement. We present a method for estimating the detector point spread function (PSF) from the mean noise power spectrum (NPS) calculated from repeated radiographs in air. The approach is mathematically equivalent to an autocovariance-based method but is more practical for long-tailed PSFs. We validate the method using simulated air data and Monte Carlo N-particle (MCNP6) calculations of energy deposition in a flat-panel detector. We show that deconvolving the experimental PSF increases the accuracy of transmission radiographs of step wedges. The method requires no phantom or alignments and is straightforward to reproduce.

items.title_en: ArabGeoText: Tool-Augmented Vision-Language Models for Arabic Geospatial Text Spotting
items.abstract_en: Geospatial text spotting involves locating and transcribing geographic labels, such as road names, district names, and landmarks, in raster maps. These labels are often small, densely arranged, and arbitrarily oriented. Although Arabic text recognition has been studied extensively in documents and natural scenes, Arabic geospatial text spotting remains underexplored. We introduce ARABGEOTEXT, an Arabic-centric benchmark covering 970 geographic locations in Riyadh and Jeddah, with 17,875 manually annotated text instances per view type. For each location, we pair an OpenStreetMap (OSM) rendering with a composite created by overlaying that rendering on the corresponding remote sensing (RS) imagery. The paired views preserve label content and pixel geometry, allowing evaluation across different backgrounds. Geographic partitions support in-city and city-disjoint evaluation of detection, recognition, and end-to-end spotting. Experiments with direct Qwen3.5-4B spotting show difficulties in recovering all labels within a tile. We therefore propose a tool-augmented vision-language framework that combines YOLO26 localization and crop rectification with Qwen3.5-4B recognition adapted through low-rank adaptation (LoRA). The framework outperforms direct LoRA-adapted Qwen3.5-4B spotting across both image views and test cities. With localization held fixed, reader adaptation further improves recognition over the pretrained zero-shot reader. The dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yakoubbazi/ArabGeoText.

items.title_en: View optimization in Computed Tomography
items.abstract_en: Many emerging CT imaging applications must operate with data from sparse projection angles, on the order of 10 views, such as first responder scenarios, dynamic imaging of detonation events, and flash imaging of materials under extreme conditions in high energy-density science. Few-view imaging is a data undersampling problem, that degrades tomographic reconstructions with streaks, shadows, and other aliasing artifacts, due to ill-conditioning. In few- view CT, the specific set of projection angles can strongly impact reconstruction quality, and the optimal angles depend on the object being scanned. Despite a surge of recent research, there is much to explore in this problem. We present an object-aware performance prediction framework for few-view projection datasets based on a matrix decomposition of the discretized forward model augmented with expected object gradient information. The method yields a quantitative score for a candidate set of view angles that can underpin a view selection recommendation algorithm. A key feature is that it can be applied at multiple stages of acquisition: a priori, before any radiographs are taken, or adaptively, after some radiographs are collected, to determine the next best view. We demonstrate the approach using simulated CT data with 5 view and 15 view configurations. Preliminary results are encouraging; images reconstructed using a standard statistical algorithm show that reconstruction accuracy agrees with our performance score. Reconstruction accuracy was evaluated against a known ground truth using an information theoretic score. Continued testing with complex objects and multiple geometries is necessary.

items.title_en: Mesh-Agnostic Refinement Models for Latent Space Encoding of 3D Human Body Shapes
items.abstract_en: Parametric human body models such as the Skinned Multi-Person Linear (SMPL) model provide compact representations of human shape and pose, but their reconstructions remain affected by both errors in estimated latent parameters and limitations in the decoder's expressive capacity. We propose a framework for refining these reconstructions by exploiting the geometric discrepancy between an initial decoded surface and a target mesh, without requiring vertex correspondences between them. The framework comprises three complementary approaches. Latent-VaRefine uses varifold-distance gradients to correct the estimated latent code while preserving the original parametric representation. Vertex-VaRefine processes multiscale varifold-gradient features with a DiffusionNet backbone to predict vertex displacements in a canonical pose, yielding an approximately pose-equivariant refinement pipeline. ElaOpt directly optimizes surface deformations under elastic regularization and normal-direction constraints.

items.title_en: ReVA-HPE: Relative 6DoF Head Pose Estimation with Synthetic Pose Supervision and Personalized Virtual Anchors
items.abstract_en: Monocular head pose estimation is usually formulated as absolute regression from a single face crop, yet many applications observe the same person over time and can supply an explicit anchor image. Recently, relative head pose estimation was proposed, which casts the problem as estimation of the relative geometric change between an anchor and a query image. However, existing methods still require the anchor image pose to be known at inference, significantly limiting their practical use. We first extend relative head pose estimation to full 6DoF by additionally predicting a depth-normalized relative translation, which composes with the anchor to recover metric query pose in the camera frame. To eliminate the need for a ground-truth anchor pose, we reconstruct a personalized avatar from a single unlabeled enrollment image and render a bank of virtual anchors with known poses. The bank provides robust rotation hypotheses through multi-anchor consensus, while the real enrollment image serves as the real anchor in the translation branch via landmark PnP. We also introduce an efficient variant that amortizes the bank cost once at enrollment, after which each query requires a single real-to-real relative prediction, with limited accuracy sacrifice. The relative pose estimator is trained exclusively on synthetic face renderings, without real pose supervision, pseudo-labels, domain adaptation, or fine-tuning on the evaluation sets. On real 6DoF benchmarks, ReVA-HPE achieves state-of-the-art rotation accuracy on BIWI and, given a near-frontal enrollment image, on FaMoS, while remaining competitive in metric translation despite relying solely on synthetic pose supervision. Project page and code: https://vasilikivas.github.io/ReVA-HPE/

items.title_en: R$^2$-Omni: Reducing Structural and Precision Redundancy in Omni-LLMs for Long-Form Generation
items.abstract_en: Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) typically process large numbers of multimodal tokens from audio-visual inputs, incurring substantial computational costs and a large memory footprint for the key-value (KV) cache. Aggressive token pruning can alleviate this problem while maintaining competitive performance on multiple-choice tasks, which require only a single option as output. However, we observe substantial quality degradation when generating long-form, open-ended responses. We attribute this gap to query-guided selection, which can retain sufficient evidence for answer selection while discarding details needed for comprehensive generation. This motivates reducing overlapping information across tokens, termed structural redundancy, while preserving diverse content. However, the retained representations may still contain precision redundancy due to unnecessarily high numerical precision in their cached values. To address these two levels of redundancy in token representations, we introduce a training-free framework named R$^2$-Omni. First, Structure-Aware Token Consolidation (STC) consolidates redundant representations using spatiotemporal similarity in video and local continuity in audio. Then, Semantic-Sensitivity Guided Precision Allocation (SSPA) allocates value precision to the retained representations according to the estimated reduction in attention-output error under quantized keys, with query attention and audio-visual alignment providing a semantic prior. Extensive experiments on long-form generation benchmarks demonstrate an average 5.0$\times$ reduction in the memory footprint while preserving 97.98% of baseline generation quality and achieving a 1.48$\times$ end-to-end speedup, highlighting the benefits of jointly reducing structural and precision redundancy.

items.title_en: HyperFlow: Class-Incremental Semantic Change Detection via Hyperbolic Flow
items.abstract_en: Semantic change detection in remote sensing aims to identify and characterize land-cover transitions observed in pairs of satellite or aerial images. Existing methods assume a fixed set of change categories, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios where changes of interest may vary, for example across geographies or over time. In this work, we tackle the problem of class-incremental semantic change detection, where a model progressively learns to detect new types of semantic change. To do so, we exploit the hierarchical structure of land-cover semantics, where newly introduced categories correspond to fine-grained refinements of existing ones, and represent said semantic categories in hyperbolic space, which is particularly well suited to represent such hierarchical relationships. To capture semantic changes, we introduce HyperFlow, a method relying on Busemann prototypes, modeling change as an anomaly in a learned semantic flow within the hyperbolic embedding space induced by segmentation. HyperFlow couples change detection to class-incremental semantic segmentation, enabling class-incremental semantic change detection. We also present HiChange, a new large-scale, high resolution remote sensing dataset with detailed, fine-grained hierarchical labels. Experimental results demonstrate that HyperFlow achieves both strong change detection and semantic segmentation performance across incremental steps. In particular, we show that progressively refining semantic categories, rather than considering them all directly, yields improved change detection, highlighting the benefits of incremental learning for semantic change detection.

items.title_en: Calibrating Multimodal Test-Time Adaptation under Reliability and Availability Modality Shifts
items.abstract_en: Multimodal test-time adaptation (TTA) enables pretrained multimodal models to accommodate distribution shifts during inference using only unlabeled test data, without recourse to the original training data. Compared with unimodal adaptation, multimodal adaptation is further complicated by the coexistence and interaction of multiple representation perspectives. This complexity is particularly pronounced under modality reliability shifts, which preserve modality availability but degrade information quality, and modality availability shifts, which render the corresponding modality entirely inaccessible. Category-conditional Gaussian modeling offers a natural starting point for handling such distributional variations, having proven effective in unimodal test-time adaptation for characterizing representation distributions, yet its extension to multimodal settings requires a more elaborate formulation. To this end, we propose Adaptive Probabilistic Gaussian Calibration (AdaPGC), which extends category-conditional Gaussian modeling across modality-specific and multimodal fusion representations for probabilistic calibration under multimodal distribution shifts. AdaPGC continuously updates category-conditional Gaussian models over modality-specific and fusion representations, using the resulting probabilistic predictions to calibrate source model predictions and guide reliability based rectification, while exploiting their joint distributions to recover unavailable fusion representations. Extensive experiments under diverse modality corruption and missingness conditions demonstrate that AdaPGC effectively improves robustness under both modality reliability and availability shifts. Our source code will be released at https://github.com/XuJinglinn/AdaPGC-plus.

items.title_en: CL3DOD: Understanding the Stability-Plasticity Dilemma in Outdoor Class-Incremental 3D Object Detection
items.abstract_en: Class-incremental learning (CIL) for outdoor 3D object detection remains largely underexplored. Existing outdoor studies are limited to single-benchmark evaluations, with SDCoT++ considering KITTI and CL2OD considering nuScenes under different incremental settings. This makes it difficult to assess whether observed continual-learning behavior generalizes across autonomous-driving benchmarks. To the best of our knowledge, we provide the first unified cross-benchmark analysis of outdoor class-incremental 3D object detection across multiple autonomous-driving benchmarks, covering both two-task and multi-stage settings. We investigate: (1) how severely existing 3D detectors forget previously learned classes, (2) how incremental training exposes the stability-plasticity dilemma between knowledge retention and new-class acquisition, and (3) which forms of supervision are most effective for balancing these objectives. We introduce CL3DOD, a class-incremental 3D detection framework that restores missing supervision for previous classes using predictions from the previous-stage detector, preserves old-class responses through query-wise knowledge distillation, and employs EMA-based temporal consistency regularization. Experiments on KITTI and nuScenes reveal a consistent stability-plasticity dilemma across both benchmarks. CL3DOD generally achieves a more favorable stability-plasticity balance than controlled incremental baselines and improves upon published prior methods in the reported benchmark comparisons. This advantage persists across multiple incremental stages, demonstrating strong retention of previously learned knowledge while maintaining effective new-class acquisition. Our code, evaluation setup, and incremental task splits will be publicly released.

items.title_en: AnchorComplete: Recovering Complete Scene Meshes from Partial Point Clouds
items.abstract_en: Most image-based 3D reconstructors primarily recover visible surfaces, producing partial point clouds with large holes and leaving unobserved geometry unresolved. To address this limitation, we introduce AnchorComplete, a framework that reconstructs complete scene meshes from partial point clouds while preserving observed geometry and supporting scenes of varying scales. Building on TRELLIS.2, our method combines partial-point conditioning, which integrates global scene tokens with local spatial evidence to anchor generation to the input, and metric-scale coarse-to-fine generation, which progressively refines scene geometry within fixed-size windows while maintaining global structural consistency. Experiments on Replica and SCRREAM demonstrate that AnchorComplete consistently outperforms strong baselines in complete-scene reconstruction, particularly under sparse-view settings.

items.title_en: MoSoLoco: Monocular 3D Human Localization through Visual Latent Features and Social Context
items.abstract_en: Estimating the metric 3D position of people from a monocular camera is important for robot navigation and motion prediction. Lightweight pose-based localizers are attractive for robotic hardware with limited computational resources because they operate on compact 2D keypoints. However, they typically discard the richer visual representations computed by the pose estimator. We introduce MoSoLoco, a per-frame monocular 3D human localizer that combines the pose detector's internal visual features with the detected 2D skeleton, without requiring an additional RGB or depth encoder. MoSoLoco can further incorporate sparse same-frame multi-person context to refine individual position estimates. Experiments on JRDB and NuScenes show that reusing pose-detector representations improves localization, reducing the best JRDB error by approximately 23 percent relative to the strongest evaluated keypoint-based baseline. A sparse social-interaction module incorporates nearby detections from the same image for further refinement. Controlled trajectory-forecasting experiments show downstream benefits, while the complete pipeline remains suitable for efficient Jetson AGX Xavier inference.

items.title_en: Visual-to-Executable Procedural Reconstruction of Buildings
items.abstract_en: Procedural modeling offers compact, editable, and reusable representations for architectural content, but building such models still depends heavily on manually authored grammars. We study image-based procedural building reconstruction from in-the-wild images, with the goal of recovering an executable procedural description that can be instantiated as an editable 3D building asset. Because a single image provides only partial and view-dependent evidence, we focus on recovering the dominant visible facade(s) and attach the recovered facade program to a simple mass model for building-level instantiation. Our method decomposes this task into two structured prediction stages. First, a Global Structure Layout Tree recovers facade-scale split-and-repeat organization through a fine-tuned layout model with render-guided visual-symbolic reflection. Second, a Component Parameterization schema maps representative facade tiles to structured procedural attributes for local architectural component synthesis. These two representations are then deterministically compiled into executable Computer Generated Architecture (CGA) programs, avoiding the brittleness of direct low-level program generation. Experiments show that the proposed framework handles both regular facades and challenging in-the-wild images, while maintaining high structural consistency, procedural executability, and fine-grained architectural detail. The recovered programs further enable controllable and reusable 3D building asset generation.

items.title_en: When Optimization Meets Human Intent: Human-Centered Diffusion Model Optimization
items.abstract_en: Diffusion models are evolving from general tools into personalized systems that adapt to user needs through fine-tuning and guidance. However, diffusion optimization mainly targets measurable objectives such as aesthetics, rarely examining whether they align with human intent. Human needs are multidimensional, contextual, and dynamic, whereas existing methods approximate them with fixed metrics. Because these metrics capture human needs only partially and may amplify deviations from true intent during optimization, higher scores need not yield results better matching human expectations. To understand how human needs enter and influence optimization, we systematically analyze how human intent is expressed, translated into optimizable objectives, applied to model behavior or generation, and evaluated through outputs. We further discuss trade-offs affecting human-intent alignment in personalized image generation and gaps between automated metrics and real user judgments. This human-centered synthesis reorganizes diffusion optimization and provides a systematic reference for personalized generation systems designed for human preferences.

items.title_en: Znaki: A Russian Fingerspelling Recognition Dataset
items.abstract_en: Fingerspelling - the sequential signing of letters that compose proper names, technical terms, and out-of-vocabulary words - is an integral component of any sign language. Despite Russian Sign Language (RSL) being used by more than 150,000 native signers, no public fingerspelling dataset for RSL exists, in contrast to American, British, German, and several other sign languages. We introduce Znaki the first open RSL fingerspelling dataset: 37,252 video recordings (35.4 hours) of 1,593 unique sequences - proper names sampled from 16 domain categories - recorded by 68 native RSL signers (37 Deaf, 29 hard-of-hearing, and 2 certified interpreters) through a crowdsourcing pipeline with a two-stage signer qualification procedure and expert validation. The dataset covers all 33 Cyrillic handshapes, and its letter-frequency distribution matches the Russian National Corpus. As reference points for future research, we establish two baselines adapted from American Sign Language fingerspelling recognition: a Squeezeformer-based encoder-decoder, reaching a character-level accuracy ($1-\mathrm{CER}$) of 0.932 and a sequence accuracy of 0.596, and Fingerspelling-PoseNet, reaching 0.886 and 0.545, respectively.

items.title_en: Behavioral Affinity Transduction for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Classification
items.abstract_en: An image that is hard to classify on its own may have a helpful neighbor in the same unlabeled batch. Zero-shot vision-language models (VLMs) score images independently and leave this evidence unused. We study small unlabeled query batches with no labeled examples. Visual similarity can reflect pose or background, so it may connect images from different classes. Each image's scores over the class vocabulary offer another way to choose neighbors. We introduce Behavioral Affinity Transduction (BAT), which builds a sparse graph from these class-response profiles. The graph supplies neighbor evidence during prediction. For EM-Dirichlet, it also screens candidate classes and initializes assignments. BAT plugs into direct and iterative readouts of a frozen VLM. Across diverse datasets, BAT improves the mean accuracy of every tested readout. In the main RN50 comparison, soft and hard EM-Dirichlet gain $4.22$ and $2.72$ percentage points.

items.title_en: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
items.title_zh: SurgPace：面向手术多模态大语言模型的复杂度感知渐进式蒸馏
items.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

items.title_en: KAUSTics-Net: Diffusion-Based Through-Water UAV Restoration with a Semi-Synthetic Dataset
items.abstract_en: Accurate mapping of shallow-water environments using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is challenged by water-induced distortions, including refraction, caustics, and wavelength-dependent attenuation. The scarcity of paired distorted and reference imagery further limits the development of supervised restoration methods. To address this challenge, we introduce KAUSTics, a semi-synthetic dataset combining 1,280 reference patches derived from 32 high-resolution UAV images with 12,800 degraded observations generated through Blender-based water-surface rendering and empirical color and blur augmentations. We further propose KAUSTics-Net, a pixel-space conditional diffusion framework integrating a multi-scale conditional encoder, feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), cross-attention, and a composite reconstruction objective to restore shallow-water imagery. We evaluated the framework against eight image-restoration methods, complemented by architectural ablations and cross-dataset experiments. On KAUSTics, KAUSTics-Net achieved a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 31.715 +/- 0.439 dB, structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.849 +/- 0.002, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) of 0.145 +/- 0.007 across three training seeds. On the independent Sea-Undistort dataset, sampler-aware fine-tuning improved restoration fidelity, reaching 19.469 +/- 0.332 dB PSNR and 0.554 +/- 0.005 SSIM under combined water-surface distortions, although perceptual trade-offs remained. Additional experiments on real UAV imagery examined feature preservation and segmentation behavior. These findings demonstrate the potential of semi-synthetic training and conditional diffusion for shallow-water image restoration while highlighting the importance of evaluating both reconstruction fidelity and downstream remote-sensing utility.

items.title_en: 3D Gaussian Splatting within Self-Learned Neural View-Dependent Color Fields
items.abstract_en: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become a vital tool in novel view synthesis. 3D Gaussian functions with attributes like color, opacity, and scale are stacked together to explicitly model a radiance field. However, discrete 3D Gaussians usually produce poor depth with few geometry details but lots of floaters, which hinders the effective modeling of smooth radiance fields. To address this issue, we propose to learn a radiance field within a continuous view-dependent color field parameterized by neural networks. With continuous constraints in color, the bias on low-frequency signals of neural networks can highly encourage the geometry modeling to contribute to high-frequency color variations on images, getting rid of solely relying on the color attribute itself. Moreover, we impose a constraint to improve the Lipschitz continuity of the neural color field, making large changes of each Gaussian's color also match with large changes of its position in terms of a ratio. To this end, we additionally introduce novel self-learning strategies to improve the learning of the neural view-dependent color field without any external knowledge or priors, aiming for better generalization on unseen scenes. Our numerical and visual comparisons on widely used benchmarks justify our idea and show better ability of high fidelity geometry recovery in 3DGS. Project page: https://github.com/yangyixi21/Neural-Color-Fields-3DGS.

items.title_en: Multimodal Prompt Learning with Dual-Granularity Contrastive Alignment for Preoperative Prediction of Lung Adenocarcinoma Invasiveness Using 3D CT
items.title_zh: 基于双粒度对比对齐的多模态提示学习用于3D CT肺腺癌侵袭性术前预测
items.abstract_en: Accurate preoperative prediction of lung adenocarcinoma invasiveness is important for surgical planning and individualized treatment. However, overlapping CT appearances make it challenging to distinguish invasive adenocarcinoma (IAD) from Pre-IAD lesions. We propose a multimodal prompt-learning framework with dual-granularity image-text alignment for 3D CT-based IAD classification. A 3D ResNet-CBAM encoder extracts global and spatial visual features. A frozen RadBERT backbone is adapted with separate learnable prompts for report-level and keyword-level text encoding. These prompts are initialized using semantic representations derived from real-world clinical reports. Global contrastive alignment connects whole-volume CT representations with reports generated from clinician-annotated radiological attributes to provide overall semantic supervision. A multiple instance learning-based local alignment module associates spatial CT features with vascular-focused radiological keywords, to capture local imaging characteristics potentially associated with tumor invasion. The framework jointly optimizes classification and alignment objectives, while inference requires only CT images. Experiments included 1,593 pathologically confirmed nodules. On the test set, the proposed method achieved an accuracy of 87.92%, F1-score of 87.78%, and AUC of 0.9499. Its AUC significantly exceeded that of the image-only Res-CBAM baseline with the same visual backbone (0.9297; DeLong test, p = 0.0078). Ablation analyses supported the complementary contributions of global and local alignment and the benefit of report-based prompt initialization. Qualitative visualizations showed activation within nodules and adjacent vascular structures. These findings suggest that dual-granularity radiological supervision can enhance CT-based invasiveness prediction while preserving a CT-only inference workflow.

items.title_en: Ray-SCR: Generalizing Scene Coordinate Regression Across Camera Models
items.abstract_en: Among visual localization strategies, scene coordinate regression (SCR) has emerged as an attractive approach for its compactness, accuracy, and speed. Despite these advantages, SCR models generalize poorly across substantially different camera models, such as omnidirectional or strongly rectified imagery. This limitation arises because, changes in field of view, lens distortion, or rectification-induced resampling can make the same scene content appear differently depending on its pixel position, degrading localization accuracy. To cope with this limitation, we introduce Ray-SCR, a lightweight extension to existing SCR architectures that conditions local visual features on their calibrated viewing rays and refines neighboring ray-conditioned features with a shallow local Transformer. We further formulate supervision directly in ray space and use sparse SfM points as metric anchors that link observations across views and camera models. Taken together, these components enable a single scene representation built from a panoramic mapping sequence to accurately localize query images captured with very different cameras, including pinhole, fisheye, and omnidirectional cameras. We evaluate Ray-SCR across multiple SCR architectures and on datasets with pinhole, fisheye, and omnidirectional cameras. The proposed ray conditioning substantially improves generalization across cameras and leads to state-of-the-art localization performance in these challenging cross-camera settings. The project page is available at https://jaeminch0.github.io/ray-scr-generalizing-scene-coordinate-regression-across-camera-models/.

items.title_en: MIRA: Reinforcing Multimodal Reasoning via Deceptive Contextual Augmentation
items.abstract_en: While Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has significantly advanced multimodal reasoning, existing frameworks suffer from a critical "perception-reasoning gap." Due to an over-reliance on seemingly relevant visual tokens, even minor perceptual perturbations can propagate through the reasoning process, leading to compounding hallucinations. To address this issue, we propose MIRA, a training framework that improves robustness to erroneous visual contexts while enhancing logical reasoning ability. By injecting filtered, deceptive visual contexts during training, we construct challenging "hard traps" that stress-test the model's robustness to misleading information. Furthermore, we introduce a group-wise reflection-triggering mechanism that enables the model to autonomously detect and rectify inconsistencies between visual cues and logical constraints, which is ultimately internalized as an intrinsic policy behavior. Importantly, MIRA does not rely on human annotations. Experimental results across multiple reasoning and perception benchmarks show that MIRA yields an average 7% improvement on in-domain benchmarks, with consistent improvements on vision-centric benchmarks. These findings highlight that active error recovery is essential for robust multimodal reasoning. Comprehensive ablation studies and analyses further provide insights into why MIRA is effective.

items.title_en: VL-Dedup: Graded Multimodal Entity Resolution for Image-Text Data Deduplication
items.abstract_en: Image-text corpora contain copies of one image, captions that describe one image in different ways, captions reused for different images, and captions that do not match their images. Each case calls for a different curation action. Deduplication and multimodal entity resolution (ER) only decide whether records are the same, and they are evaluated on labeled pairs. Yet pair scores do not tell which records end up in the same cluster or which useful captions get deleted. We therefore formulate image-text deduplication as graded multimodal ER, which decides visual identity, caption handling, and mismatches for each pair, and we evaluate it at three levels: pairs, clusters, and the retained set. Our method, VL-Dedup, groups records of the same visual entity into clusters and caps the size of each cluster. Within each cluster, a vision-language model (VLM) and CLIPScore decide which captions to keep and which to flag. We also build VL-DedupBench, with 50,000 COCO and SOP records and 66,788 labeled pairs. On it, a classifier that selects no false edge among the labeled pairs still joins millions of record pairs from different entities. Spending VLM calls on the pairs inside clusters, rather than on pairs with uncertain scores, gives better caption decisions from the same model. Even when almost all clusters are correct, keeping one record per cluster loses facts in many deletions, while the deletions of VL-Dedup lose much less information.

items.title_en: Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Image Classification
items.abstract_en: Multi-source remote sensing image classification benefits from complementary spectral and structural information. However, identifying discriminative cross-modal features remains challenging. This letter proposes a Cross-Layer Refinement and Frequency-aware Fusion Network (CRFNet) within a lightweight dual-branch architecture. Specifically, a Cross-Layer Refinement Attention (CLRA) module propagates selected attention relationships across successive layers and employs top relation selection to progressively strengthen discriminative spatial dependencies while suppressing irrelevant responses. Furthermore, a Frequency-aware Complementary Fusion (FCF) module combines frequency-wise interactions with cross-modal channel attention in the Fourier domain. The resulting representations are then converted into spatial-domain gates to selectively modulate complementary features. Experiments on the Houston 2013 and Augsburg datasets demonstrate that the proposed CRFNet consistently outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. The codes are publicly available at https://github.com/oucailab/CRFNet

items.title_en: Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network for Multi-Source Remote Sensing Data Classification
items.title_zh: 用于多源遥感数据分类的共享模式协同网络
items.abstract_en: Multi-source remote sensing data classification has received growing attention recently. However, existing methods still struggle to jointly model long-range contextual dependencies and shared spatial patterns across heterogeneous modalities. To address this issue, we propose a Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network (SPCNet) for HSI and SAR/LiDAR joint classification. To enhance cross-modal collaborative learning, Shared-Pattern Collaborative Block (SPCB) is designed by introducing a shared large-kernel operator and a dynamic convolution branch, enabling the network to capture common spatial structures and content-adaptive local features. Furthermore, Region-Adaptive Modality Allocator (RAMA) is developed to assign spatially varying modality weights for reliable feature fusion. Experiments on Houston2013, Augsburg, and Houston2018 datasets demonstrate that SPCNet achieves superior classification performance over several state-of-the-art methods. The code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/oucailab/SPCNet

items.title_en: PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making
items.abstract_en: Real-world driving requires context-aware decision-making. Existing end-to-end driving benchmarks primarily assess trajectory quality through safety, compliance, comfort, and driving progress, leaving context-dependent decision-making insufficiently characterized. To fill this gap, we present PlanContext, a benchmark for evaluating in-context driving decision-making. PlanContext constructs paired evaluations by varying high-level driving intentions while keeping the observed scene fixed, enabling a natural and controllable assessment of context-dependent decision-making. We further define six representative driving contexts and jointly evaluate contextual decision correctness, road compliance, and dynamic safety with class-balanced metrics. Experiments on 9,561 scene-condition instances from NAVSIM and 23 public end-to-end driving models show that high conventional driving-quality scores do not consistently correspond to strong route-level in-context driving decision-making. Further analysis shows that model behavior varies with decision timing, road structure, and traffic interaction depending on the decision required by the current context. Our results highlight in-context driving decision-making as an important complementary dimension for evaluating end-to-end driving systems.

items.title_en: MuCHMDPoser: Multiview RGB-Camera Full-Body Pose Tracking for Virtual Reality
items.abstract_en: Accurate full-body tracking in Virtual Reality (VR) is heavily underconstrained when relying solely on consumer-grade sparse sensors, such as Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs) and handheld controllers. Indeed, the self-avatar full-body pose must be inferred based on the 3 available upper-body joints tracked by these devices. This leads to significant tracking error, especially in lower-body pose. To overcome this issue, we propose to extend the tracking setup with external multiview RGB cameras. We show that integrating RGB-based pose estimation this framework is able to significantly decrease lower-body tracking errors, even under common artifacts in RGB-based estimates. Additionally, we evaluate a only-once HMD-camera calibration procedure that does not require any physical markers. We finally propose an implementation of the overall framework, achieving an end-to-end animation at 60 FPS on a Nvidia RTX3080 GPU. Codes are available at https://github.com/antmaio/MuCHMDPoser.

items.title_en: VideoEditor-MoE: Scaling Complex Video Editing with Mixture of Experts
items.abstract_en: Complex video editing requires understanding complex instructions while jointly fulfilling multiple editing requests. Meeting these demands through dense model scaling substantially increases computational cost. We introduce VideoEditor-MoE, the first open-source mixture-of-experts framework for video editing. Beyond sparse MLP-MoE layers, MoE-Attention expands attention capacity through routed key--value experts while preserving global interactions among video tokens. Initialized from a 5B video editing model, VideoEditor-MoE scales to 14B and 56B parameters, with approximately 8B parameters activated per token in both variants. Comparisons with existing methods and two complementary baselines, Explicit-MoE and MLP-MoE, assess its benefits over explicit expert guidance and MLP-only expert architectures. Further analyses demonstrate that all experts remain active and reveal that learned routing responds more strongly to sample content and diffusion noise levels than to human-defined editing categories. Spatial analysis further indicates sensitivity to object-level semantic features. We also identify decoupled weight decay as a strategy for stabilizing expert scaling.

items.title_en: Bayesian Sequential Optimal Experimental Design for Single-Pixel Imaging using Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract_en: Adaptive compressed sensing (CS) aims to select the most informative measurements sequentially, which is crucial for many modern imaging systems. This task can be formulated as a Bayesian sequential optimal experimental design (sOED) problem, where each new acquisition is chosen to maximally reduce uncertainty about the unknown image given prior information and subsequent data provided by acquisitions. However, in single-pixel imaging (SPI), the large design space consists of all possible binary illumination patterns. Directly optimizing the Bayesian sOED objective over this space using conventional methods is generally challenging. In this work, we reformulate sOED for SPI as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem. In RL, an agent learns a policy through repeated experimental trials to maximize a reward, here given as the expected information gain, the most complete measure of uncertainty reduction in Bayesian OED. This avoids the need to directly optimize complex information-theoretic objectives during a measurement to obtain the next design. Instead, the result is a learned policy function that directly maps the current posterior belief about the image to the next optimal binary measurement pattern, in a computationally efficient way. Using a simple yet representative SPI imaging scenario, this work evaluates the scalability of the learned policy under two different policy parameterizations. Furthermore, we investigate how performance deteriorates when only approximate posterior information is available or the measurements are impaired by noise, and propose several strategies to introduce additional design constraints motivated by biomedical applications. The numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed Bayesian sOED-RL framework remains robust and can be extended to more complex, large-scale SPI scenarios.

items.title_en: GPU-Native Real-Time Textured Mesh Reconstruction with Seam-Aware Multi-View Radiometric Correction
items.abstract_en: We present a GPU-native volumetric-video system for real-time reconstruction of graphics-compatible textured triangle meshes from multiple RGB-D sensors. Existing TSDF systems accelerate fusion and mesh extraction, but extending them to per-frame textured meshing adds CPU mesh processing, CPU-side texturing work, or extra CPU-GPU transfers between stages. After input staging, our method keeps the reconstruction and texturing stages (TSDF fusion, Marching Cubes, connected-component noise removal, view-based texture mapping, inpainting, and radiometric seam correction) resident on the GPU; no intermediate mesh or image data returns to the host between these stages. A fixed-size-array representation of mesh topology gives constant-time neighbor access on the GPU and makes the downstream mesh-level operations data-parallel. Because we texture each face from a single camera, exposure seams that vary smoothly across each image remain; we estimate a per-camera low-frequency gain field and bake it into the atlas on the GPU. On the CMU Panoptic dataset, our method is faster than the baselines at every tested voxel resolution and number of sensors, achieves peak speedups of more than an order of magnitude over CUDA-accelerated nvblox and CPU-based Open3D, and approaches an offline textured-meshing baseline in perceptual re-rendering quality.

items.title_en: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
items.title_zh: 面向实时 EEG 相位估计的贝叶斯优化双二阶滤波器-Burg 模型
items.abstract_en: Real-time phase estimation on stimulus-aligned transient EEG is critical for closed-loop neuromodulation systems targeting the theta-band, yet most real-time phase estimation methods have been developed and validated on resting-state, high-fidelity signals in the alpha band. Recent work has pursued deep learning architectures, while individualized classical bandpass filter tuning remains underexplored. This study characterizes the spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering and demonstrates the performance gains achieved through individualized tuning. We present a Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model evaluated on EEG recorded during peripheral vibrotactile stimulation of the left median nerve (theta, N=20 healthy subjects) and on resting-state recordings from the Max Planck Institute's LEMON dataset (alpha, N=20 healthy subjects). BOB was benchmarked against the Deep Dual-Branch Complex Neural Network (DBCNN), EEG Phase Prediction Network (EPN), Phastimate, and Phase Estimation with Autoregressive Padding (PEAP) under matched testing conditions: channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation time points, and an offline reference phase obtained through zero-phase filtering and the Hilbert transform. Under these testing conditions, BOB achieved matched or better performance than these models at a fraction of the calibration time.
items.abstract_zh: 对刺激锁定的瞬态脑电（EEG）实时估计相位，是靶向 theta 频段闭环神经调控的关键，但现有方法多在静息态、高保真的 alpha 频段上开发验证。近期研究转向深度学习，个体化的经典带通滤波调参却未被充分探索。本研究刻画非预测性（因果）带通滤波的频谱与时间特性，提出贝叶斯优化双二阶滤波器-Burg（BOB）模型，并在左正中神经振动触觉刺激下的 EEG（theta，20 名健康被试）与马克斯·普朗克研究所 LEMON 数据集的静息态记录（alpha，20 名被试）上评估。在通道选择、个体化优化、评估时间点及零相位滤波+Hilbert 变换离线参考相位等匹配条件下，BOB 与 DBCNN、EPN、Phastimate、PEAP 对比，以极少的校准时间取得相当或更优的性能。
items.highlight_zh: 个体化贝叶斯调参的经典滤波，以极少校准时间媲美深度相位估计。
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：闭环神经调控（例如按脑电相位在 theta 频段施加刺激）需要从刺激锁定的瞬态脑电中实时估计相位。但现有实时相位估计方法几乎都在“静息态、信噪比高”的 alpha 频段数据上开发和验证，未必适用于真实刺激场景。近年大家纷纷转向深度学习，反而冷落了给每个被试单独调好经典带通滤波器这条朴素路线。

方法：作者先分析“非预测性”（因果）带通滤波在频谱与时间上的固有特性，说明为什么个体化调参能带来收益。随后提出 BOB 模型：用贝叶斯优化为每位被试自动搜索双二阶（biquad）滤波器参数，再结合 Burg 方法做相位预测。

实验设置：两组数据——左正中神经外周振动触觉刺激下的脑电（theta 频段，20 名健康被试），以及马克斯·普朗克研究所 LEMON 数据集的静息态记录（alpha 频段，20 名被试）。对比对象是 DBCNN、EPN、Phastimate、PEAP 等深度或经典方法。为保证公平，所有方法在通道选择、个体化优化、评估时间点，以及由零相位滤波+Hilbert 变换得到的离线参考相位上完全一致。

结果：在这些匹配条件下，BOB 达到与深度模型相当甚至更好的相位估计精度，而所需校准时间只是后者的一小部分。

为何重要：它提醒领域不要一味追新，个体化调参的经典滤波是被低估的强基线；对讲求低延迟、需快速上线的实时闭环神经调控系统而言，“少校准、够准确”尤为实用。

items.title_en: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
items.title_zh: iGC：基于学习型体细胞超突变先验的强化学习抗体优化
items.abstract_en: Antibody affinity maturation is a natural optimization process in which B cells acquire mutations through somatic hypermutation (SHM), undergo selection for improved antigen binding, and iteratively evolve toward higher affinity. Computationally modeling this process requires capturing both biologically plausible mutations and antigen-specific selection. However, existing mutation models do not directly optimize binding, while affinity optimization often neglects realistic mutation trajectories. We introduce iGC (in silico Germinal Centers), a two-stage reinforcement learning (RL) framework for antigen-specific antibody optimization. Stage 1 learns an SHM mutation prior from parent-child pairs in B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to a target affinity-maturation dataset. Stage 2 initializes an RL policy from this prior and optimizes antigen binding with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization toward the frozen prior. To prevent reward exploitation, including repetitive high-reward substitutions and structurally tolerated framework mutations, we introduce a Reward-Tax Meta-Gradient objective. RewardNet smooths the affinity landscape, while TaxNet penalizes reward overexploitation, jointly defining a learned meta-reward for policy optimization. We evaluate iGC on mutation prediction, SHM consistency, affinity optimization, and mutation diversity. The mutation prior more than doubles the strongest baseline in mutation-site prediction. Following RL optimization, iGC maintains SHM sequence structure. It also achieves a strong exploration-exploitation balance, yielding competitive reward-diversity products across candidate-selection cutoffs. These results demonstrate that iGC integrates biologically plausible mutation generation with antigen-specific affinity selection, providing an in silico framework for iterative antibody affinity maturation.
items.abstract_zh: 抗体亲和力成熟是B细胞通过体细胞超突变（SHM）获得突变、经选择提升抗原结合力并迭代进化的天然优化过程。计算建模需同时兼顾生物学上合理的突变与抗原特异性选择，但现有突变模型不直接优化结合力，亲和力优化又常忽视真实的突变轨迹。我们提出iGC（in silico Germinal Centers），一个两阶段强化学习框架：第一阶段从B细胞谱系树的亲子对中学习SHM突变先验，并适配到目标亲和力成熟数据集；第二阶段以该先验初始化强化学习策略，并以向冻结先验的KL正则化来优化抗原结合。为防止奖励被滥用（如重复高奖励替换、结构上可容忍的框架突变），我们引入奖励—税收元梯度目标：RewardNet平滑亲和力景观，TaxNet惩罚奖励过度开发，共同定义用于策略优化的学习型元奖励。我们在突变预测、SHM一致性、亲和力优化与突变多样性上评估iGC：突变先验在突变位点预测上超过最强基线一倍以上；强化学习优化后iGC保持SHM序列结构，并实现良好的探索—利用平衡，在各候选筛选阈值下获得有竞争力的奖励—多样性乘积。结果表明iGC将生物学上合理的突变生成与抗原特异性亲和力选择相结合。
items.highlight_zh: 先学SHM突变先验再做强化学习，兼得真实突变轨迹与亲和力优化
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：设计抗体药物时，需要让抗体与抗原结合得更牢，也就是提升亲和力。自然界中，免疫系统靠“体细胞超突变+筛选”的进化过程完成这件事。既有的计算方法分两类：一类模仿突变规律但不直接优化结合力，另一类直接优化结合力却生成不真实的突变序列。如何二者兼顾是本文要解决的问题。

方法：作者提出iGC，把该过程拆成两步。第一步，从真实的B细胞谱系数据中学习“突变先验”，即哪些位置的氨基酸更可能发生突变，并在目标抗体数据集上做适配。第二步，用这个先验初始化强化学习策略，让策略在优化抗原结合打分的同时，通过KL正则化约束它不要偏离先验太远，从而保持突变的生物学真实性。此外，作者发现强化学习容易“钻空子”：反复堆叠同一高奖励替换，或在框架区做结构上无碍但无益的突变。为此设计了Reward–Tax元梯度目标：RewardNet把亲和力景观平滑化，TaxNet对奖励过度开发征税，二者构成元奖励指导策略更新。

结果：在突变位点预测任务上，学到的突变先验把最强基线提升了一倍以上；经过强化学习优化后，序列仍保持SHM特征结构；在不同候选筛选严格程度下，奖励与多样性的乘积具有竞争力，说明探索与利用取得了较好平衡。

为何重要：该工作把“像真实免疫系统那样突变”和“真正提升结合力”统一到一个框架中，为计算抗体设计提供了既有生物学可信度、又有优化效率的新思路，有望减少湿实验筛选负担。

items.title_en: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
items.title_zh: 面向连续冷冻电镜异质性的经验贝叶斯流匹配
items.abstract_en: We address the problem of learning generative priors over high-dimensional latent variables from indirect, noisy observations, with a focus on continuous heterogeneity in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). In this setting, 3D atomic structures $x \in \mathbb{R}^{3N_a}$ are never directly observed and must be inferred from 2D projection images $y$ generated by a complex, non-linear forward operator. We propose Empirical Bayes Flow Matching (EB-FM), a method that learns a flow matching prior $p_θ(x)$ directly from observations using a Monte Carlo stochastic approximation Expectation-Maximization framework. EB-FM alternates between an E-step that performs approximate posterior sampling from $p_θ(x \mid y)$ via guided flow-based generation while maintaining persistent latent estimates through stochastic approximation, and an M-step that updates the flow model using these stabilized latent variables as training targets. This approach eliminates the need for pretraining on clean data and naturally accommodates non-linear forward models. We validate our method on controlled inverse problems using two-moons and MNIST data, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated cryo-EM data with known poses, showing that EB-FM can recover continuous distributions of protein conformations directly in atomic-coordinate space.
items.abstract_zh: 我们研究从间接、带噪观测中学习高维隐变量生成先验的问题，重点关注冷冻电镜（cryo-EM）中的连续异质性。在此场景下，三维原子结构 x∈R^{3N_a} 从不被直接观测，必须由复杂非线性前向算子生成的二维投影图像 y 推断。我们提出经验贝叶斯流匹配（EB-FM），在蒙特卡洛随机近似期望最大化框架下，直接从观测中学习流匹配先验 p_θ(x)。EB-FM 交替执行：E 步通过引导式流生成从 p_θ(x|y) 做近似后验采样，并借助随机近似维持持续的隐变量估计；M 步以这些稳定化的隐变量作为训练目标更新流模型。该方法无需在干净数据上预训练，且天然适配非线性前向模型。我们在 two-moons 与 MNIST 的受控逆问题上验证方法，并在位姿已知的模拟冷冻电镜数据上展示其有效性，表明 EB-FM 能直接在原子坐标空间中恢复蛋白质构象的连续分布。
items.highlight_zh: 无需干净数据预训练，直接从投影图学出蛋白质构象连续分布
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：冷冻电镜能拍出成千上万张蛋白质颗粒的二维投影图，但蛋白质本身是柔性的，会在不同构象之间连续摆动（即“连续异质性”）。科研人员真正想要的是三维原子结构的分布，而不是单一张静态结构。难点在于：三维结构从未被直接看到，只能由二维投影间接反推，而且投影过程是非线性的、带噪声的。

方法：作者提出 EB-FM（经验贝叶斯流匹配）。核心想法是把“学先验”这件事放进期望最大化（EM）框架里：E 步用流模型生成候选三维结构，并结合观测图像做引导采样，得到近似后验；同时用随机近似保留一份持续更新的隐变量估计，避免每轮从头采样带来的抖动。M 步则把这些稳定下来的隐变量当作训练目标，用来更新流匹配模型。这样就不需要在“干净的三维结构”上预训练，也能自然地容纳非线性前向模型。

结果：作者先在两个受控逆问题（two-moons、MNIST）上验证框架正确性，再在位姿已知的模拟冷冻电镜数据上测试，结果显示该方法能在原子坐标空间直接恢复蛋白质构象的连续分布。

为何重要：传统冷冻电镜异质性分析往往依赖已知位姿、线性近似或干净训练数据，而 EB-FM 把生成先验学习与非线性观测模型统一起来，为从真实投影图直接刻画蛋白质动态构象集合提供了可行路径，对结构生物学与药物设计有潜在价值。

items.title_en: Exploring the World of Lipids with Machine-Learned Coarse-Grained Models
items.title_zh: 用机器学习粗粒化模型探索脂质世界
items.abstract_en: Lipid bilayers are central to cellular organization and function, yet their atomistic modelling remains constrained by its high computational cost. While coarse-grained (CG) models can overcome this bottleneck, they are limited in accuracy due to the use of simplified functional forms based on molecular mechanics. Using a hybrid functional form combining physics-based terms with a graph neural network, we present implicit-solvent, machine-learned CG models for POPC. When trained on single-lipid data, the model recovers the atomistic conformational landscape. By adding short atomistic simulations of a small flat bilayer to the training data and combining force matching with a denoising objective, we train a model that accurately reproduces bilayer structure and dynamics, in closer agreement with the atomistic reference than existing models, like Martini3 and DryMartini. Beyond its training data, the model stabilizes curved geometries, including vesicles, and captures complex cooperative phenomena such as bilayer and vesicle self-assembly and pore sealing. While limitations remain, particularly regarding chemical transferability, our results establish machine-learned coarse-grained potentials as a promising path towards robust and accurate CG models of lipids and membranes.

items.title_en: Ablating Design Choices for Protein Ensemble Generators Across Structural Regimes
items.title_zh: 跨结构状态下蛋白质系综生成器设计选择的消融研究
items.abstract_en: Generative models of protein conformational ensembles inherit much of their design from structure prediction for folded proteins. Ordered and disordered proteins, however, occupy distinct structural regimes, and we investigate how design choices hold up across them. Using a minimal C$α$ flow-matching model, we ablate choices of architecture, sequence conditioning, rigid-body alignment and training source, and evaluate each variant against experimental SAXS and NMR chemical-shift data partitioned into ordered, disordered, multi-domain and transitional proteins. Mixture-of-experts routing, a static pair representation and a disorder probe have no detectable effect, a smaller protein language model performs worse on ordered proteins but not on disordered ones, and alignment in the loss degrades agreement with SAXS. Replacing coarse-grained simulations of disordered proteins with fragment-assembled ensembles improves agreement with chemical shifts at a cost to SAXS, while an equal mixture of the two keeps most of the gain at a smaller cost. This points to the training data, rather than the architecture, as the main constraint.

items.title_en: A phase decoder for reconstructing missing muscle activity
items.title_zh: 一种用于重建缺失肌肉活动的相位解码器
items.abstract_en: Upper-limb assistive devices are commonly controlled with electromyographic (EMG) signals, but nerve injury, muscle loss, or practical limits on electrode placement can leave only a few usable signals, which constrains the decoding of intended movements. Here, we introduce a decoder that reconstructs missing muscle activations from sparse EMGs using a two-stage real-time approach: (1) estimating ongoing movement phase from available signals, and (2) retrieving corresponding muscle activations from a library of pre-recorded muscle activity templates. In proof-of-concept tests, neurologically intact participants (N=4) performed object-transfer tasks under simulated denervation conditions. The decoder accurately estimated movement phase (median root-mean-square error [RMSE] <0.17 of movement duration) and reconstructed missing muscle activations (RMSE 0.08-0.34; correlation up to 0.97) within ~2 ms, in a previously unseen participant. The results indicate that template based reconstruction could leverage sparse EMG for low latency control of assistive technology.
items.abstract_zh: 上肢辅助装置通常由肌电（EMG）信号控制，但神经损伤、肌肉缺失或电极放置的实际限制可能只留下少数可用信号，从而制约意图运动的解码。本文提出一种解码器，采用两阶段实时方法从稀疏EMG重建缺失的肌肉激活：（1）由可用信号估计当前运动相位；（2）从预先录制的肌肉活动模板库中检索相应的肌肉激活。在概念验证测试中，4名神经功能完好的参与者在模拟去神经支配条件下完成物体转移任务。解码器能准确估计运动相位（中位均方根误差<0.17个运动时长），并在约2 ms内重建缺失的肌肉激活（RMSE 0.08–0.34，相关性最高0.97），且可推广到此前未见过的参与者。结果表明，基于模板的重建可利用稀疏EMG实现辅助技术的低延迟控制。
items.highlight_zh: 用运动相位加模板库，从稀疏EMG在约2 ms内重建缺失肌肉激活
items.digest_zh: 1）研究什么问题：肌电控制的假肢和辅助装置在临床上常遇到可用信号太少的问题——神经损伤、肌肉切除或电极贴不下，只剩两三个通道，传统解码器难以还原使用者想做的动作。2）用了什么方法：作者没有直接“预测”缺失通道，而是把连续控制拆成两步。第一步，用现有少量EMG估计当前动作进行到周期的哪个“相位”；第二步，按这个相位去一张事先录好的肌肉活动模板库里查表，取回该时刻各肌肉应有的激活水平，从而补全缺失通道。3）得到什么结果：4名神经完好被试在人为屏蔽部分通道（模拟去神经）的条件下做物体转移任务。相位估计的中位均方根误差小于整个动作时长的0.17；重建的缺失肌肉激活与真实值误差在0.08–0.34之间，相关系数最高达0.97；整个计算约2 ms完成；并且对一位未参与模板录制的新被试同样有效。4）为何重要：这套思路把“预测”换成了“检索”，计算量极小、延迟极低，适合嵌入式实时控制；对残存信号极少的患者提供了一条务实路径。局限也很清楚：只是小样本概念验证，动作类型有限，模板库需要为每个人单独采集，病理状态下的相位估计仍待检验。

items.title_en: State-dependent emergence of coupling between oscillatory and aperiodic neural activity
items.title_zh: 振荡与非周期神经活动之间耦合的状态依赖性涌现
items.abstract_en: Neural oscillations and aperiodic activity are two quintessential mesoscopic-level features arising from shared circuits, yet what governs their relationship remains unclear. Here we show that coupling between oscillatory frequency and aperiodic exponent is sporadic and state-dependent. Bias-reduced analyses of 3,245 intracranial contacts from 61 awake subjects showed significant coupling in only <13% of contacts per band. A connectome-constrained dynamical model predicted that neither changes of input to local circuit nor removal of long-range connections modulated the coupling; whereas stronger local inhibitory feedback drove covariation between oscillatory frequency and aperiodic exponent. The model predictions were supported by three independent experiments: transcranial stimulation shifted each component independently and focal ablation of remote cortical tissues did not change coupling; whereas coupling emerged during seizures that altered local excitatory-inhibitory balance. These results suggest that the relation between periodic and aperiodic neural activity is neither intrinsically independent nor coupled, but determined by local circuit states.
items.abstract_zh: 神经振荡与非周期活动是共享环路产生的两种典型介观特征，但什么决定了它们之间的关系仍不清楚。本文表明，振荡频率与非周期指数之间的耦合是偶发且依赖状态的。对61名清醒被试的3245个颅内触点做偏差校正分析显示，每个频段仅不到13%的触点存在显著耦合。一个受连接组约束的动力学模型预测：改变对局部环路的输入或移除长程连接都不调节耦合，而更强的局部抑制性反馈会驱动振荡频率与非周期指数的共变。三项独立实验支持了模型预测：经颅刺激分别独立改变两个成分，远端皮层组织的局灶消融不改变耦合；而在改变局部兴奋-抑制平衡的癫痫发作期间，耦合出现了。这些结果提示，周期性与非周期神经活动的关系既非内禀独立、也非固有耦合，而是由局部环路状态决定。
items.highlight_zh: 振荡与非周期活动的耦合罕见，由局部抑制性环路状态决定
items.digest_zh: 1）研究什么问题：脑电或颅内记录里既有节律性振荡（如α波），也有不呈节律的1/f样“非周期”成分。两者都来自同一批神经环路，但学界长期不清楚它们是否耦合、由什么决定。这直接影响一个常见做法：用非周期指数去校正振荡功率是否合理。2）用了什么方法：作者分析了61名清醒被试共3245个颅内触点的信号，用偏差校正的谱参数化方法分别估计振荡频率和非周期指数，统计显著耦合的比例；再用受连接组约束的动力学模型提出机制假设；最后用三类实验验证。3）得到什么结果：耦合其实很罕见，每个频段只有不到13%的触点显著。模型显示，改变外部输入或切断长程连接都不影响耦合，只有增强局部抑制性反馈才会让两个成分一起变化。实验验证一致：经颅刺激对两个成分各自独立起作用，远端皮层局灶消融不改变耦合，而癫痫发作（局部兴奋-抑制平衡被打破）时耦合才出现。4）为何重要：这说明周期与非周期的关系不是脑的固定属性，而是局部环路状态的一种读出，有望作为兴奋-抑制平衡的指标；也提醒研究者不要默认二者耦合。局限是数据主要来自需颅内监测的癫痫患者，存在选择偏倚。

items.title_en: Pubertal timing is a critical dimension of adolescent brain vulnerability
items.title_zh: 青春期时序是青少年大脑脆弱性的关键维度
items.abstract_en: Adolescence is a period of rapid brain development, during which biological maturational timing varies substantially between individuals. This variability may drive specific developmental vulnerabilities to adverse experiences with long-term consequences, warranting early identification of at-risk individuals. We utilized ultrasonic bone age measurements to track pubertal maturity, classifying participants by adolescent biological maturity relative to chronological age (accelerated, average, decelerated). Brain hierarchy was quantified as the irreversibility of brain signals in resting state electroencephalography, providing a brain-based method to detect vulnerability patterns. The COVID-19 pandemic presented a unique opportunity to also assess alterations in brain hierarchy following external disruption. We mapped maturity-defined trajectories and rates of hierarchical organization, and their post-pandemic deviation from expected development, capturing two distinct vulnerability forms. First, early maturing adolescents showed persistent reduction in brain hierarchy. Second, those undergoing their fastest phase of development - specifically, decelerated adolescents - showed the strongest disruption in brain hierarchy following the pandemic. These findings suggest that pubertal timing is a critical dimension of individual variation in adolescent brain development and vulnerability. They also emphasize the need for objective maturity measurements to tailor support to individual pubertal timelines, particularly given the secular trend toward earlier puberty and ongoing global ecological crises.
items.abstract_zh: 青春期是大脑快速发育的时期，个体间的生物学成熟时序差异很大。这种差异可能造成对不良经历的特异性发育脆弱性并带来长期后果，因此需要早期识别高风险个体。我们利用超声骨龄测量追踪青春期成熟度，按相对于实际年龄的生物学成熟度（加速、平均、减速）对被试分类。以静息态脑电信号的不可逆性量化“大脑层级”，提供一种基于大脑的脆弱性检测方法。COVID-19大流行则提供了考察外部干扰后大脑层级改变的机会。我们刻画了成熟度所定义的层级组织轨迹与速率，以及疫情后偏离预期发育的程度，捕捉到两种不同的脆弱性形式：早熟青少年的大脑层级持续降低；而处于发育最快阶段的青少年——特别是减速组——疫情后大脑层级受扰最严重。这些发现表明，青春期时序是青少年大脑发育与脆弱性个体差异的关键维度，也强调需要客观的成熟度测量，以便按个体青春期时间线提供支持，尤其考虑到青春期提前的长期趋势与持续的全球生态危机。
items.highlight_zh: 青春期成熟早晚决定大脑层级轨迹与疫情下的脆弱程度
items.digest_zh: 1）研究什么问题：青少年期大脑快速重塑，但每个孩子“生物学上成熟”的时间早晚差别很大。同样一次外部冲击（如疫情），对早熟和晚熟的孩子可能伤害不同。问题是缺乏客观的成熟度标尺，也缺乏能识别脆弱个体的脑指标。2）用了什么方法：作者用超声骨龄测量客观刻画青春期成熟度，把被试按“生物学成熟度相对实际年龄”分为加速、平均、减速三组。再用静息态脑电信号的不可逆性（时间序列在时间反演下有多不对称）量化“大脑层级”组织程度，追踪各组发育轨迹与速率。COVID-19大流行被当作一次天然扰动，用来观察疫情后大脑层级偏离预期轨迹的程度。3）得到什么结果：识别出两种脆弱形式。一是早熟（加速）青少年，其大脑层级持续偏低；二是正处在发育最快阶段的青少年，特别是减速组，在疫情后大脑层级受到的扰乱最严重。4）为何重要：它把“什么时候发育”提到了和“发育到什么程度”同等重要的位置，说明青春期时序是理解个体差异与脆弱性的一个关键维度。方法上，骨龄这类客观测量加上脑电标记，有望在群体层面提前筛出高风险个体，并按各自的时间线给予支持——在全球青春期普遍提前、生态危机频发的背景下尤有意义。局限是脑电层级只是间接指标，疫情属于不可控的自然实验，因果推断仍需谨慎。

items.title_en: Paraquat Inhalation Produces Male-Biased Dopaminergic Neuron Loss and Motor Deficits in Mice: Relevance to Parkinsons Disease
items.title_zh: 百草枯吸入导致小鼠雄性偏向性多巴胺能神经元丢失和运动缺陷：与帕金森病的相关性
items.abstract_en: Long-term exposure to paraquat (PQ), a widely used herbicide, has been linked to increased risk of Parkinsons Disease (PD) in agricultural workers and rural communities in the United States (US), findings further supported by experimental animal studies. Although banned in many countries across the globe, PQ remains widely used in the US. Inhalation of PQ has been known to induce systemic organ failure at acute concentrations. However, prolonged low-dose inhalation from agricultural spraying and pesticide drift has not been readily evaluated for its potential to contribute to neurodegenerative diseases in vivo. Instead, many experimental studies have relied on systemic routes of exposure, which do not effectively replicate the most common route of exposure to PQ in the environment. In the current study, Parkinsonian features were examined in mice that had been exposed via whole-body inhalation to PQ aerosol for either 40 or 60 days. Levels of PQ in brain were highest in olfactory bulb, followed by frontal cortex and then brainstem in both sexes. After 60 days of exposure, male-specific impairments in locomotor activity were observed, in addition to reductions in striatal dopamine, in substantia nigra tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression and number of TH+ dopaminergic neurons, the latter being considered the primary basis of PD, along with increased olfactory bulb -synuclein levels. As such, these studies confirm the dopaminergic neurotoxicity of inhaled PQ. These findings raise significant concerns as to the contribution of PQ exposures to the continued increase in the incidence of PD in the US.

items.title_en: Imipramine binds to amyloid-β and extends the survival of Alzheimer's disease patients
items.title_zh: 丙咪嗪与淀粉样蛋白β结合并延长阿尔茨海默病患者的生存期
items.abstract_en: Background Apolipoprotein E (apoE) plays numerous roles in the pathogenic pathway to Alzheimer's disease (AD). We previously performed a high-throughput screen and identified the antidepressant imipramine as an inhibitor of the interaction between apoE and amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}). We also found that imipramine use to treat depression in AD patients was associated with better Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) scores. Here we studied the mechanisms by which imipramine inhibits the AD pathogenic pathway and investigated its effect on mortality in AD patients. Methods Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy was used to characterize the interaction between imipramine and A{beta} monomers. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived AD cerebral organoids (COs) and transgenic AD rats treated with imipramine underwent neuropathological evaluation, while rat learning and memory were assessed in the Morris Water Maze. AD patient mortality in the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center's database was analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models. Results Imipramine inhibits the apoE-A{beta} interaction by binding directly to A{beta} monomers. Imipramine reduces A{beta} accumulation and neuronal cell loss in AD COs. Imipramine-treated female AD rats had enhanced reference memory and increased hippocampal cellularity and cholinergic neurotransmission. AD patients prescribed imipramine had reduced all-cause mortality over 10 years relative to those prescribed other tricyclic antidepressants (TCA), non-TCA antidepressants, or no antidepressants. Conclusions The findings support the conclusions that: a) the mechanism by which apoE confers risk for AD is by catalyzing the polymerization of A{beta} into neurotoxic species, b) targeting apoE is a promising, underappreciated strategy for the prevention of AD, c) imipramine should be used more frequently to treat depression in AD clinical practice, and d) imipramine should be evaluated in prospective trials, particularly in APOE4 carriers, as a potential method to improve cognition and reduce mortality in AD.

items.title_en: NeuralFieldManifold: Uncovering the Manifold Geometry of Local Field Potentials
items.title_zh: NeuralFieldManifold：揭示局部场电位的流形几何
items.abstract_en: Manifold geometry has become a powerful framework for understanding how the brain organizes high-dimensional neural activity into compact, interpretable structure. To date, however, most theoretical and methodological advances in neural manifold analysis have focused on spiking activity, leaving unresolved a fundamental question: What are the geometric principles governing the dynamics of local field potentials (LFPs); population level signals reflecting integrated subthreshold and suprathreshold neural activity that are broadly integral to clinical and brain-computer interface settings. Here, we establish, analytically and empirically, that the lag-embedded dynamics of LFP signals lie on a low-dimensional K-torus, where K directly relates to sustained oscillatory modes present in the signal. Modeling LFPs as bounded autoregressive processes, we show that each oscillatory component contributes an independent circular degree of freedom, while aperiodic 1/f structure and noise contribute only geometric thickness around the manifold without altering its topology. To apply this theory to real nonstationary recordings, we introduce DeepLagField, a physics-informed network that jointly estimates time-varying AR structure and effective model order, with formal guarantees that local toroidal geometry is preserved despite non-stationary nature of neuronal processes. Persistent homology analysis on real recordings reveals topological signatures consistent with the predicted toroidal Betti numbers in primate V1 LFP, rodent hippocampal LFP, and mouse cortical EEG, with varying degrees of agreement across recordings and temporal windows. Crucially, decoding analyses across three distinct neural datasets demonstrate that these geometric structures are not merely descriptive but capture behaviorally relevant information rivaling conventional spectral features. Together, these findings establish a theoretically grounded and empirically validated geometric framework for neural field analysis, extending the manifold perspective beyond spiking activity and offering a complementary language to spectral analysis for understanding and translating population dynamics across neural modalities.

items.title_en: Hmox1/CO regulates retina regeneration via modulation of Wnt/β-catenin signalling and induction of vaspb in zebrafish
items.title_zh: Hmox1/CO通过调控Wnt/β-catenin信号传导和诱导斑马鱼vaspb来调节视网膜再生
items.abstract_en: Muller glia (MG) in the zebrafish retina retain a latent stem cell capacity that is absent in mammals, yet the injury responsive signals that drive this reprogramming remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify heme oxygenase-1 (Hmox1), the stress-inducible, rate-limiting enzyme of heme catabolism, as a previously unrecognized regulator of this process. Following injury, hmox1a is selectively and rapidly induced among the heme oxygenase gene family, localizing to photoreceptors with expression peaking during the MG proliferation window. Pharmacological inhibition and morpholino mediated knockdown of Hmox1 dysregulate the acute inflammatory response, impair Muller glia-derived progenitor cell (MGPC) proliferation, and produce lasting deficits in retinal lamination, establishing Hmox1 as a potentially non-redundant, early-acting node required for structural recovery. Exogenous delivery of carbon monoxide (CO), a bioactive Hmox1 metabolite, partially rescues each of these phenotypes, functionally implicating CO as a key downstream effector. Mechanistically, Hmox1/CO signalling stabilizes {beta}-catenin likely via transcriptional repression of the Wnt antagonist dkk1b. This stabilized {beta}-catenin is enriched at a predicted Tcf7l2 site in the promoter of vaspb, which encodes an actin binding protein and is newly identified here as an injury-induced Wnt target gene. Bioinformatic and functional analyses further implicate Nfe2l2a (Nrf2) as a candidate intermediary bridging Hmox1/CO to Wnt regulation, with putative antioxidant response elements identified within the dkk1b locus. Together, these findings outline a putative Hmox1[->]CO[->]Nrf2[->]dkk1b[->]{beta}-catenin[->]vaspb relay coupling redox biology to Wnt-dependent glial reprogramming. Notably, HO-1 is similarly induced in stressed mammalian retina, yet Wnt/{beta}-catenin activation fails to sustain regeneration, positioning the Hmox1/CO axis as a candidate target for future investigation in mammalian retina regeneration.

items.title_en: Brain-wide representations of olfactory behavior in C. elegans
items.title_zh: 秀丽隐杆线虫嗅觉行为的全脑表征
items.abstract_en: Olfactory navigation emerges from dynamic interactions between sensory input, brain activity state and the animal's own movements. In C. elegans, a compact nervous system enables brain-wide imaging in behaving animals exposed to controlled olfactory environments, with an undulatory locomotion that reduces navigation to transitions among forward runs, reversals, and turns. Here, we used tracking microscopy to record and compare brain-wide neural activity in crawling worms navigating spatial odor gradients or isotropic environments, and in immobilized worms responding to temporal odor pulses. Across conditions, we identified strongly correlated brain-wide activity patterns spanning olfactory sensory neurons, interneurons, and premotor interneurons. Comparisons between navigation in odor gradients and exploration in isotropic environments revealed a compact functional circuit linking olfactory sensory neurons, interneurons, and premotor neurons. Comparisons between different odors distinguished sensory activity relationships associated with odor identity from a shared sensorimotor circuit for navigational movement. Comparisons between crawling and immobilized animals revealed profound differences in motor-state transitions and brain-wide correlation structure, further demonstrating the dependence of sensory representations and motor decision-making on behavioral context. Our findings reveal a functional organization linking olfactory sensory activity to navigational movement and show how this organization depends on behavioral state and environmental context.

items.title_en: Graph neural network approach for inferring neuronal connectivity
items.title_zh: 用于推断神经元连接性的图神经网络方法
items.abstract_en: Understanding the connectivity of neuronal networks is essential for understanding brain function. Current anatomical mapping techniques, such as serial section microscopy and viral tracing, are resource-intensive and cannot capture the efficacy of connectivity. A complementary approach is to infer effective connectivity from single-neuron-resolution population activity. We developed a graph neural network (GNN)-based tool, CircuitGNN, that accurately infers neural effective connectivity from population activity. CircuitGNN accurately inferred the connectivity of several small circuits and detected both the strengthening and weakening of connections, such as those that occur during learning. CircuitGNN outperformed other methods when applied to simulated population activity generated by an invertebrate central pattern-generating circuit and a cortical microcircuit. CircuitGNN was evaluated on networks of varying size, recording duration, and proportion of hidden neurons. Although performance improved with longer recordings, CircuitGNN achieved high precision with recordings as short as 4 min, scaled to large circuits of up to ~750 neurons, and remained robust when 20% or 40% of neurons were hidden. These results establish CircuitGNN as an accurate and robust technique for inferring neural connectivity from activity.

items.title_en: Noise-referenced multi-shell diffusion-weighted imaging for regional cerebrospinal fluid thermometry
items.title_zh: 用于区域脑脊液测温的噪声参考多壳扩散加权成像
items.abstract_en: We developed a multi-shell diffusion-weighted imaging approach for separate ventricular and subarachnoid cerebrospinal fluid thermometry. The approach uses measured image noise to assess agreement among temperature estimates. In 12 participants, temperature was estimated from four non-zero diffusion weightings.
