For each voxel, disagreement between these estimates was compared with that expected from image noise, accounting for their shared reference image. Voxels meeting this consistency criterion were retained for regional analysis. Mean diffusion-derived temperature ({+/-} SD) was 38.4 {+/-} 0.4 {degrees}C in the lateral ventricles and 36.0 {+/-} 1.1 {degrees}C in the subarachnoid space. Ventricular estimates were consistently higher than subarachnoid estimates across all participants, with a mean difference of 2.4 {+/-} 1.2 {degrees}C (95% confidence interval 1.6 -3.1 {degrees}C). This difference persisted under alternative noise models and temperature estimators. Subarachnoid estimates increased with retained voxel count; in a post hoc analysis of the six participants with the largest retained counts, ventricular estimates remained higher by 1.6 {+/-} 0.7 {degrees}C. Absolute temperature accuracy and the physiological origin of the regional difference require independent validation. This approach provides an internal consistency check for CSF thermometry and supports separate assessment of ventricular and subarachnoid temperatures.

items.title_en: Adipocyte Kindlin-2 Coordinates an E-cadherin/β-catenin/IGFBP2 Endocrine Axis to Regulate Skin Regeneration and Diabetic Wound Healing
items.title_zh: 脂肪细胞Kindlin-2协调E-cadherin/β-catenin/IGFBP2内分泌轴调控皮肤再生与糖尿病伤口愈合
items.abstract_en: Skin wound healing is a complex, multicellular process essential for maintaining tissue integrity and homeostasis. Despite advances in biomaterial and cell-based therapies, the mechanisms by which adipose tissue regulates skin regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify adipocyte Kindlin-2 as a critical regulator of cutaneous wound repair. Adipocyte-specific deletion of Kindlin-2 markedly accelerates wound closure in mice by enhancing fibroblast proliferation, angiogenesis, and suppressing inflammation. Transplantation of visceral white adipose tissue (vWAT) from Kindlin-2-deficient mice similarly promotes wound healing, indicating an endocrine contribution of vWAT to skin regeneration. Mechanistically, loss of Kindlin-2 promotes E-cadherin proteolysis, resulting in increased release of a 33-kDa C-terminal fragment (CTF2) that activates {beta}-catenin signaling and induces transcriptional upregulation and secretion of insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2 (IGFBP2). Elevated circulating IGFBP2, in turn, stimulates integrin signaling in target cells to enhance wound repair. Pharmacological inhibition of {beta}-catenin signaling abrogated the healing advantage conferred by Kindlin-2 deficiency. Conversely, local delivery of IGFBP2 via lentiviral significantly accelerates wound closure in both wild-type C57BL/6 and diabetic ob/ob mice. Collectively, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized adipose-skin endocrine axis governed by Kindlin-2 and IGFBP2 that orchestrates tissue regeneration. Targeting this Kindlin-2/E-cadherin/{beta}-catenin/IGFBP2 pathway offers a promising therapeutic strategy for enhancing wound healing, particularly in chronic and diabetic wounds.

items.title_en: The pupal stage shapes life-history trade-offs across metamorphosis
items.title_zh: 蛹期塑造跨变态的生活史权衡
items.abstract_en: Dealing with ecological stressors during development often comes at the expense of later-life performance. Although such trade-offs are well studied as two-stage systems such as larva-adult trade-offs, they are rarely examined across multiple developmental stages, limiting our understanding of how ecological effects are integrated throughout complex life cycles. We addressed this gap using a multistage experimental framework in Aedes aegypti, where we exposed individuals to predation risk during the larval stage, the pupal stage, both stages, or neither, and quantified developmental, physiological, and adult fitness traits. Contrary to expectations, predation risk across successive stages did not produce cumulative fitness costs, and traits varied in their responses. Both males and females emerged faster when exposed to risk, with lighter bodies, but males paid an additional cost of reduced starvation resistance when the pupal stage was exposed. Surprisingly, despite their lower body mass, females showed enhanced reproductive performance when both stages were exposed to risk. Overall, responses were stage- and sex-specific, with exposure during the non-feeding pupal stage imposing greater life-history costs than larval exposure alone. Measurements across the larva-pupa-adult continuum further revealed that traits such as body mass and energy reserves respond differently before and after metamorphosis, highlighting the role of the pupa in mediating trade-offs. Our findings identify the pupal stage as a critical mediator of life-history trade-offs and demonstrate the value of a multistage framework for understanding the role of each stage in life-history evolution.

items.title_en: Cell-lineage selection interacts with development and life history to shape the rates and identity of heritable mutations
items.title_zh: 细胞谱系选择与发育和生活史相互作用，塑造可遗传突变的速率与类型
items.abstract_en: Mutation rates determine the supply of heritable variation and are central to evolutionary theory, yet they are usually treated as properties of molecular mutational processes. We hypothesised that mutation rates are also shaped by selection among cell lineages within organisms and that the strength of this process depends on developmental and life-history traits. To test the extent of this idea, we combined mathematical modelling with experiments in Drosophila melanogaster and treated mutation rates as emergent properties of interactions among molecular mutagenesis, development, life history, and cell-lineage selection. The model predicts that even modest effects of mutations on cellular fitness can substantially alter the probability that mutations are transmitted, and that these effects depend strongly on developmental architecture, germline dynamics, and time to reproduction. In Drosophila, we experimentally demonstrate biased transmission of a mutation affecting cellular proliferation and show that this bias changes over the reproductive lifespan of the individual. Extending the model genome-wide reveals that the cellular distribution of fitness effects and its interaction with developmental parameters influence both the estimated mutation rate and the composition of transmitted mutations, producing transmission biases that favour mutations with particular cellular fitness effects. These results suggest that developmental and life-history parameters determine how cellular fitness effects translate into transmission bias; therefore, estimates of heritable mutational input can vary from species to species even under constant molecular mutagenesis. By filtering mutations before they enter populations, developmental and life-history evolution can modify both the rate and the nature of heritable variation and thereby influence evolutionary trajectories.

items.title_en: Association between trajectories of breastfeeding duration and infant health: Prospective cohort study
items.title_zh: 母乳喂养持续时间轨迹与婴儿健康的关联：前瞻性队列研究
items.abstract_en: Background: Breastfeeding is a modifiable pathway contributing to infant health. Objectives: To estimate trajectories of breastfeeding and the association between trajectories of breastfeeding and infant health. Methods: We conducted a prospective longitudinal cohort study (2014-2020, Canada) with 3217 cohabitating English-literate mother-father-infant triads with internet or telephone access. Women with major psychiatric conditions or suicidality were excluded. Data were collected online at baseline ( 90th percentile). We estimated trajectories of breastfeeding using latent class growth analysis. Associations were estimated using adjusted linear mixed models. Results: Most included mothers (n=2548) were of Canadian birth (2078/2548, 82%) and graduated from university (1920/2548, 75%); few reported unemployment (222/2548, 9%) or prenatal depression (240/2548, 9%). We identified two trajectories of breastfeeding: Constant Breastfeeding (1522/2548, 60%) and Decreasing Breastfeeding (1026/2548, 40%). No statistically significant differences were observed between classes for either the risk of challenging behaviors (RR -0.006 95% CI -0.028 to 0.016) or the risk of emergent visits (RR -0.015 95% CI -0.053 to 0.023). Conclusions: In this study, discontinued breastfeeding was not associated with infant health. Future studies should focus on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding, a modifiable therapeutic infant feeding target.

items.title_en: Maternal ADHD and exclusive breastfeeding: A prospective community-based cohort study
items.title_zh: 母亲ADHD与纯母乳喂养：一项前瞻性社区队列研究
items.abstract_en: Importance: Maternal attention-deficit disorder with or without hyperactivity (ADHD) is an established risk factor for adverse perinatal outcomes that remains understudied to breastfeeding. Objective: To estimate the effect of maternal ADHD on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding. Design: A prospective longitudinal community-based cohort study. Setting: Canada, 2014-2020. Participants: We included 3217 English-literate mother-father dyads with internet or telephone access, comprising women with singleton birth within 3 weeks postpartum (study baseline) and were cohabiting with the biological father. Women with major psychiatric conditions or suicidality were excluded. All participants provided informed consent at recruitment. Data were collected online through self-report questionnaires. Exposure: Maternal ADHD was measured at baseline using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (sum of scores [≥]14). Main Outcomes and Measures: We defined 6-month exclusive breastfeeding based on maternal reported infant feeding, assessed at 3 and 6 months. Maternal childhood adversity (Adverse Childhood Experiences International Questionnaire, ACE-IQ; sum score) was included as a confounder. The average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) was estimated using linear probability models. We calculated 95% percentile bootstrap CI. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation by chained equations with 10 iterations. Results: Complete-case analyses included 2071/3217 mother-father dyads, most of which were Canadian-born (79%). Childhood adversity, mental health conditions, and substance use were higher among mothers who screened positive for ADHD (4%) than among those who did not: the median number of ACE was 5 IQR 4-6; 38% self-reported prenatal depression, 13% smoked cigarettes and 19% drank alcohol during pregnancy; 11% of infants used the neonatal intensive care unit. Notably, though 90% of mothers with ADHD intended to breastfeed exclusively only 28% breastfed exclusively for 6 months. Among families with maternal ADHD, the effect of maternal ADHD on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding was ATT -0.105, 95% CI -0.209 to -0.003 in the model adjusted for maternal ACE and paternal ADHD. With multiple imputation: ATT -0.109, 95% CI -0.213 to -0.004. Conclusions and Relevance: Mothers with ADHD intend to breastfeed their infants exclusively, but additional challenges shorten the duration of exclusive breastfeeding, indicating a need for interventions tailored to neurodevelopmental differences.

items.title_en: Polydrug use and recreational motives are associated with lower posttraumatic symptoms in survivors of a mass trauma event
items.title_zh: 多药使用和娱乐性动机与大规模创伤事件幸存者较低创伤后症状相关
items.abstract_en: Objective: Drug use after trauma is common, but polydrug use patterns, motives, and associations with subsequent symptoms are poorly understood. We examined these associations among mass-casualty terror attack survivors, 72% of whom used drugs immediately before trauma exposure. Methods: Survivors of the October 7, 2023 Nova Festival attack reported use of six drug types (alcohol, cannabis, ketamine, stimulants, MDMA, psychedelics) and motives (avoidance, emotional regulation, self-medication, sleep, recreation) longitudinally at three timepoints (TP): 1-6 months (N=772), 8-12 months (N=453), and 17-24 months (N=302) post-attack. Separate latent class analyses of TP2 data characterized drug use, motives, and their combination. Linear regression and mixed-effects models examined associations between class membership and PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) scores, adjusting for age, sex, time since trauma, and TP1 PCL-5 scores. Results: At TP2, 70% reported polydrug use, 17% used one drug, and 13% reported no use. The high drug-load class (mean 4.6 drug types) had lower PCL-5 scores than the low drug-load class (mean 1.5 drug types); this difference was evident among participants using [≥]4 drug types and persisted through TP3. The self-medication-motive class had higher PCL-5 scores than the recreational-motive class. In joint analyses, recreational-motive users at both low and high drug loads had lower PCL-5 scores than participants reporting self-medication motives and primarily cannabis use. Conclusions: Polydrug use was common among the mass-trauma survivors in our study. Self-medication motives were associated with higher PTSD symptom severity than recreational motives. Unexpectedly, higher polydrug use was associated with lower PTSD symptom scores.

items.title_en: ACCURACY OF COMPRESSED SENSING ACCELERATED 3D-FLAIR IN THE DIAGNOSTIC WORK-UP OF MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AT 1.5 T
items.title_zh: 压缩感知加速3D-FLAIR在1.5 T多发性硬化诊断检查中的准确性
items.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: 3D-FLAIR is central to MR-based diagnosis and monitoring of MS, but long acquisition times remain a limitation. OBJECTIVES: This single-center prospective non-inferiority study evaluated whether compressed sensing (CS) - accelerated 3D-FLAIR at 1.5T provides lesion detection comparable to optimized Generalized Autocalibrating Partially Parallel Acquisition (GRAPPA) - accelerated 3D-FLAIR. Optimized CS- and GRAPPA-accelerated 3D-FLAIR sequences were incorporated into MRI examinations in patients with known or suspected MS. The primary endpoint was manual lesion count by two blinded readers using a 10% non-inferiority margin. Secondary endpoints included image quality, SNR, CNR, and automated lesion count and volumetry. RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients were included (mean age, 40.1+/-13.3 years; 61.8% women). CS-accelerated 3D-FLAIR reduced acquisition time by 31.8% compared with GRAPPA (4:00 vs 5:52 minutes). Non-inferiority for manual lesion count was demonstrated for both readers (reader A, p < .0001; reader B, p = .005). Interrater agreement was excellent for CS (ICC = 0.921; 95% CI, 0.837-0.957) and very good for GRAPPA (ICC = 0.851; 95% CI, 0.769-0.906). Subjective image quality was high for both techniques. GRAPPA showed higher objective signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise-ratio (CNR), whereas automated lesion counts and volumes were higher for CS. CONCLUSION: CS-accelerated 3D-FLAIR provided non-inferior lesion detection with substantial scan-time reduction.

items.title_en: PROSPECTIVE COMPARISON OF OPTIMIZED COMPRESSED SENSING AND GRAPPA-ACCELERATED 3D-TOF-MRA FOR EVALUATION OF UNTREATED INTRACRANIAL ANEURYSMS AT 1.5 T: A NON-INFERIORITY STUDY
items.title_zh: 优化压缩感知与GRAPPA加速3D-TOF-MRA用于评估1.5 T未治疗颅内动脉瘤的前瞻性比较：一项非劣效性研究
items.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES 3D-TOF-MRA is a standard non-invasive method for detecting and monitoring intracranial aneurysms, but long scan times remain a limitation. Compressed sensing (CS) acceleration for intracranial aneurysm evaluation has mainly been studied at 3T. This prospective single-center non-inferiority study compared CS-accelerated 3D-TOF at 1.5T with GRAPPA-accelerated 3D-TOF-MRA for evaluating untreated intracranial aneurysms. MATERIALS AND METHODS Sample size was determined via a preliminary retrospective study. 25 patients with 32 untreated aneurysms underwent both CS- (factor 7, 3:04 min) and GRAPPA-accelerated (factor 2, 5:00 min) 3D-TOF, yielding a 38.7% scan-time reduction. Two blinded neuroradiologists assessed overall image quality (primary endpoint) and artifacts, subjective CNR, aneurysm delineation and diameters (secondary endpoints). Non-inferiority was tested via one-sided t-test (prespecified 10% margin); interrater agreement used ICC. RESULTS CS demonstrated non-inferiority to GRAPPA for overall image quality in both readers (p <= .023), though interrater agreement was low (ICC 0.241-0.262), reflecting subjective variability. Secondary exploratory analyses showed heterogeneous preferences. ROI-based CNR was lower for CS (median 169.6; IQR, 91.0-226. vs. 278.2; 181.0-366.2). Aneurysm diameter measurements showed excellent interrater agreement for both techniques (CS ICC, 0.899-0.980; GRAPPA ICC, 0.877-0.973; all p < .001). CONCLUSION CS-accelerated 3D-TOF at 1.5T met non-inferiority criteria vs. GRAPPA-TOF for overall image quality, reducing scan time by 38.7% while preserving aneurysm measurement reliability. However, reduced CNR and reader-preference variability important trade-offs.

items.title_en: Fibromuscular Dysplasia in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Common yet Underrecognized Vascular Phenotype in Women
items.abstract_en: Objectives: Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is a non inflammatory, non atherosclerotic arterial disease characterized by multifocal arterial beading that predominantly affects women. Although FMD commonly involves the renal and carotid arteries, its relationship with acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) remains poorly understood. We investigated the proportion of patients with FMD among patients with ATAAD, focusing on sex based differences. Materials and Methods: Patients aged below 70 years with ATAAD and ECG triggered aortic CT angiography (CTA) were consecutively included in this retrospective single-center study. FMD was defined as multifocal arterial beading (string-of-beads appearance) in at least one vascular territory, according to international consensus criteria. The highest-quality CTA examination was evaluated by an experienced cardiovascular radiologist. All suspected FMD cases were independently reviewed by a second experienced cardiovascular radiologist, with the final diagnosis established by consensus. Proportions were reported with 95% confidence intervals and compared between sexes . Results: Of 214 patients screened, 200 were included (138 men and 62 women). FMD was confirmed in 18/200 patients (9%; 95% CI, 6 till 14%), none of whom had a prior FMD diagnosis. FMD was more frequent in women (12/62, 19%; 95% CI, 11 till 31%) than men (6/138, 4%; 95% CI, 2 till 9%; P<0.001). FMD predominantly involved the renal arteries. Additional carotid CTA was available in 49/200 patients (25%) and in 7/18 patients with FMD (39%); three of these seven patients had carotid FMD. Conclusion: FMD was observed in a substantial proportion of patients presenting with ATAAD, particularly women. These findings suggest that FMD is an underrecognized vascular phenotype in patients with ATAAD.

items.title_en: Screening for rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease using lung ultrasound: a systematic review and quality appraisal of recent studies
items.abstract_en: Interstitial lung diseases (ILD) associated with systemic autoimmune disease can have a strong negative impact on patient outcomes. The diagnostic gold standard is high-resolution computer tomography (HRCT). Numerous studies have proven lung ultrasound's (LUS) utility in ILD, as well as other lung pathologies. Recently, there has been more focus on ILD in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a previously overlooked complication, and screening methods. The purpose of this systematic review was to summarize the recent knowledge regarding LUS compared to HRCT in screening ILD in RA patients. We reviewed relevant literature from the last 10 years and selected 10 articles. Results show that LUS is effective compared to HRCT as a screening tool. Several diagnostic and severity scores have been elaborated and tested. Further focus should be on LUS in long-term follow-up and standardization of protocols.

items.title_en: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
items.abstract_en: Background: Cognitive training (CogT) is an established non-pharmacological intervention for people with Parkinson's disease (PD) and mild cognitive impairment (PD-MCI). However, overall effects on cognitive outcomes are small to moderate and interindividually highly heterogeneous. Sleep -especially deep sleep- could be an important determinant of CogT responsiveness in PD, and may have beneficial effects on PD pathophysiology. Therefore, the enhancement of deep sleep by phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) could strengthen the effects of CogT on cognitive symptoms and counteract disease progression. Methods: PD-CogT-Sleep is a monocentric, partly decentralized, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial that combines two remotely delivered non-pharmacological interventions, to assess the additive effect of PTAS on digital CogT responsiveness in people with PD-MCI. The primary outcome is executive functions; Secondary and exploratory outcomes include further cognitive functions, participant-reported outcome measures, blood-based biomarkers, and high-density sleep electroencephalography markers. Outcomes are assessed at baseline, five weeks post-allocation and at 3-month follow-up. We aim to consecutively recruit N=50 participants, who will be randomized 1:1 to receive CogT+PTAS or CogT+Sham. Discussion: The PD-CogT-Sleep study integrates wearable and digital technologies to systematically combine a novel, non-invasive, sleep-enhancing intervention (PTAS) with established CogT to improve cognition and evaluate PTAS' disease-modifying potential through its effects on blood-based biomarkers in PD-MCI. The expected results will foster our understanding of the interplay of sleep, cognition, and neurodegeneration, and may guide further development of safe, feasible, scalable, patient-centered, technology-based non-pharmacological interventions counteracting cognitive decline in neurodegenerative diseases.

items.title_en: Quantitative deep motor phenotyping of 102 people with SCN2A, KCNQ2, CSNK2A1, CACNA1A or SCN8A-related disorders
items.abstract_en: Background and Objectives: Motor dysfunction is a major contributor to disability in pediatric-onset monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), yet systematic quantifications of motor phenotypes across development using validated clinical scales remain underdeveloped. Existing studies have classified motor phenotypes rather than quantified domain-specific severity, limiting their use as outcome measures in clinical trials. Here, we systematically quantify motor dysfunction using established clinical rating scales to explore their utility as motor endpoints. Methods: In this cross-sectional observational study, 102 individuals with NDDs (0.5-38 years) secondary to pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in five genes (SCN2A, KCNQ2, CSNK2A1, CACNA1A, SCN8A) and 31 unaffected sibling controls underwent standardized motor assessments using the Scale for Assessment and Rating of Ataxia, Burke-Fahn-Marsden Dystonia Scale, and the Modified Ashworth Scale. Regional and functional categorization of parameters enabled differentiated interpretation. Gene-specific patterns were evaluated using z-score standardization across the pooled affected cohort, with gene-level averaging and nonparametric bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. Results: Dysfunction was present in individuals with NDDs across speech (90%), coordination (87%), dystonia (83.3%), gross motor (82.4%) and spasticity (42.2%), with minimal impairment in controls (0-12.9%). We observed substantial heterogeneity across motor domains and subdomains; ataxic dysarthria had the highest score distribution (median 0.83 [IQR, 0.17-1.0]), whereas spasticity showed near-floor scores. Individuals with SCN2A variants demonstrated higher mean z-scores across multiple subdomains than other genes, with more consistent deviations observed in coordination and speech domains (Coordination: mean z = 0.29, 95% CI 0.03-0.54; Speech: mean z = 0.3, 95% CI 0.03-0.57), whereas domain-specific or less pronounced patterns were observed in other genes. The ataxia and dystonia scales demonstrated low floor and ceiling effects. Discussion: Using three clinical scales across a broad developmental and functional range, our study moves motor phenotyping in monogenic NDDs from categorical description toward quantitative, domain-resolved severity assessment. Exploratory analysis indicates marked heterogeneity in severity profiles across genes, most notably in SCN2A, suggesting potential selective motor vulnerability. These findings provide evidence for the feasibility of motor phenotyping and provide preliminary, cross-sectional benchmark severity distributions. Subsequent longitudinal validation and validation in larger, longitudinal, and variant-stratified cohorts will enable natural history studies and future therapeutic trials alongside seizure outcomes.

items.title_en: Variant Classification of a Non-Protein Coding Gene: ACMG/AMP Specifications for RMRP from the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel
items.abstract_en: Purpose: This study, conducted by the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel (ClinGen SCID-VCEP), aimed to adapt the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework for germline variant interpretation in RMRP. Unlike the protein-coding genes for which the framework was primarily developed, RMRP encodes a non-protein-coding RNA. Biallelic pathogenic variants in RMRP cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia, which can include severe combined immunodeficiency disease and other immune abnormalities. Methods: An RMRP-focused SCID-VCEP subgroup reviewed all 28 ACMG/AMP evidence criteria using population databases, published clinical and experimental data, computational predictions, and expert consensus. Each criterion was retained, modified, or designated as not applicable based on RMRP biology and disease mechanisms. The resulting specifications were pilot tested using 27 variants selected from ClinVar and research laboratory data. Results: Fifteen ACMG/AMP criteria were determined to be applicable to RMRP, while 13 were considered not applicable. Several criteria were modified to evaluate nucleotide-level effects on transcriptional regulation, critical promoter regions, and RNA secondary structure. The specifications also incorporated RMRP-specific recommendations for population frequency, functional evidence, variant phase, segregation, and phenotype. Application of the specifications classified 6 variants as pathogenic, 10 as likely pathogenic, 7 as variants of uncertain significance, and 4 as benign. Previously pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants remained within the pathogenic spectrum, and all previously benign variants remained benign. Variants with conflicting ClinVar interpretations were resolved as either likely pathogenic or uncertain. PM1, PM3, and PP4 were the primary criteria supporting pathogenic classifications. Conclusion: The SCID-VCEP specifications provide a standardized approach to the classification of germline RMRP variants in cartilage-hair hypoplasia and demonstrate how the ACMG/AMP framework can be adapted for a disease-associated non-protein-coding RNA gene. These specifications support the development of variant interpretation frameworks for other clinically relevant non-protein-coding genes.

items.title_en: Effects of Pantoprazole Based on Dialysis Status: A Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan for a Secondary Analysis of the REVISE Trial
items.abstract_en: Background A recent international randomized trial found that the proton pump inhibitor (PPI) pantoprazole significantly reduced the risk of clinically important upper gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding among invasively ventilated patients in the intensive care unit (ICU), with no effect on mortality. Pantoprazole may be of particularly high utility among patients at high-risk of bleeding, such as those receiving renal replacement therapy (RRT) prior to ICU admission. However, given the complex mechanisms by which renal insufficiency may increase bleeding risk, as well as the possible association between PPI use and adverse kidney outcomes, investigating whether kidney failure treated with RRT at baseline modifies the treatment effect of PPIs is clinically relevant. Methods We have planned a post hoc secondary analysis of the Re-evaluating the Inhibition of Stress Erosions (REVISE) Trial (NCT03374800). The primary objective if this study is to evaluate whether any RRT on study day 1 (e.g., maintenance RRT in the outpatient setting, or RRT initiated in the hospital [intermittent hemodialysis, continuous renal replacement therapy, sustained low efficiency dialysis, or peritoneal dialysis]) modifies the treatment effect of pantoprazole on clinically important upper GI bleeding and 90-day mortality. The secondary objective is to evaluate whether maintenance RRT (intermittent hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis) in an outpatient setting before the index hospital admission modifies the effect of pantoprazole on clinically important upper GI bleeding and 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes for both analyses are patient important upper GI bleeding, ICU and hospital mortality. We will perform Cox proportional-hazard analyses, including the RRT exposure of interest, randomized group, and their interaction for each outcome, reporting results as hazards ratios with 95% confidence intervals, and p-values for the interaction term. Conclusion Results of this study will inform critical care practice, particularly for the care of patients at risk of stress-related GI ulceration in the ICU who have received RRT.

items.title_en: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional Molecular Sequences
items.title_zh: 自动生成新型高功能分子序列
items.abstract_en: While multiple methods now exist to generate functional sequence variants from existing annotated examples, it is unclear how well such methods can be used to generate sequences that exceed the functionality of those contained in the example set. Using two complete fitness landscapes, we quantify how effectively generative tools can search sequence space and find rare, novel, highly functional sequences, focusing on variational auto-encoders and information-theoretic methods. We find that an information-theoretic method that does not require training and runs significantly faster than standard Machine-Learning/Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI) methods also is significantly more effective in finding rare highly-functional sequences. We discuss the application of this novel method to discover rare polypeptides with anti-bacterial properties that are specific to bacterial, but not eukaryotic, cell membranes.
items.abstract_zh: 目前已有多種方法可以从已有标注样本生成功能序列变体，但这些方法能否生成功能超过样本集内序列的新序列，仍不清楚。我们利用两个完整的适应度景观，定量评估生成式工具在序列空间中搜索并找到稀有、新颖、高功能序列的效果，重点考察变分自编码器与信息论方法。我们发现，一种无需训练、运行速度远快于标准机器学习/人工智能（ML/AI）方法的信息论方法，在寻找稀有高功能序列方面也显著更有效。我们还讨论了如何用这一新方法发现具有抗菌特性、且特异作用于细菌细胞膜而非真核细胞膜的稀有���肽。
items.highlight_zh: 无需训练的信息论方法比VAE更快更有效地找出稀有高功能序列
items.digest_zh: 1）研究什么问题：现在有不少生成模型可以从已有标注样本出发，造出“像样”的蛋白或核酸序列。但真正有用的问题是：它们能不能造出功能比训练集中最好的序列还强的新序列？这一点此前缺乏严格检验。2）用了什么方法：作者借助两个已知的“完整适应度景观”——即任意序列的功能值都能被精确计算甚至穷举的数据集——把序列搜索变成一个可严格打分的任务。然后比较变分自编码器（VAE）与一类信息论方法，看谁能在巨大的序列空间中更高效地找到稀有但高功能的序列。3）得到什么结果：一种不需要训练、运行速度显著快于标准ML/AI方法的信息论方法，在找到稀有高功能序列上也显著更有效。也就是说，在这类任务上，“训练一个生成模型去模仿数据分布”未必是最优策略。4）为何重要：序列空间极其庞大而功能实验昂贵，搜索策略的效率直接决定能否发现有用的分子。作者进一步提出把该方法用于发现只攻击细菌膜、不伤真核细胞膜的抗菌多肽，这对应对耐药菌有潜在价值。局限是只在两个适应度景观上做了验证，能否推广到其他蛋白家族与更复杂的功能，还需要更多实验检验。

items.title_en: In-depth data movement characterization of DNA read mapping algorithms
items.abstract_en: Read mapping algorithms represent a critical bottleneck in genomic analysis pipelines due to the resources required; a problem that is becoming more pronounced as sequencing technologies advance and datasets expand. We present an extensive workload characterization of leading read mapping algorithms across diverse sequencing technologies to identify hardware acceleration and optimization opportunities. We analyzed the following implementations: MashMap, wfmash, and Minimap2 for whole-genome alignment (WGA); NGMLR, Minimap2, and LRA for long reads; and Bowtie2, BWA-MEM, StrobeAlign, and minibwa for short reads. We used the Intel VTune Profiler for detailed memory analysis to identify memory- bound functions, cache usage patterns, and data transfer bottlenecks. We further analyzed a selected subset of alignment tools using the DAMOV-SIM simulator to obtain a more granular view of data movement characteristics for two different cache structures. Based on our results, Minimap2 emerges as the fastest alignment tool for long read scenarios, but falls behind in whole-genome alignment due to poor multithreading. Across all three categories, some programs (e.g., LRA, BWA-MEM) are highly memory-bound. More in-depth analysis via DAMOV-SIM revealed that some memory-bound tools, in particular, do not fully utilize the multi-level cache hierarchy in modern multi-core CPU architectures. Our results show that while some tools require algorithmic redesign for performance gains, some others can benefit from running on PIM architectures.

items.title_en: RangeFinder: Predicting Ligand Property Ranges from Protein Pockets
items.title_zh: RangeFinder：从蛋白质口袋预测配体性质范围
items.abstract_en: Identifying ligands for a protein target requires searching a vast chemical space for a comparatively small set of compatible molecules. Existing machine learning approaches primarily address this problem by generating candidate ligands or scoring individual protein-ligand pairs, but provide limited information about the broader chemical space compatible with a binding pocket. We introduce RangeFinder, an SE(3)-equivariant transformer pocket-level model, trained and evaluated on BioLiP2 data, that predicts ranges over nine physicochemical ligand properties directly from pocket structure, chemistry, and evolutionary context. Using an intersection-over-union objective and evaluation metric (range-IoU), RangeFinder achieves a range-IoU of $0.464 \pm 0.002$, outperforming all deployable baselines while requiring only $12.2$ ms per pocket. We also quantify our method's ability to reduce the ligand search space while retaining compatible binders; in this regard, RangeFinder achieves a Reduction-Recall F-Score of $0.543 \pm 0.011$ --- once again outperforming all deployable baselines. Ablation experiments indicate that RangeFinder's performance depends more strongly on the density and quality of ligand supervision than on any individual input modality or specialized training strategy. Together, these results position RangeFinder as an inexpensive and effective molecular filtering prior, with demonstrated potential in narrowing the ligand search space of target pockets before docking, generation, or synthesis. The code for this project can be found at: https://github.com/alannadels/RangeFinder.

items.title_en: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science
items.abstract_en: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and their capabilities have advanced rapidly over the past few years, leading to widespread interest and adoption in the biological and ecological sciences. However, the data infrastructure and computational resources that provide the foundation for AI workflows in ecology and biodiversity science remain fragmented. Moreover, the flow of value remains largely unidirectional: data move from collectors, through repositories and aggregators into models, and finally to research products or management actions. The derived value, such as corrected taxonomies, annotations, quality flags, and insights, rarely returns to source communities. We propose an extension of the original FAIR principles to address the needs of AI-ready infrastructure: the AI-FAIR metadata criteria, which place AI-enabled science in the context of a bidirectional Question-Data-Model triangle. This framework is designed to facilitate large-scale content-based analysis across diverse collections and ensure that the scientists generating the data benefit from the AI-enabled advances built on their data. Alongside these criteria, we introduce an agentic evaluation workflow that both rates existing datasets on the AI-FAIR and traditional FAIR criteria and provides actionable feedback where critical metadata is missing or incomplete. This modular dataset evaluation tool, paired with a domain-appropriate checklist, translates these principles into a reusable assessment of machine-learning readiness, AI-readiness for specified tasks, traceability, and ethical and CARE-aligned stewardship. Through this approach we aim to create a community-informed system to close the model data loop, so that AI also enriches data to further enable scientific discovery.

items.title_en: Intrinsic network dynamics catalyze switching in functional connectivity states of the brain
items.abstract_en: Dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) reflects ongoing reconfiguration of large-scale brain networks, but the temporal organization and network processes underlying spontaneous state transitions remain poorly understood. We developed functional connectivity state switching (FCSS), a phase-coherence-based framework that tracks multiscale changes in dominant whole-brain connectivity configurations. In Human Connectome Project fMRI, FCSS was strongly evoked by cognitive state and condition switches, and distinct transition dynamics differentially predicted working-memory performance. During rest, spontaneous FCSS was characterized by progressive changes in network segregation, integration, and cross-network communication as connectivity approached a switching event. Critically, event-related analysis time-locked to spontaneous FCSS revealed opposing pre-switch dynamics: salience-network contribution increased while default-mode-network contribution decreased, suggesting coordinated engagement and disengagement of these networks before switching. This reciprocal reweighting may provide a network-level mechanism for spontaneous FC reconfiguration. Together, these findings identify both global reorganization and network-specific processes underlying spontaneous and task-evoked brain-state transitions in the human brain.

items.title_en: Scalable Contact-Gated Stochastic Operators and Universal Reduction Laws for Macromolecular Protein Dynamics, Allostery, and Kinetics
items.title_zh: 面向大分子蛋白质动力学、变构与动力学的可扩展接触门控随机算子与普适约化定律
items.abstract_en: Constructing continuous, thermodynamically reversible reduced equations of motion from atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) that scale from fast-folding miniproteins to multi-domain allosteric enzymes in explicit water remains a foundational problem in computational biophysics. Across 15 molecular systems (890,000 SHA-256-verified frames, 0.89 us cumulative sampling) spanning 13 structurally diverse proteins from Chignolin (d=18) to explicit-solvent Adenylate Kinase (d=426, 40,110 particles) and Maltose-Binding Protein (d=738, 49,215 particles), plus two analytical verification peptides (d=2, 4), we formulate a contact-gated, GENERIC-regularized stochastic operator on the backbone torus T^d. We show that collective slow modes compress sub-linearly across two orders of magnitude in chain length - with spectral participation ratio scaling as PR(d)=1.061 d^0.494 (95% CI [0.332, 0.666], Delta AICc=-18.15) and short-time diffusion rank as r_D^90(d)=0.799 d^0.930 (Delta AICc=-14.39) - whereas cumulative 90% equilibrium variance in large native-basin enzymes transitions to extensive proportionality (10.0% blind extrapolation error vs. 35.7% for small-protein power laws). Consequently, macromolecular tractability above d>200 requires off-diagonal sparsity rather than global PCA truncation alone: universal peptide-plane crankshaft anti-correlation (mean R(psi_i, phi_i+1)=-0.603 +/- 0.054) and sparse 3D tertiary contact gating (mean k_eff=5.97, reaching 99.3% sparsity at d=738) enable a sparse directed acyclic contact-graph Cholesky estimator scaling empirically as O(d^0.92) in time and O(d^1.06) in memory (65.8x memory compression, 99.6x faster than Graphical LASSO, and higher blind held-out log-likelihood +0.303/d vs. dense +0.205/d on MBP). Biophysically, relative solvent-accessible surface area (rSASA_i) unifies dry linear equipartition in protein cores (alpha_core=1.00, 12.33% blind thermal error) with viscosity-coupled loops (alpha_loop=1.28) and peptides (alpha_peptide=1.57); parameter-free kinematic projection reproduces solution NMR Lipari-Szabo S^2 order parameters (mean r_s=+0.483 across four BMRB enzymes, Ubiquitin Pearson r=+0.921) and X-ray B-factors (mean r_s=+0.276); and 13-fold zero-shot Leave-One-Protein-Out transfer predicts unseen protein operators directly from static PDB coordinates (r_s=+0.706, R^2=+0.359 ridge; r_s=+0.721, R^2=+0.410 GBDT). Applied to functional discovery, explicit-solvent apo toroidal operators localize mechanical domain-closure hinges in AdK (PR-AUC=0.348) and MBP (AUROC=0.690 vs. 0.446 ANM), resolve distal Met20 FG catalytic loop coupling in E. coli DHFR (71.6% recovery at 93.2% sparsity) and beta1-beta2 Ile44 routing in Ubiquitin (7.1x amplification) on blind trajectories, and quantify sub-diffusive Mori-Zwanzig reaction-coordinate memory (mean gamma_M=0.593 +/- 0.126). A validation-tuned head-to-head benchmark against Markov State Models, TICA, Smoluchowski diffusion, Elastic Network Models, and unconstrained SDEs across all 13 proteins maps the physical regimes where continuous contact-gated GENERIC operators (lowest Frobenius error 0.288, exact 0.000 spurious entropy vs. median 65.79 kB/ns/d, IQR 53.76-104.66, mean 346.17) and discrete or harmonic baselines each excel.

items.title_en: Whole methylome changes in Barrett's metaplasia, dysplasia, and cancer
items.title_zh: Barrett化生、异型增生和癌症中的全甲基化组变化
items.abstract_en: The clinical management of Barrett's esophagus (BE) and the risk of esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) is dependent on the presence or absence of dysplasia. The histopathological diagnosis of dysplasia is unreliable however, and would benefit from additional diagnostic criteria. Here, we obtained EM-seq whole-genome methylation profiles from 86 samples across the BE/EAC disease spectrum, notably supplementing the scant existing methylation evidence for low-grade and high-grade dysplasia. While the bulk of methylation changes occur in the transition from normal squamous epithelium to intestinal metaplasia (non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus), we identified a smaller set of changes that mark the onset of dysplasia and progression to EAC. Methylation changes were broadly independent of copy number variation. They were tightly anticorrelated with RNA-seq expression for some genes. Deconvolution of the bulk methylation signatures into constituent cell types revealed four sample groupings enriched with a particular cell type (squamous, columnar, lymphoid and erythroid cells), somewhat reflecting existing clinical classifications. We outline potential markers that could improve the diagnosis of metaplasia and dysplasia in EAC.

items.title_en: Characterizing the Metabolic Fate and Pharmacokinetics of the RyR2 Inhibitor ent-Verticilide
items.title_zh: 表征RyR2抑制剂ent-Verticilide的代谢命运与药代动力学
items.abstract_en: ent-Verticilide is a synthetic macrocyclic depsipeptide and ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) inhibitor with potential therapeutic applications in cardiac arrhythmias. This study characterized its in vitro metabolism and in vivo pharmacokinetics to better understand factors that may influence its disposition. Metabolic stability was evaluated in mouse, rat, dog, and human liver S9 fractions, followed by CYP reaction phenotyping in human liver microsomes and metabolite profiling in human and rat liver S9 fractions. Pharmacokinetics were evaluated in rats following intravenous and oral administration. ent-Verticilide underwent rapid, NADPH-dependent depletion across all species, with in vitro half-lives ranging from 2.1 to 5.3 min. CYP reaction phenotyping indicated that CYP3A was the predominant CYP subfamily involved in its metabolism. Eight putative metabolites were identified in human and rat liver S9, primarily resulting from hydroxylation, oxidation, and desaturation, with generally similar metabolite profiles between species. In rats, ent-verticilide exhibited a systemic clearance of 29.6 mL/min/kg, a steady-state volume of distribution of 4.86 L/kg, and a terminal half-life of 6.85 h following intravenous administration. Absolute oral bioavailability was 10.5%. Overall, these findings show that ent-verticilide undergoes extensive oxidative hepatic metabolism and provide an initial DMPK framework for its continued preclinical development.

items.title_en: Mapping and Probing the Substrate Scope of a Ketoamide-Forming Splicease by Computational Design
items.title_zh: 通过计算设计绘制和探测酮酰胺形成剪接酶的底物范围
items.abstract_en: -Keto-{beta}-amide warheads are protease-inhibiting pharmacophores in peptidomimetic antiviral drugs and drug leads, but their diversity-oriented synthesis for library-based drug discovery can be challenging. The same moiety is installed enzymatically in gene-encoded peptides by tyramine spliceases from spliceotide natural products. However, their substrate scope remains poorly understood. We mined bacterial spliceotide pathways for multi-precursor spliceases and identified HypX from Hyella patelloides that modified 5 of 7 native precursors in E. coli. Single-point mutagenesis showed promiscuity for HypX and the previously identified PlpX but different substrate scopes, suggesting that splicease mining can provide enzymes for focused libraries of various substrate types. To evaluate multipoint variants without exhaustive screening, we combined AlphaFold3 models with Rosetta calculations to rank millions of variants. Top-scoring peptides were spliced more efficiently than single-point mutants. Structural modeling rationalized position-specific tolerance, including a cofactor constraint. This work establishes a mining- and structure-guided strategy to streamline library-based splicease applications.

items.title_en: Facing the waves of negative mood: Trait mindfulness moderates the links between physiology and emotion
items.title_zh: 面对负性情绪的浪潮：特质正念调节生理与情绪之间的联系
items.abstract_en: Trait mindfulness is a dispositional ability characterized by awareness, non-judgment, and acceptance of internal and external experiences. Stress is associated with numerous psychological and physical health concerns including depression and anxiety. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) have consistently been shown to reduce perceived stress and improve a variety of other health outcomes. However, the mechanisms through which mindfulness confers these benefits are not yet fully understood. This study aimed to examine (1) the relationship between trait mindfulness and changes in cortisol following a negative Mood Induction Procedure (MIP) and (2) whether trait mindfulness moderates the relationship between changes in cortisol and mood reactivity following a negative MIP. Participants were recruited from the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex (N = 25 participants) and completed a series of self-report questionnaires, negative and positive mood induction, and mood assessments. Participants provided salivary cortisol samples before and after negative MIPs. Results indicated that, following the negative MIP, sadness and anxiety were associated with greater reductions in cortisol. Trait mindfulness moderated these associations. Overall, these findings contribute to a broader understanding of emotional responses to negatively-valenced stressors and how they are mitigated by mindfulness. They suggest support for future applications of mindfulness-based interventions in high-stress populations.

items.title_en: Anorectal care products cause variable inflammation and adverse barrier effects in a mucosal epithelial model
items.title_zh: 肛肠护理产品在黏膜上皮模型中引起不同程度的炎症和不良屏障效应
items.abstract_en: Introduction: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and colorectal cancer (CRC) are rising in the United States, yet their shared mucosal environment remains underexplored. Rectal douching, a common practice among individuals engaging in receptive anal intercourse, has been epidemiologically linked to increased STI and HPV risk, but biological mechanisms are unclear. Methods: Using a human colorectal epithelial co-culture model (Caco-2/HT29-MTX-E12), we compared the effects of common douching products on cell viability, barrier integrity, and cytokine response. Results: Hyperosmolar or surfactant-containing solutions, including saline enemas, detergents, and soaps, caused rapid declines in metabolic activity and transepithelial electrical resistance, coupled with IL-6 and TNF- upregulation. In contrast, isotonic formulations maintained epithelial viability and barrier function comparable to buffered controls while reducing inflammatory signaling. Discussion: These findings provide mechanistic evidence that many consumer douching products compromise mucosal health and highlight the feasibility of harm-reduction designs for safer anal hygiene and sexual preparation.

items.title_en: Metagenome-assembled genomes reveal water-mass-associated distribution ecotypes of marine Archaea in the Western Arctic Ocean
items.title_zh: 宏基因组组装基因组揭示北冰洋西部海洋古菌与水团相关的分布生态型
items.abstract_en: Archaea are important contributors to marine biogeochemical cycling, yet their ecology remains poorly characterized in the Arctic Ocean. The three dominant marine archaeal lineages, Marine Groups I, II, and III (MG-I, MG-II, and MG-III), are generally reported to have distinct, clade-consistent vertical distributions that are attributed to light penetration and temperature. Here, we used shotgun metagenomic sequencing of seawater collected during the 2015 U.S. Arctic GEOTRACES expedition (GN01) to recover archaeal metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from the Western Arctic Ocean and to relate their relative abundances to water mass structure. Temperature, salinity, silicate, and N* distinguished four water mass layers: the summer surface layer, the Polar Mixed Layer, Atlantic Water, and Arctic Ocean basin water. Of 155 MAGs recovered from a metagenomic co-assembly, 17 were archaeal and represented all three marine groups (four MG-I, eleven MG-II, and two MG-III). Abundance-based clustering of samples from two deep central Arctic stations separated microbial communities according to water mass. Mapping MAG relative abundance across several hundred samples revealed surface, mid-depth, and deep distribution ecotypes; members of every marine group displayed more than one ecotype, and ecotype was not consistent with MAG phylogeny. These results indicate that archaeal distributions in the Western Arctic Ocean are more closely tied to water mass stratification than to clade identity, and that previously reported clade-specific depth distributions of marine Archaea may partly reflect the limited resolution of amplicon-based surveys and shallow sampling.

items.title_en: Guanosine tetraphosphate (ppGpp) promotes tolerance to 2 excess light in Arabidopsis thaliana.
items.title_zh: 鸟苷四磷酸（ppGpp）促进拟南芥对过量光的耐受性
items.abstract_en: Guanosine tetraphosphate (ppGpp) is a hyperphosphorylated nucleotide originally discovered in prokaryotes and found in the chloroplasts of plants and algae. In plants, ppGpp regulates photosynthetic activity, which is important in acclimation to environmental stresses such as nitrogen limitation. However, the full range of stresses involving ppGpp signalling is not yet known. Here, we investigated the role of ppGpp accumulation in the acclimation of plants to excess light. We found that the over-accumulation of ppGpp in transgenic lines that overexpress RSH3 (OX:RSH3) increases tolerance to excess light. Although ppGpp leads to higher non-photochemical energy dissipation (NPQ) than in wild-type plants, we show that NPQ is not critical for the enhanced excess light tolerance. Rather, our results show that ppGpp accumulation leads to broad changes in plant physiology that prime plants to resist and subsequently recover from excess light exposure. ppGpp levels themselves also increase in response to excess light exposure, suggesting that ppGpp may play a physiological role in excess light acclimation. Our work adds to a growing body of evidence for the importance of ppGpp in plant stress acclimation.

items.title_en: Cholinergic-dopaminergic synergy and antagonism shape prediction-error broadcasting
items.title_zh: 胆碱能-多巴胺能协同与拮抗塑造预测误差广播
items.abstract_en: Cholinergic and dopaminergic pathways control reinforcement learning, yet how their basal forebrain and midbrain populations interact remains unresolved. We simultaneously monitored both systems using dual-cell-type optogenetic tagging and neurotransmitter measurements in mice engaged in psychometric learning. Their activity contributed synergistically to reward prediction-error signaling. However, punishment-inhibited dopaminergic neurons showed antagonistic interactions with cholinergic neurons as well. Optogenetic stimulation and channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping revealed a cholinergic-to-dopaminergic disynaptic inhibitory pathway through basal forebrain GABAergic neurons consistent with this antagonism. Chemogenetic suppression of cholinergic activity reduced dopaminergic responses to reward-predicting stimuli, attenuated punishment-induced dopamine suppression, and impaired learning. These findings reveal how a common underlying circuit architecture can flexibly shape prediction-error signaling through synergistic and antagonistic interactions, with implications for adaptive learning and neuropsychiatric disease.

items.title_en: Assessing reinforcement learning and vigor with an online decision-making battery
items.title_zh: 通过在线决策成套测验评估强化学习与活力
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning and vigor are two fundamental aspects of decision-making modulated by dopamine. Although vigor is highly relevant for mood disorders, it has been overlooked by previous batteries characterizing decision-making abilities. We developed a test battery with two RL tasks (RL/working memory, go/no-go task) and two vigor tasks (physical effort discounting, foraging task) and administered it to an online community sample (N = 162). We used computational modeling and factor analysis to identify two factors reflecting RL and vigor. The RL factor reflected participants' general decision-making ability, while vigor corresponded to a motivational propensity to obtain rewards. Both factors demonstrated moderately strong test-retest reliability (ICC(2,1) = .65 and .67, respectively) over a one-to-two-week interval. Moreover, both factors were meaningfully related to self-report scales. The RL and vigor factors were negatively and positively associated with mania, respectively, although further analyses revealed that vigor was not fully independent of RL. Neither factor was significantly associated with depression symptoms. Collectively, we present preliminary evidence that vigor may represent a separate factor from RL in line with the putative dopamine hypothesis, paving the way for future longitudinal assessments of RL and vigor in mood disorders.

items.title_en: Betrayal is worse than loss during cooperation
items.title_zh: 合作中背叛比损失更严重
items.abstract_en: Cooperative behavior refers to activities that benefit another individual or benefit both the person performing the behavior and the recipient. Although both betrayal aversion and loss aversion (the financial detriment incurred from betrayal) are established determinants of cooperative behavior, their relative potency remains undetermined. Here, we investigated these effects by integrating computational modeling and event-related potential (ERP) techniques. In two tasks involving risk and cooperation, participants decided whether to take financial risks or to cooperate under possible betrayal. Our results showed that betrayal aversion had a stronger effect on reducing cooperation compared to loss aversion. Furthermore, ERP data demonstrated a temporal pattern consistent with sequential processing: betrayal was encoded early in decision-making, reflected by increased P3 with weaker betrayal aversion, whereas loss aversion manifested later, marked by increased LPP. By dissociating the contributions of betrayal and loss, our finding provides novel insights into the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying cooperative behavior.

items.title_en: An interferon-like off-switch in invertebrates: Vago4 downregulates Domeless to restrain JAK/STAT signaling
items.title_zh: 无脊椎动物中的干扰素样关闭开关：Vago4下调Domeless以抑制JAK/STAT信号传导
items.abstract_en: Whether invertebrates possess a functional interferon (IFN)-like system remains controversial, as canonical IFN ligands and their receptors are absent from invertebrate genomes. Although Vago proteins in Drosophila and shrimp are compelling functional analogs of IFN, direct evidence for a canonical cytokine-receptor axis and, importantly, for how such signaling is restrained to prevent excessive immune activation, has been lacking. Here, we identify Vago4 as a bona fide ligand of Domeless, the canonical type I cytokine receptor upstream of JAK/STAT signaling. Vago4 binds the extracellular CBM1 and CBM2 domains of Domeless, triggering receptor endocytosis followed by lysosomal trafficking and K27-linked ubiquitination-dependent proteasomal degradation. This ligand-induced receptor downregulation serves as a negative feedback mechanism that restrains excessive JAK/STAT activation. During acute Vibrio infection, Vago4 silencing accelerated shrimp mortality, whereas recombinant Vago4 alleviated inflammatory lesions and oxidative stress, enhanced phagocytosis, and improved survival, phenocopying JAK or STAT knockdown. Thus, by downregulating Domeless, Vago4 limits immunopathology and defines an IRF-Vago4-Domeless-JAK/STAT IFN-like axis in invertebrates, offering new insight into the evolution of IFN-mediated immune regulation.

items.title_en: Somatic genetic variation shapes clonal selection of memory NK cells
items.title_zh: 体细胞遗传变异塑造记忆NK细胞的克隆选择
items.abstract_en: Adaptive immune memory relies on selective clonal expansion and persistence of lymphocyte populations. Whether and how clonal selection occurs in innate lymphocytes that lack rearranged antigen receptors remains poorly understood. Here, we used somatic genetics to reconstruct the natural history of human natural killer (NK) cell responses to cytomegalovirus infection. Across a large cohort of healthy seropositive individuals, we found strong clonal dominance in memory NK cells consistent with clonal selection. Dominant memory NK cell clones were marked by coherent receptor and chromatin configurations, emerged early in life and diversified into genetically related subclones. Both an excess of coding mutations, and the reconstructed population dynamics of the dominant clones, provided evidence for positive selection acting on somatic genetic variation. We identified somatic loss-of-function mutations in the chromatin modifier KMT2D, and showed in a mouse model that Kmt2d deletion alters NK-cell fitness depending on timing and environmental context. Together, these findings establish clonal selection as an organizing principle of human NK-cell memory and support a model in which heritable cell states and acquired genetic variation contribute to shape clonal competition.

items.title_en: Age Associated Shifts Toward Anaerobic Taxa and Amino Acid Degradation Potential in the Canine Oral Microbiome
items.abstract_en: Introduction: Periodontal disease is common in dogs and is associated with changes in oral microbial community composition. How the canine oral microbiome restructures across age at both ecological and metabolic levels remains incompletely characterized. Methods: We analyzed shotgun metagenomic buccal-swab profiles from 1,125 dogs using MetaPhlAn. Functional profiles from HUMAnN were analyzed at pathway and functional-group levels. We annotated species-level taxa with oxygen preference and evaluated oxygen-tolerant and anaerobic taxa abundances across age. We also characterized community structure, metabolic potential, Shannon diversity, and age and weight prediction using nested cross-validated Elastic Net models. Results: Age was associated with substantial restructuring in the oral microbiome. Mean oxygen-tolerant taxa abundance decreased from 67.5% in puppies to 29.1% in mature dogs, whereas anaerobic abundance increased from 14.3% to 53.8%. The oxygen-tolerant: anaerobe log-ratio declined with age (Spearman {rho} = -0.616). Metabolic profiles also varied with age, with higher amino-acid-degradation potential and lower glycolysis and central-carbohydrate potential, and aerobic-respiration-I abundance in older dogs. Shannon diversity increased with age ({rho} = 0.537, p < 0.001). Elastic Net models trained on microbiome species abundance predicted age (Pearson r = 0.609; R-squared = 0.371) and weight (r = 0.498; R-squared = 0.248) with moderate accuracy. Discussion: Canine age was associated with coordinated changes in oral-community oxygen preference and metabolic pathways. These findings extend prior taxon-specific observations by examining a broader ecological shift and metabolic potential in the canine oral microbiome. This provides a reference for future longitudinal or clinical studies of oral maturation and periodontal disease.

items.title_en: Genome-wide CRISPRi-seq maps essential-gene contributions to aminoglycoside susceptibility in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
items.abstract_en: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic ESKAPE pathogen whose multiple intrinsic and acquired antibiotic resistance mechanisms restrict treatment options. Essential genes offer potential antimicrobial targets, but their vulnerability to partial inhibition and contribution to antibiotic susceptibility remain incompletely characterized. Here, we developed a rhamnose-inducible CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) platform and an 83,078-guide library for genome-wide screening in PAO1, with mismatch guides enabling graded repression. Fitness profiling in antibiotic-free Mueller-Hinton medium identified 743 genes whose repression reduced competitive fitness and revealed sequence features associated with guide performance. Combining full-match and mismatch-guide responses revealed substantial variation in essential-gene fitness effects across predicted repression strengths, while comparison of fitness profiles between Mueller-Hinton medium and fetal bovine serum identified condition-dependent effects alongside a conserved fitness landscape. Under aminoglycoside exposure, we identified 118 recurrent sensitizing and 120 recurrent protective gene knockdowns, including many targeting essential and fitness-associated functions. Growth and killing assays with individual strains confirmed that CRISPRi targeting of atpI, accC, secA and ftsZ enhanced tobramycin activity. Finally, transcriptome analysis of these knockdowns confirmed target silencing, captured polar effects on neighboring genes and revealed distinct but overlapping transcriptional responses. Together, these findings quantify the variable fitness costs of essential-gene repression and identify candidate targets for potentiating aminoglycoside activity. IMPORTANCE Essential bacterial genes are difficult to study because their complete disruption prevents growth. Yet knowing that a gene is essential does not reveal how strongly its activity must be reduced to impair growth. Here, we developed a method to examine how reduced gene expression affects fitness across the genome of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a major cause of difficult-to-treat infections. This approach identified essential functions particularly vulnerable to partial depletion and mapped how gene repression alters aminoglycoside susceptibility. Repressing selected genes impaired growth and disproportionately increased killing by tobramycin. These tools and datasets provide a resource for prioritizing candidate antibacterial targets and investigating whether partial inhibition of essential functions can enhance the activity of existing antibiotics.

items.title_en: Gαq-mediated contact release is required for efficient mitochondrial quality control
items.abstract_en: Lysosomes and mitochondria are highly dynamic organelles whose coordinated interactions are essential for cellular homeostasis, while their dysfunction contributes to numerous human diseases. Here, we identify the mitochondrial outer membrane protein Fis1 and the RabGAPs TBC1D15 and TBC1D17 as novel interacting partners of the heterotrimeric G protein -subunit Gq. Using mitochondrial proteomics, co-immunoprecipitation, proximity ligation assays, and in vitro binding studies with purified proteins, we demonstrate that Gq forms a complex with Fis1 and TBC1D15/TBC1D17 through a non-canonical interaction interface. Gq localizes to mitochondria-lysosome contact sites, where it regulates the dynamic balance between contact formation and dissociation. Loss of Gq resulted in enlarged and clustered lysosomes and increased the extent and duration of mitochondria-lysosome contacts. Live-cell imaging revealed prolonged organelle tethering in Gq-deficient cells, while proximity ligation and three-dimensional reconstruction analyses localized Gq and TBC1D15 to mitochondrial tips closely associated with lysosomes. This localization, together with increased mitochondrial fission and altered mitophagic turnover following Gq loss, links the regulation of contacts at mitochondrial tips to mitochondrial fragmentation and quality control. Re-expression of Gq, but not the non-canonical interaction-deficient mutant, restored normal lysosomal morphology, contact-site dynamics, mitochondrial fragmentation, and mitophagy. Together, these findings identify a Gq as a dynamic regulator of mitochondria-lysosome untethering and connect contact site turnover with mitochondria fragmentation and mitophagy. Our work uncovers a novel link between G protein signaling, organelle communication, and mitochondrial quality control.

items.title_en: A generative network model reveals hierarchical structural memory guiding post-mitotic 3D genome inheritance
items.abstract_en: How three-dimensional (3D) genome organization is reestablished after mitosis to preserve gene regulatory programs and cell identity remains unresolved. We asked whether mitotic chromosome architecture contributes to cellular memory by preserving structural information while maintaining the flexibility required for cellular adaptation. Here we introduce HiCONA, a generative Bayesian framework that infers hierarchical genome organization and quantifies the structural contribution of individual interactions through an Entropy Impact Score. HiCONA resolves genome organization across multiple scales, revealing structure-defining interaction patterns underlying chromatin architecture, independently of experimental modality. We identify structurally impactful chromatin interactions retained during mitosis delineating distinct trajectories of post-mitotic genome reassembly. These mitotically preserved interactions are enriched for active, transcriptionally competent regulatory elements, consistent with a cis-encoded architectural memory subsequently remodeled by trans-acting regulators. Together, our findings suggest that molecular information retained on mitotic chromosomes guides structural trajectories, providing an architectural basis for epigenetic memory and post-mitotic genome inheritance.

items.title_en: FoXSight: Facilitating Computational Hit Identification in Crystallographic Fragment Screening Experiments
items.abstract_en: X-ray crystallographic fragment screening reveals how small molecules bind to proteins, providing important starting points for drug design. Identifying these weak binding events remains difficult when electron density signals are noisy, partially occupied or obscured by solvent, and campaigns may comprise thousands of datasets. Here, we present FoXSight, a computational method for hit identification in crystallographic compound screening. FoXSight applies Difference-of-Gaussian (DoG) filtering to multi-reference subtraction maps to detect recurring, target-specific density features associated with bound ligands. Its output maps remain visually interpretable and support subsequent ligand modeling. We evaluated FoXSight on in-house and public datasets spanning seven protein targets, comparing its maps with PanDDA where suitable comparison data were available. FoXSight was successfully used as the primary hit identification tool in a challenging crystallographic fragment screening campaign for human Cathepsin L, where the output of established methods was impractical to inspect systematically.

items.title_en: AdaGeneBudget: Cell-Adaptive Gene-Token Allocation for Efficient Single-Cell Foundation Models
items.title_zh: AdaGeneBudget：用于高效单细胞基础模型的细胞自适应基因令牌分配
items.abstract_en: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) represent each cell using sequences of gene-associated tokens, making embedding extraction increasingly costly as the number of cells and expressed genes grows. Existing input policies typically rely on fixed input budgets, with retained genes determined by random subsampling, model-native ranking, or a dataset-level highly variable gene (HVG) panel. However, they do not jointly determine, for each cell, which genes to retain and how many tokens to allocate. We introduce AdaGeneBudget, a training-free gene-token selection method that combines each gene's expression with reference-derived inverse detection frequency and retains the shortest ranked prefix that captures a target fraction of the cell's expression-specificity score mass. The resulting cell-specific budget is bounded by minimum and maximum lengths, requires no cell-type labels, and leaves the pretrained backbone unchanged. We evaluated AdaGeneBudget in a frozen-backbone inference setting using pretrained scGPT and Geneformer models on Kang and PBMC reference-mapping tasks, with an additional scPRINT comparison against its official HVG policy and an expressed-only HVG control. Across four scGPT and Geneformer backbone-dataset pairs, AdaGeneBudget substantially reduced mean gene-token counts and peak GPU memory while increasing embedding-extraction throughput by up to 4.63x. Despite this compression, it preserved native-level aggregate annotation utility and numerically outperformed token-matched random and Top-Expression baselines. AdaGeneBudget also preserved fine-grained and low-support cell identities and retained lineage-marker programs and stimulation-associated pathway genes under compression. In scPRINT, both HVG controls achieved higher annotation macro-F1, whereas AdaGeneBudget more faithfully preserved the stimulation-induced embedding direction. These results establish biologically informed, cell-adaptive gene-token allocation as a practical complement to architectural and systems-level efficiency methods for applying existing scFMs to new datasets. They also suggest that cell-adaptive input allocation may be a useful design principle for future models operating under finite token budgets.

items.title_en: MERIT: Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care
items.abstract_en: Background: Dementia is frequently underdiagnosed in primary care, with fewer than half of cases identified and only 8-20% detected at early stages. Our objective is to develop an Agentic AI-powered clinical decision support systems (CDSS) maintaining the patient's virtual cognitive status and provide physicians with ready-to-use summaries and next step suggestions. Methods: We developed MERIT (Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care) via participatory co-design with primary care provider. It maintains a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's electronic health records (EHR) and conversation with the patient and provide clinical decision support based on it. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) was employed by the system to retrieve dementia-related risk factors from multimodal EHR. Additionally, we used reflection Agentic AI design pattern to improve quality of AI Agent generated text. We used one PCP's patient data to optimize the system, then used patients from another four PCPs for testing. We mainly used expert manual evaluation based on 5-point Likert-Scales. For readability of patient summary and personalized education material, besides manual evaluation, we also employed widely used Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch We-Kincaid Grade Level. Results: MERIT has four modulars: 1) patient conversation agent; 2) patient virtual cognitive status maintainer; 3) personalized education provider; and 4) decision support provider. Our evaluation focused on the provider-facing part, which relies on EHR without involving any patient conversation. The evaluation on the testing data demonstrates good performance. On a 5-point Likert scale, in the test set, patient virtual cognitive status summaries received average scores of 4.0 (SD 0.74) for correctness, 4.2 (SD 0.59) for completeness, 4.3 (SD 0.59) for readability, and 4.1 (SD 0.71) for clinical usefulness; clinical decision support received 3.9 (SD 0.87) for correctness, 4.3 (SD 0.66) for completeness, and 4.3 (SD 0.64) for adoptability; and the personalized education material received average ratings of 4.3 (SD 0.62) for completeness, 4.5 (SD 0.60) for readability, 4.3 (SD 0.78) for usefulness, and 4.4 (SD 0.49) for empathy. Automated readability assessment showed that patient summaries had a mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 18.3 (SD 4.9) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 13.7 (SD 0.7), consistent with college-level text, whereas personalized patient education had a Flesch Reading Ease score of 50.1 (SD 7.1) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 11.7 (SD 1.5), which is high-school student understandable text. Conclusion: Our developed system MERIT can maintain a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's multimodal EHR, provide the patient with clear and readable personalized education materials, and provide the PCP with ready-to-use cognitive summaries and decision support with high adoptability. By integrating our CDSS into Epic in the near future, our developed system will largely benefit older adults with cognitive decline and slow down the progression.

items.title_en: Validation of CSF αSyn-SAA in an autopsy cohort with whole-body assessment of Lewy pathology
items.abstract_en: Background & Objectives: As recently recommended by neuropathologists, we assessed the diagnostic accuracy of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) alpha-synuclein (-syn) seed amplification assay (SAA) in an autopsy cohort with systemic assessment of Lewy pathology. Methods: CSF was obtained antemortem and stored at -80 . -syn SAA and systemic Lewy pathology assessment were conducted as previously reported. Kinetic parameters, including maximum fluorescence (Fmax) and time to reach 50% of Fmax (T50), were also evaluated. Results: CSF samples were available from 30 patients (8 with symptomatic Lewy body disease [LBD], 2 with multiple system atrophy [MSA], 3 with Alzheimer's disease [AD], and 17 disease controls). Despite different clinical stages, all patients with LBD had diffuse neocortical or limbic-stage pathology at autopsy, with widespread peripheral Lewy bodies, including in the esophagus, heart, and sympathetic ganglia. Lewy pathology was not observed in disease controls. SAA was positive in all 8 with LBD, low positive in one patient with AD, and negative in all others. Fmax was significantly higher in LBD compared with cases without -syn pathology (9091{+/-}2083 vs. 1659{+/-}113 relative fluorescence units). The low-positive case had a lower positivity rate (25% vs. 75-100%), lower Fmax, and longer T50 than LBD cases. Conclusions: In this pilot study, CSF -syn SAA demonstrated high specificity (95%) and high sensitivity (100%) for detecting LBD; however, all LBD cases had widespread pathology, including peripheral involvement. Larger studies are needed to understand the association between CSF -syn SAA and Lewy pathology in the body.

items.title_en: Challenges in Quantifying Upper Extremity Dysmetria in the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA)
items.abstract_en: Background Assessments of upper extremity control in ataxia are susceptible to measurement error and inherent variability. Objectives Quantify trial-to-trial variability in the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) nose-to-finger (NTF) and finger chase (FC) tasks, and test agreement between scores derived from live assessment and retrospective video review. Methods 17 patients with cerebellar ataxia were video-recorded performing tasks behind a transparent, calibrated 1-cm grid. NTF tremor amplitude and FC undershoot/overshoot distance derived from live scores were compared with measurements from video review. Results NTF tremor amplitude and FC under/overshoot varied between consecutive trials. Patients received 2.4 {+/-} 0.7 (NTF) and 2.6 {+/-} 0.8 (FC) different SARA scores for limb excursions within one session. Live and video score match was NTF: 64.7% left, 70.6% right; FC: 64.7% left, 41.2% right. Live scoring often overestimated impairment. Conclusions Trial-to-trial variability and live/video discordance limit the precision of SARA upper-limb tasks.

items.title_en: Sex shapes plasma molecular signatures of dementia risk across APOE ε4 strata
items.abstract_en: Sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 influence dementia risk, but whether its molecular predictors differ across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata remains unclear. We investigated plasma proteomic and metabolomic signatures predicting future dementia in 43,759 UK Biobank participants across four sex-by-APOE {varepsilon}4 groups. The association between APOE {varepsilon}4 carrier status and dementia differed by sex (interaction p = 0.027). Machine-learning models achieved higher discrimination in APOE {varepsilon}4 carriers (AUC 0.85-0.90) than non-carriers (AUC 0.74-0.76), with the highest performance in female carriers. Most top molecular predictors were subgroup-specific, including C7, CDON and EDIL3 in female carriers and KLK4, MMP12 and TGFBI in male carriers. When UK Biobank models were applied to the Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium, 12/17 available top predictors in female carriers and 10/16 in male carriers remained highly ranked. These findings identify distinct molecular signatures of dementia risk across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata, supporting stratified biomarker discovery.

items.title_en: Prebiotic Inulin for Late-Reproductive Individuals (P.I.L.I. study): A Protocol for a Placebo-Blind, Cross-Over Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract_en: Background: Perimenopause is a transitional stage preceding menopause, characterized by hormonal fluctuations and physiological changes that may increase cardiometabolic risk. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiome may influence these changes through estrogen metabolism and microbial metabolite production.
