Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior sum rate performance under QoS constraints, while significantly improving computational efficiency compared with conventional numerical optimization approaches.

items.title_en: TinyML Hits the Memory Wall: A Benchmark of Ten Sub-Watt Edge Devices
items.title_zh: TinyML 遭遇内存墙：十款亚瓦级边缘设备的基准测试
items.abstract_en: Neural network inference at the edge must fit tight energy budgets. Existing benchmarks compare few devices, do not report energy on a common basis, and omit the newest microcontrollers with an NPU or the 1 GHz Cortex-M85. Hardware-aware design also ranks networks by MAC count, yet no study has tested whether this proxy holds across accelerators. We benchmark sub-watt edge AI hardware by evaluating four CNNs (MobileNetV3, MCUNetV1, EfficientNet, SqueezeNet) and two tiny transformers (MobileViT-XXS, DeiT-tiny) on ten commercial devices: an in-sensor DSP (Sony IMX500), four MCUs with an NPU (STM32N6, Alif Ensemble E7/E8, GreenWaves GAP9), and five MCUs without an NPU (STM32U5, Apollo510B, ESP32-S3 Xtensa LX7, RA8M2, STM32V8). Four devices are novel (Alif E8, Apollo510B, RA8M2, STM32V8). Measured as energy above idle, the IMX500 (0.13-0.35 mJ) uses 1.3-3x less energy than the STM32N6 (0.31-1.05 mJ) on every model; the GAP9 uses the least on MobileNetV3 and the Alif E7 the least on MCUNetV1 and SqueezeNet. All four use 6-34x less energy than the STM32V8 (1.85-3.98 mJ), and the Alif E7 and IMX500 form the power-performance Pareto front. Latency on all four accelerators scales with memory traffic (bytes of weights and activations, r >= 0.98) and not with MACs, so they are memory-bound, while no MCU without an NPU is. The NPU advantage grows with intensity from 1.4x over a 1 GHz Cortex-M85 on MCUNetV1 to 8.2x on SqueezeNet. MAC count is therefore a misleading cost proxy for sub-watt accelerators.

items.title_en: A Geometry-Informed Neural Operator surrogate of LISFLOOD-FP for rapid pluvial-fluvial flood forecasting: the case of Forlì, Italy
items.abstract_en: Physically based two-dimensional hydraulic models are too slow for real-time inundation forecasting and large ensembles. We present a time-dependent geometry-informed neural operator (GINO) surrogate of LISFLOOD-FP for the municipality of Forlì (Italy), severely affected by the May 2023 Emilia-Romagna floods. The surrogate is designed for an operational setting in which only river stage gauges and rain gauges are available. A reproducible pipeline turns public regional observations into a physically based training set: each river inflow is driven by the first stage gauge downstream of it through a calibrated water-surface boundary condition, and rain enters as SCS-CN effective rainfall. The surrogate is an autoregressive GINO trained on 216 simulations of 24 observed events with scaled forcing. It predicts volume-conserving polygon-mean depths on an exposure-based Voronoi mesh of 659 nodes, with a 20 min step over 72 h. The surrogate is tested on 38 independent observed events that it never saw during training. On these events it reaches a critical success index (CSI) of 0.934 at 0.05m and 0.844 at 0.3 m, a depth RMSE of 0.008m and an $R^2$ of 0.984 for maximum-depth maps. On one NVIDIA A10G GPU a 72-h forecast takes 1.7 s instead of 55 s with LISFLOOD-FP, and a 50-member ensemble, computed in a single batched rollout, takes 6.2 s instead of about 46 min, which makes probabilistic flood forecasting practical. These results show that neural-operator surrogates can deliver accurate pluvial-fluvial flood forecasts driven by river stage for operational early warning.

items.title_en: Characterizing When Language Models Take Harmful Actions to Protect Their Assigned Goals
items.abstract_en: Recent language model (LM) safety failures have largely been studied as disparate phenomena. In agentic misalignment, a model blackmails an executive to avoid being replaced. In alignment faking, it complies with harmful requests during training to keep its values from being modified. We argue that these behaviours share a common decision structure: a model assigned a goal must either take a harmful action to preserve it or refuse and lose it. We formalize this as a goal-harm conflict and present the same conflict under various elicitation protocols that range from compact forced-choice prompts to simulated agentic environments. These protocols span two perspectives on LM decision-making, which we term (i) the logit view, reading preferences from answer-token probabilities, and (ii) the sampling view, classifying open-ended responses with an LM judge. Under the logit view, we show that goal importance and harm severity additively shape how a model resolves these value conflicts. Under the sampling view, we derive two factorizations of the harmful-action probability that safety evaluations commonly report. The first measures how well a preference read from answer tokens carries over into behaviour, such as making a harmful tool call. The second attributes a low harmful-action rate either to refusal or to responses that reach no resolution. We then show how fictional context changes a model's preference under the logit view, and how tool use and partial observability -- two features of agentic evaluations -- change its harmful-action rate under the sampling view. Our work offers a descriptive framework for studying how LMs resolve such value conflicts and for estimating low-probability harmful actions at a finer granularity than the aggregate harm rates commonly reported in safety evaluations.

items.title_en: Multidimensional Suicide Risk Assessment with Machine Learning using Electronic Health Records
items.abstract_en: Suicide prevention remains a critical public health challenge, and electronic health records (EHRs) provide an opportunity to characterize suicide-related risk indicators using documented clinical, behavioral, medical, and social-contextual information. This paper presents a multidimensional machine learning framework to model and estimate suicide-related outcomes using MIMIC-IV EHR data. We construct clinically motivated diagnosis categories and define a composite outcome from documented codes corresponding to suicidal ideation, suicide attempt, prior suicidal behavior, and intentional self-harm. To address severe class imbalance and reduce age-related confounding, we apply age-matched resampling that retains all positive patients and samples comparison-cohort patients from the same age group. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost classifiers are evaluated before and after resampling with isotonic calibration. The calibrated XGBoost model achieves the strongest matched-cohort performance, outperforming the other evaluated classifiers. SHAP-based interpretation shows that diagnostic burden, depression-related features, age, personality-disorder history, social determinants related to violence, and medical comorbidity contribute to elevated predicted probabilities. Our results demonstrate that combining broad EHR-derived features, age-matched cohort construction, calibration, and feature-level interpretation provides a practical framework for retrospective suicide-related risk modeling.

items.title_en: Neural Actor--Critic Learning with Minimax Critics and Reflected Langevin Sampling
items.abstract_en: Actor--critic methods rely on critic gradients to improve continuous-action policies, yet finite-sample guarantees must control both value and gradient errors and their propagation through the actor. We develop a neural actor-critic procedure that combines a regularized minimax Bellman estimator over sigmoid networks with a finite reflected Langevin sampler driven by the fitted critic gradient. Under uniform Bellman regularity and covered reset sampling, a positive high-order action-derivative penalty yields value and action-gradient risk bounds with classical nonparametric minimax exponents up to logarithmic factors. We propagate estimation, mixing, discretization, temperature, and policy-iteration errors to obtain return guarantees, with refinements for bounded multimodal potentials and strongly concave regimes. Empirical studies across controlled simulations, logged continuous-control data, and a simulated decision task show favorable performance relative to the considered baselines.

items.title_en: Certifying Graph Neural Networks Against Label and Structure Poisoning
items.abstract_en: Robust machine learning for graph-structured data has made significant progress against test-time attacks, yet certified robustness to poisoning - where adversaries manipulate the training data - remains largely underexplored. For image data, state-of-the-art poisoning certificates rely on partitioning-and-aggregation schemes. However, we show that these methods fail when applied in the graph domain due to the inherent label and structure sparsity found in common graph datasets, making effective graph-partitioning difficult. To address this challenge, we propose a novel semi-supervised learning framework called deep Self-Training Graph Partition Aggregation (ST-GPA), which enriches each graph partition with informative pseudo-labels and synthetic edges, enabling effective certification against node-label and graph-structure poisoning under sparse conditions. Our method is architecture-agnostic, scales to large numbers of partitions, and consistently and significantly improves robustness guarantees against both label and structure poisoning across multiple benchmarks, while maintaining strong clean accuracy. Overall, our results establish a promising direction for certifiably robust learning on graph-structured data against poisoning under sparse conditions.

items.title_en: NormMoX: A Normative Mixture of Experts for Explainable Autism Classification from Structural and Functional MRI
items.title_zh: NormMoX：一种用于从结构和功能 MRI 进行可解释自闭症分类的规范性专家混合模型
items.abstract_en: While structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI, fMRI) offer profound potential for researching autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and understanding individual neurodivergence, current classifiers lack the explanatory power needed for scientific study, clinical use and personal-level insights. Most models learn from imaging features that also vary with age, sex, scanner site and head motion. They fuse the two modalities without a common reference and explain decisions against arbitrary reference inputs rather than a typical brain. We present NormMoX, a normative mixture of experts that makes the typical brain the shared reference for prediction, fusion and explanation. Normative models trained on large healthy cohorts give the value each brain measure is expected to take for a person's age and sex. NormMoX learns from each person's deviations from these expected values. For each modality, a neural network expert turns the deviations into a score of evidence for ASD. A fusion head, MoX, compares each score with those of typical controls before combining them. It therefore needs no imputation when a modality is missing and shows in which modality each person is atypical. On 1,035 participants of ABIDE I, NormMoX reached an AUROC of $0.728 \pm 0.004$ in repeated cross-validation, above linear, single-modality and deep fusion baselines. NormMoX thus shows not only whether a person is likely to have ASD, but where, and in which modality, their brain departs from typical. The implementation is available at https://github.com/Novelex/NormMox.

items.title_en: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
items.abstract_en: Generative AI is billed per token, yet tokens are not equally expensive. Each token enters the KV-cache and raises the cost of those that follow, so energy grows non-linearly along a sequence whose tokens look identical. No analytical model states what a token costs, and the most accurate SOTA model is a fit, not a law: it absorbs architecture into fitted coefficients, requiring per-LLM fitting. We derive closed-form expressions of the computational and memory-access complexity of LLM inference in terms of architectural hyperparameters, covering MHA and GQA, and compare a family of analytical models of increasing granularity. From these, we obtain the SIMPLE Inference Model to Predict LLMs Energy (SIMPLE), a four-parameter law that separates prefill from decode, and decode into KV-cache cost and next-token computation. Over traces of 13 dense LLMs from six families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it attains R2 = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE, 3.1-3.5x below the SOTA, without per-LLM calibration. The SIMPLE law explains as well as predicts: prefill energy grows quadratically with the hidden dimension, so larger LLMs suffer most from long inputs; and more aggressive GQA KV grouping reduces the per-token energy by up to 3x relative to standard MHA. Increasing the reasoning token budget pushes output length beyond the analytically derived energy minimum, driving super-linear energy growth; although accuracy grows with the budget, energy grows faster, so Intelligence per Joule peaks at an intermediate budget and falls by up to 3.14x across a 4.0x reasoning-budget range. Agentic serving raises energy per request by 13.0x relative to non-agentic ones, driven by the growth of both the prefill and the KV-cache terms with input length; while prefix caching removes most of the prefill cost (-93%), the KV-cache term is unaffected, so even a cached agentic request costs 4.8x more.

items.title_en: End-to-End NTT on FPGA for FHE Acceleration
items.title_zh: 面向 FHE 加速的 FPGA 端到端 NTT
items.abstract_en: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data without decryption. Despite its strong security guarantees, FHE incurs substantial computational and memory overhead. In FHE-based deep learning inference, on average 63% of the CPU time is spent on the number theoretic transform (NTT) and its inverse (INTT), which reduce the complexity of polynomial multiplication from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N \log N)$. Prior FPGA works follow two approaches: accelerating entire FHE schemes, which yields significant speedups but ties them to specific parameters and algorithms, or accelerating only the NTT, which applies across schemes, algorithms, and libraries. Most FPGA NTT designs require interconnects that grow with parallelism and utilize significant resources, which complicates routing on multi-die FPGAs. Additionally, to the best of our knowledge, end-to-end NTT acceleration within an FHE context has so far been left unexplored. We design a fully unrolled, delay-commutator streaming NTT/INTT kernel, and floorplan it across the three dies of an AMD Alveo V80. At 400 MHz, the kernel transforms a polynomial of $2^{16}$ coefficients every 5.12 $μ$s, the highest throughput among FPGA designs at this size. Offloaded end to end, it is up to 22x faster than the CPU per transform. We integrate the kernel into the Lattigo FHE library and evaluate it end to end. With 128-bit secure parameters, it accelerates core FHE operations, such as key switching and bootstrapping, by 1.8-2.2x, and neural network inference by 1.8-2.1x.

items.title_en: LLMs Depend on Specialist Tools for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in MS/MS Structural Elucidation
items.abstract_en: A frontier language model was recently reported to solve 1D NMR structural elucidation without tools. We ask whether this capability transfers to tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) in the de novo setting, where the model must propose a structure directly from the spectrum without a candidate list or reference library. To separate reasoning from recall, we build a 100-analyte benchmark from MassSpecGym, split by each analyte's textual footprint into in-distribution (well documented in literature) and out-of-distribution (essentially undocumented) arms. We hold the model, harness, and output format fixed and vary only the LLM's access to domain-specific tools. Without tools, a frontier LLM reaches 52% Top-1 accuracy in-distribution but only 2% out-of-distribution. Only access to de novo structure generators improves out-of-distribution accuracy, raising it to as much as 38% Top-1, and the resulting agent outperforms the standalone de novo models both in and out of distribution. These results suggest that LLMs are not effective at de novo MS/MS structural elucidation on their own, and that further gains depend on the specialist tools available to the agent rather than on the LLM itself.
authors: Devesh Shah Antonio H. de O. Fonseca

items.title_en: Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Deterministic and Randomized Sample Complexity
items.abstract_en: Calibrated multiaccuracy asks that a predictor be globally calibrated and multiaccurate with respect to a bounded test family $G$; that is, its residuals should be uncorrelated with every test $g(x)\in G$. This weakening of multicalibration suffices for many applications. Its sample complexity was not known to improve on that of full multicalibration, which is $\widetildeΘ\left(\frac{\log|G|}{\varepsilon^2} + \frac{1}{\varepsilon^{3}}\right)$ when $|G|$ is at least a sufficiently large power of $\log(1/\varepsilon)$. We resolve the sample complexity of $\varepsilon$-calibrated multiaccuracy, showing that it scales as $$ \widetildeΘ\left(\frac{\log|G|}{\varepsilon^2} + \frac{1}{\varepsilon^{5/2}}\right), $$ separating it from the complexity of multicalibration. The upper bound is obtained by an algorithm that outputs a randomized predictor. For deterministic predictors, we establish the tight rate $$ \widetildeΘ\left( \frac{\log|G|}{\varepsilon^2} + \frac{(\log|G|)^{1/3}}{\varepsilon^{8/3}} \right) $$ whenever $\log|G|=Ω(\log(1/\varepsilon))$. When $\log|G|\le\varepsilon^{-1+κ}$ for any fixed $κ\in(0,1)$, this rate is polynomially larger than the rate for randomized predictors. Thus, unlike for multicalibration, calibrated multiaccuracy exhibits a genuine sample-complexity separation between deterministic and randomized predictors. The matching upper and lower bounds show that the unusual cube-root dependence on $\log|G|$ is intrinsic. At $\log|G|\asymp\varepsilon^{-1}$, the minimax rates for randomized and deterministic calibrated multiaccuracy both coincide with the minimax rate for multicalibration.

items.title_en: EventGPT: Next-Event Pretraining on Banking Customer Histories
items.abstract_en: A model pretrained to predict a customer's next event can estimate the probability of future events without training on their labels and provide a reusable representation for supervised downstream banking tasks. We pretrain EventGPT, a hierarchical causal transformer, by next-token maximum likelihood estimation on the public Multimodal Banking Dataset (MBD-mini: 100,224 clients, 38.8 million transactions and 66.3 million geolocation pings). Keeping one state per event, EventGPT trains in about two hours on one L4 GPU at windows up to 8,192 tokens. From its next-event distribution, with no labels, EventGPT scores five targets of the form "the client makes a transaction of a given kind for the first time next month" at ROC-AUC 0.79 to 0.92. Gradient boosting on 114 engineered features needs 10,000 to 300,000 labeled client-months to match it on four targets and stays below it on the fifth. For product prediction, frozen EventGPT embeddings score below the engineered features (mean ROC-AUC 0.787 against 0.808 over five test folds), and a rank-averaged ensemble of EventGPT, profile fields and token counts with the engineered features adds 0.014 to 0.017, of which 0.007 to 0.016 is EventGPT's own. The code and pretrained weights are released.

items.title_en: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
items.abstract_en: Open multi-agent systems, where only a subset of agents are controllable, are central to real-world domains such as smart grids, yet lack a principled foundation for reinforcement learning algorithm design. We study this setting through n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT), a recent framework for learning in open multi-agent environments. We propose an axiomatic framework that derives value function learning from the Shapley axioms (Efficiency, Symmetry and Linearity), treating them as structural constraints rather than heuristic design choices. This formulation builds on a novel NAHT decomposition, which characterises the fundamental difference between open and fully controllable multi-agent systems, and establishes a cooperative game-theoretic foundation for learning. We further show that enforcing these axioms on learning individual value functions recovers the Shapley value for Dec-POMDPs, providing a principled bridge between reinforcement learning and classical cooperative game theory. Building on this framework, we introduce Shapley Machines and Banzhaf Machines, two generic algorithmic templates that can be instantiated with standard reinforcement learning methods. When applied to strong base algorithms such as IPPO and POAM, our methods consistently improve learning efficiency and generalisation to unseen agent types and conventions across NAHT benchmark tasks. The code of experiments is published on https://github.com/hsvgbkhgbv/axiomatic-rl-naht.

items.title_en: Inferring Transferable Rewards via Active Inverse Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract_en: Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) aims to recover expert rewards that transfer across environments with differing dynamics. Prior work has shown that such transfer is possible when gathering expert demonstrations across sufficiently different dynamics. In practice, however, expert demonstrations are costly, making it critical to select the right dynamics to reduce the quantity of expert data required for learning transferable rewards. We propose a two-phase approach: we first cycle through the available dynamics to obtain a reliable reward estimate, then actively select dynamics to reduce our uncertainty about the expert reward. Crucially, this yields novel sample complexity guarantees on transfer that hold for any dynamics, with a rate independent of the number of available dynamics. Empirically, our method significantly reduces the number of expert demonstrations needed to learn a transferable reward.

items.title_en: ENGINE: Endogenous Variational MultiScale Optimization for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
items.abstract_en: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization enables memory-efficient large language model (LLM) fine-tuning, and recent methods incorporate curvature-aware strategies. However, in the high-dimensional parameter space of LLMs, these methods inherently suffer from exploding gradient variance and prohibitive costs. Conversely, confining updates to a low-dimensional subspace reduces variance but discards critical high-dimensional information, degrading performance. This creates a fundamental dilemma: full-space optimization is informative but has high variance, while subspace optimization has low variance but loses information. To break this trade-off, we propose ENGINE (Endogenous Variational MultiScale). Inspired by computational mechanics, we adapt static Variational MultiScale (VMS) theory to dynamic optimization, treating low- and high-dimensional spaces as resolved coarse and unresolved fine scales. Through a multigrid-style V-cycle, ENGINE alternates between spaces, dynamically probing fine-grained information in the high-dimensional space and injecting it to correct the efficient low-dimensional sampling process. Under appropriate assumptions, statistical analysis characterizes variance reduction and correction of curvature-induced bias, and convergence analysis establishes a stationarity bound for the corrected coarse updates. Evaluations on standard LLM benchmarks show that ENGINE achieves higher accuracy and faster convergence than existing ZO methods, achieving up to a $2.61\times$ speed-up in forward passes with zero additional peak memory overhead. Code is available at https://github.com/AI4Science-WestlakeU/ENGINE.

items.title_en: Strictly proper scoring rules for node selection tasks on graphs
items.abstract_en: In node selection tasks, the goal is to identify a single unknown target node in a graph. We consider probabilistic supervised node selection, where the estimator outputs a probability distribution over the nodes of the graph and the ground-truth node is available for evaluation. Classical evaluation metrics for such tasks are either statistically ill-conceived or blind to the graph structure. To fill this gap, we introduce two strictly proper scoring rules that are explicitly graph-aware: the Resistance score, which is parameter-free, and the Diffusion score, which operates at an adjustable coarse-graining resolution. We show that the Diffusion score interpolates between the multi-category Brier score and a cluster-level weighted Brier score. The Resistance score generalises two classical scoring rules: the multi-category Brier score and the Ranked probability score. Applied to rooted trees, it also serves as the strictly proper version of the improper Hierarchical error distance used in hierarchical classification. In the same setting, we furthermore establish strict propriety of the Hierarchical cross-entropy family, a recently introduced separate class of hierarchy-aware scoring rules. Experiments on epidemic source detection and on ImageNet classification confirm that the proposed scores detect meaningful differences in estimation quality that classical metrics miss.

items.title_en: A Human-Verified AI Workflow for Annotating Environmental Sound Data
items.abstract_en: Large-scale annotation of environmental sound recordings presents significant challenges under time and resource constraints, particularly when sound categories are imbalanced and only part of a dataset has been labeled. This paper describes the development and evaluation of a human-AI workflow used during annotation of the Kenya Forest Sounds Dataset (KFSD), using a project-stage working collection of 7,531 audio recordings across 21 categories. We investigated zero-shot classification, a feature-based ensemble, and a fine-tuned Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST). The fine-tuned AST achieved 89.36% accuracy, 85.98% precision, 89.24% recall, and 87.58% F1 on held-out test data for binary classification of Person talking. Because this result remained below the predefined 95% threshold for autonomous annotation, model predictions were used as suggestions and subjected to human verification. Of the 5,026 initially unlabeled recordings, 2,337 were routed to a speech-verification queue and 2,689 remained for ordinary manual annotation. The verifier reviewed all 2,337 machine-labeled files and detected zero false positives, yielding 100% verification accuracy. The observed average verification time was approximately 4.2 seconds per file. At an average rate of 35 seconds per file for manual annotation, the hybrid workflow reduced work on the remaining queue from approximately 48.9 to 28.9 person-hours, saving about 20.0 hours (41%). The study documents the model-selection process, provenance-aware file organization, verification procedure, observed errors, practical limitations, and opportunities for extending AI assistance beyond one category.

items.title_en: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract_en: Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) is a fundamental inverse problem in geophysics to estimate subsurface properties, such as velocity, from seismic measurements. Recently, self-supervised learning methods remove the need for ground-truth velocity maps during training by leveraging a forward operator to simulate seismic data from predictions and backpropagate the gradients of reconstruction loss through it. In this work, we consider a more challenging setting without accessing such gradients. To this end, we incorporate reinforcement learning into self-supervised FWI and propose a framework named DeepWaveRL. Specifically, we reformulate FWI as a policy learning problem, where the policy network predicts velocity maps as actions, and a forward operator is used solely for simulation. A global scalar reward is computed based on data misfit for each prediction and used to weight policy gradients. Thus, learning proceeds without accessing the gradients from the forward operator. Given the indirect and coarse supervision signals, we further identify key strategies to stabilize learning and mitigate the spatial credit assignment bottleneck. Experimental results show that, despite relying entirely on a single scalar reward, DeepWaveRL achieves competitive performance compared to supervised and self-supervised baselines. These findings suggest that our framework offers a flexible and complementary learning paradigm for the FWI research community.

items.title_en: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
items.title_zh: PaddleMaterials：面向材料科学的端到端深度学习工具包
items.abstract_en: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted code generation without changing model definitions. Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compiled execution accelerated every instance in eight groups, with group median speedups of 11%-224% and group maximum speedups of 11%-336%. Case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene link structure generation or spectrum elucidation, interatomic-potential relaxation, property prediction and electron-density prediction, using same-geometry density functional theory (DFT) calculations as references. For LiMnO2, predicted formation energies for generated and relaxed structures differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV per atom, while the computational cost of model steps was less than one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation. PaddleMaterials extends unified materials workflows beyond conventional property, potential and structure-generation tasks while supporting verifiable cross-task operations and compiled execution.

items.title_en: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
items.title_zh: CoworkOS：面向真实世界自动化的协作智能体规模化扩展
items.abstract_en: Rapid advances in cowork agents are shifting human-AI collaboration toward real-world automation, delivering software, designs, and other artifacts. However, such productivity work demands both high-quality delivery on complex productivity tasks and continued monitoring and decision-making over long horizons, a combination that remains an open challenge. We introduce CoworkOS, a general-purpose harness for long-horizon work that separates task strategy from execution management: the model decides actions, delegation, and acceptance, while the runtime maintains state and feedback. Its three-layer architecture enables direct execution or delegation to Subagents, synchronously or asynchronously, under stable responsibilities. Through a shared application layer, humans and agents inspect and revise the same evolving documents, presentations, CAD models, and Blender scenes, so human-in-the-loop participation can enter both through conversation and through direct modification of the work itself. To sustain continuity across agents and sessions, CoworkOS further introduces hierarchical workspaces and persistent semantic memory, so working files, key decisions, and long-running Job logs remain shareable, reusable, and resumable after interruption. Across 12 benchmarks and 6 categories of real-world applications, CoworkOS proves highly competitive with frontier agent applications such as Codex and DeepSeek Harness. As a sustained-work case study, CoworkOS uses GLM-5.3 as its backbone to conduct RSI-driven automated post-training on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Over five rounds, the model's average score across eight benchmarks rose from 33.19 to 42.95 (+9.76). Looking ahead, we believe CoworkOS opens a meaningful path toward general cowork-agent intelligence.
items.abstract_zh: 协作智能体正把人机协作推向真实世界自动化，但生产性工作既要高质量完成复杂任务，又需在长周期中持续监控与决策。本文提出 CoworkOS——一个面向长周期工作的通用框架，将任务策略与执行管理分离：模型负责决定动作、委派与验收，运行时维护状态与反馈。其三层次架构支持直接执行，或同步/异步委派给 Subagent；共享应用层让人与智能体共同查看、修改同一份不断演化的文档、演示、CAD 模型与 Blender 场景；分层工作空间与持久语义记忆保证工作跨智能体、跨会话可共享、可复用、可续做。在 12 个基准、6 类真实应用中，CoworkOS 与 Codex、DeepSeek Harness 等前沿智能体应用相比极具竞争力；以 GLM-5.3 为骨干对 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 做五轮 RSI 驱动自动后训练，八个基准平均分从 33.19 升至 42.95（+9.76）。
items.highlight_zh: 分离策略与执行的长周期协作智能体框架，支持人机共编同一文件
items.digest_zh: 【研究了什么问题】现有“协作智能体”能替人写代码、做设计、出文档，但大多只擅长短任务。真实的生产性工作往往横跨数小时乃至数天，需要一边交付成果、一边持续监控和做决定。如何让智能体胜任这种长周期工作，仍是开放难题。【用了什么方法】作者构建 CoworkOS，核心思路是把“想干什么”（任务策略）与“怎么推进”（执行管理）拆开：模型只负责决策、委派与验收，运行时系统负责保存状态、汇总反馈。架构分三层，既能自己直接执行，也能把子任务派给 Subagent，同步或异步皆可。所有参与者共享同一个应用层，人类和智能体可以打开并修改同一份文档、演示幻灯片、CAD 模型或 Blender 场景，因此人既能“用对话介入”，也能“直接动手改作品”。为让工作不断线，系统还设计了分层工作空间与持久语义记忆，保存工作文件、关键决策与长任务日志，中断后可续做。【有什么结果】在 12 个基准、6 类真实应用场景中，CoworkOS 与 Codex、DeepSeek Harness 等前沿智能体应用表现相当乃至更具竞争力。在“长期持续工作”的案例中，它以 GLM-5.3 为骨干，对 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 自动做 RSI 式后训练，五轮之后八个基准平均分从 33.19 升到 42.95，提升 9.76 分。【为何重要】它重新设计了“人的参与方式”：不是让人盯着 AI，而是让人随时在同一件工作物上接手；并用持久记忆解决长任务“断片”问题。若此类系统成熟，AI 有望从单次任务工具变成能长期共事的“同事”。

items.title_en: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
items.title_zh: IdeaTaste：大模型是否拥有与人类研究者相同的科研品味？
items.abstract_en: Research taste, the judgment of what to read, which problems to pursue, and which methods to try, increasingly shapes the work of AI scientists, yet it remains far less understood than their ability to execute research. We introduce IdeaTaste, a benchmark that scores an LLM by how closely the research proposals it writes from a literature snapshot frozen at 2025 match the work the same communities published in 2026. Our experiments span six contemporary language models and four research areas from established to emerging fields, covering more than 90{,}000 proposals in total. LLM agents fall well short of human communities in both the literature they cite and the ideas they state, reaching about 26\% of the human level on citation matching and only 18\% on idea matching. Their populations can cite as diversely as a community and take up its tasks and methods, yet rarely arrive at the concrete approaches and research plans it pursues. Neither richer field context nor larger populations substantially close this gap. In blinded expert review, AI proposals trail the 2026 papers least in presentation and most in expected success, echoing their gap in concrete approaches, and those whose ideas no human paper shares fare worst, suggesting weaker directions rather than overlooked opportunities. These results indicate that the main bottleneck in AI research taste lies less in finding the directions a community works on than in turning them into the concrete approaches it goes on to pursue. We release IdeaTaste as an open, continuously updated leaderboard (https://cxcscmu.github.io/IdeaTaste) that benchmarks contemporary AI proposals against future publication cycles.
items.abstract_zh: 科研品味——决定读什么、追什么问题、试什么方法——日益塑造 AI 科学家的工作，但其受理解程度远不如执行能力。我们提出 IdeaTaste 基准：让 LLM 基于冻结在 2025 年的文献快照撰写研究提案，再以这些提案与同一社区 2026 年实际发表工作的吻合度打分。实验覆盖 6 个当代语言模型与 4 个研究领域（从成熟到新兴），共 9 万余份提案。LLM 智能体在引用文献与提出想法上均远逊于人类社区：引用匹配约为人类水平的 26%，想法匹配仅 18%。模型群体可以像社区一样广泛引用，也能采纳其任务与方法，却很少给出该社区真正采用的具体方案与研究计划；更丰富的领域上下文或更大规模群体都无法显著弥补差距。盲审显示，AI 提案在“表述”上差距最小、在“预期成功率”上差距最大，且其想法无任何人类论文共享的提案表现最差，说明方向更弱而非机会被忽视。可见 AI 科研品味的主要瓶颈不在发现方向，而在把方向转化为具体可推进的方案。
items.highlight_zh: LLM 提案与未来论文的想法匹配度仅达人类水平的 18%
items.digest_zh: 【研究了什么问题】AI 已能写研究提案、做实验，但“科研品味”——即判断该读什么、该做哪个问题、该试哪种方法——很少被检验。论文要问的是：大模型写出的研究想法，与人类学术社区真正会去做的工作有多接近？【用了什么方法】作者构建 IdeaTaste 基准，做法是把时间“冻结”：让模型只看 2025 年及以前的文献撰写提案，再把这些提案与同一社区 2026 年实际发表的论文比对，从引用匹配与想法匹配两个维度打分。实验覆盖 6 个当代大模型、4 个研究领域（从成熟到新兴），共 9 万多份提案，并辅以专家盲审。【有什么结果】差距非常明显：模型提案在“引用了哪些文献”上只达到人类水平的约 26%，在“提出了什么想法”上仅约 18%。值得注意的是，模型群体能达到与社区一样多样的引用分布，也能抓住社区关心的任务与方法，却很少收敛到社区真正采用的具体方案和技术路线；给更多领域上下文、或扩大模型群体规模，都补不上这个缺口。盲审中，AI 提案与 2026 年真实论文差距最小的是“写作表述”，差距最大的是“预期能成功”，与其缺乏具体方案相呼应；那些找不到任何人类论文共享想法的提案得分最差，说明它们是方向本身偏弱，而不是被埋没的好点子。【为何重要】结论指出，AI 科研品味的主要短板不在“选题方向”，而在“把方向变成可执行的具体方案”。这对 AI 科学家系统的设计有直接指导意义：与其喂更多背景知识，不如提升把模糊方向落实为技术路线的能力。作者还公开了一个持续更新的榜单，用未来论文不断检验当下的 AI 提案。

items.title_en: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
items.title_zh: ToolSpace：面向长程智能体的工具中心环境合成扩展
items.abstract_en: Large language models are deployed as long-horizon agents that compose diverse tools across MCP services into executable workflows. Existing MCP environment-scaling methods are data-centric: they first synthesize a database and scenario, then derive tools and tasks from them. As a result, tool interfaces may not match real ones, tool compositions are not grounded in execution, and tasks rarely span more than one environment. We propose ToolSpace, a tool-centric framework that reverses this order. ToolSpace mines data, state, and retry dependencies from adjacent calls in execution traces of real MCP services and open agent corpora, using deterministic rules rather than LLM judgment, and clusters the resulting weighted tool-composition graph into environments. Databases are synthesized only for state-mutating environments, while query and stateless tools replay recorded returns. ToolSpace then performs state-aware random walks with rollback and decompiles each chain into a natural-language task with assertion-based checks, keeping only samples that replay successfully from the initial state. Applied to AutomationBench and tau3-Bench Banking, the pipeline produces harder Pro versions on which 7 frontier models drop by up to 38.2 points. Across seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks, ToolSpace raises Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 23.0 to 41.0 average score (43.2 with RL) and GLM-5.2 from 44.6 to 56.6, on par with Claude Opus 5. Ablations show that execution-witnessed edges clearly outperform LLM-judged ones, and performance keeps improving with data and environment scale.
items.abstract_zh: 大语言模型正作为长程智能体被部署，将跨 MCP 服务的多样工具组合成可执行工作流。现有 MCP 环境扩展方法以数据为中心：先合成数据库与场景，再派生工具与任务，导致工具接口可能与真实不符、工具组合缺乏执行依据、任务很少跨越多于一个环境。我们提出 ToolSpace，一个反转该顺序的工具中心框架。它从真实 MCP 服务与公开智能体语料的执行轨迹中，用确定性规则（而非 LLM 判断）挖掘相邻调用间的数据、状态与重试依赖，并将加权工具组合图聚类为环境；仅对状态变更型环境合成数据库，查询与无状态工具则回放记录返回值。随后进行带回滚的状态感知随机游走，把每条链反编译为带断言检查的自然语言任务，只保留能从初始状态成功重放的样本。应用于 AutomationBench 与 tau3-Bench Banking，生成的更难 Pro 版本使 7 个前沿模型最高下降 38.2 分。在七个长程工具使用基准上，ToolSpace 将 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 平均分从 23.0 提升到 41.0（配合 RL 为 43.2），GLM-5.2 从 44.6 提升到 56.6，与 Claude Opus 5 相当。消融显示执行见证的边明显优于 LLM 判断的边，且性能随数据与环境规模持续提升。
items.highlight_zh: 从真实执行轨迹逆推工具环境，造出更难更真的智能体训练场
items.digest_zh:
1) 问题：大模型智能体要跨多个 MCP 服务调用工具完成长流程任务，训练它们需要大量真实、可执行、跨环境的工具环境。现有做法是“数据优先”：先造数据库和场景，再倒推工具和任务，结果工具接口不像真的、工具组合没有执行依据、任务基本只在一个环境里打转。
2) 方法：ToolSpace 把顺序反过来，以工具为中心。它从真实 MCP 服务和公开智能体语料的执行轨迹中，用确定性规则（不靠 LLM 主观判断）挖掘相邻调用之间的数据依赖、状态依赖与重试依赖，构建加权工具组合图并聚类成“环境”。只对会改状态的环境合成数据库，查询类和无状态工具直接回放记录下来的返回值。然后做带回滚的状态感知随机游走，把每条调用链“反编译”为自然语言任务，附上基于断言的检查，只保留能从初始状态成功重放的样本。
3) 结果：在 AutomationBench 和 tau3-Bench Banking 上生成的更难“Pro”版本，让 7 个前沿模型分数最多掉 38.2 分，说明确实更难更真实。用它造的数据训练，Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 平均分从 23.0 升到 41.0（加 RL 为 43.2），GLM-5.2 从 44.6 升到 56.6，与 Claude Opus 5 相当。消融表明“执行见证”的边明显优于 LLM 判断的边，且随数据与环境规模增大持续变好。
4) 意义：为长程工具使用智能体提供了一条可扩展、执行可验证的环境生产线，把训练环境的构建从“凭空编造”变成“从真实执行中反推”。

items.title_en: Avatar Intelligence: Amplifying Human Agency Through Persistent Personal Agents
items.title_zh: Avatar Intelligence：以持久个人智能体放大人的能动性
items.abstract_en: Personal AI agents are increasingly capable of handling long-horizon tasks across applications, yet users often need to invest substantial effort in specifying goals, resolving ambiguity, and verifying outcomes. We argue that progress should be measured by how effectively agents amplify human agency: enabling people to pursue their goals with less routine supervision while retaining control over consequential decisions. We advocate Avatar Intelligence, a paradigm of persistent personal agents that represent users' goals, values, and constraints through sustained decision delegation across contexts and time. We describe a maturity roadmap from human-directed execution to autonomous operation within delegated domains, and introduce the Agentic Oversight Index (AOI) as a framework for evaluating delivered value against agent-side operational cost and human oversight burden. We identify three core research challenges: identity-continuous personalization that carries user preferences across tasks, user-situated evolution through Rehearsal Engineering, and safety mechanisms that combine technical control with accountability and recourse. These directions define a research agenda for reliable decision delegation to personal agents across tasks and over time.
items.abstract_zh: 个人 AI 智能体已能跨应用处理长周期任务，但用户仍需投入大量精力去明确目标、澄清歧义并核验结果。我们认为，进展应以智能体在多大程度上放大人的能动性来衡量：让人减少例行监督，同时保留对重要决策的控制权。为此我们倡导 Avatar Intelligence（分身智能）——一种持久个人智能体范式，通过跨情境、跨时间的持续决策委派来表征用户的目标、价值观与约束。我们给出从“人指挥执行”到“在受委托领域内自主运行”的成熟度路线图，并提出 Agentic Oversight Index（AOI），用以权衡交付价值、智能体侧运行成本与人的监督负担。我们进而指出三项核心挑战：跨任务保持偏好一致的身份连续个人化、通过 Rehearsal Engineering 实现的用户情境化演化，以及结合技术控制与问责救济的安全机制。
items.highlight_zh: 提出以“放大人的能动性”衡量个人智能体，并给出 AOI 评估框架
items.digest_zh: 【研究了什么问题】个人 AI 智能体已能跨应用处理长任务，但用户往往要花大量精力去说清目标、澄清歧义、核对结果。论文主张，衡量智能体进步的真正标准应是“它多大程度上放大了人的能动性”——让人少做例行监督，同时保留对重要决策的控制权。【提出了什么】作者提出“Avatar Intelligence（分身智能）”范式：持久的个人智能体长期代表用户的目标、价值观与约束，在不同场景与时间中持续承担决策委派；并给出一条成熟度路线图，从“人指挥执行”逐步走向“在受委托的领域内自主运行”。换言之，评估重点不是智能体能做多少事，而是它能不能替人扛下例行的判断负担。【如何评估】论文提出 Agentic Oversight Index（AOI，智能体监督指数），把“交付的价值”与“智能体侧运行成本＋人的监督负担”放在一起权衡，而不是只看任务完成率。这一视角提醒：一个频繁需要人纠偏的智能体，即使完成任务，也未必真正减轻了人的负担。【三大研究挑战】一是身份连续的个人化，让用户偏好跨任务迁移而不走样；二是用户情境化的演化，作者称之为“Rehearsal Engineering（预演工程）”，让智能体在贴近用户的模拟情境中成长；三是安全机制，既要技术层面的控制，也要有责任归属与申诉救济渠道。【为何重要】这是一篇立场与议程型论文，价值在于把讨论焦点从“智能体能做多少任务”转向“人是否更省心且仍掌控关键决定”，并为个人智能体的评测与设计提供了可操作的坐标系（AOI）与明确的研究路线。

items.title_en: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
items.title_zh: 从自主智能体到认知共生体：迈向 AI 增强的人类智能
items.abstract_en: For a decade, progress in artificial intelligence has been measured by how much a machine can do on its own. Large foundation models now write code and run multistep tasks, and personal agents act on a person's behalf. Yet people still forget what they once knew, miss what they are not looking at, fail to find the right words, and face hard choices without the benefit of their own history, because the machine that could help stands outside the situation. As AI moves into the physical world, attention has settled on one kind of intelligent individual, the embodied robot; we argue that the era of Physical AI holds a second kind of equal importance, the person augmented by AI. Alongside artificial general intelligence, which asks how intelligent a machine can be, stands AI-augmented human intelligence (AHI), which asks how much intelligence a machine can enable in a particular person. Realizing it calls for a new kind of system, a cognitive symbiont: a lifelong, embedded, real-time, private, low-friction, and proactive companion that senses what the person senses through external devices, keeps their context across years, models their situation and their mind, takes part in their thinking at the right moment, carries out everyday tasks with their context, and keeps learning the person as both change. We give the paradigm a conceptual core, the cognitive gap between what a person could bring to a situation and what they can hold in working memory, and organize its design space as a symbiosis loop of sensing, keeping, understanding, living alongside, acting for and thinking with the person, and growing, enclosed by a personal runtime and by trust. Because a symbiont changes what a person can do in front of others, it also raises risks of a new kind, from covert assistance in examinations to pressure on everyone to adopt it, and we treat their governance as part of the paradigm.
items.abstract_zh: 十年来，AI 的进展常以机器独立完成多少任务来衡量：大模型能写代码、执行多步任务，个人智能体可代表用户行动。但人仍会遗忘旧知、错过视野之外的信息、想不起恰当的词，并在缺乏自身历史时面对抉择，因为本可帮忙的机器置身情境之外。随着 AI 进入物理世界，具身机器人备受关注；本文主张 Physical AI 时代还有同等重要的第二类——被 AI 增强的人。与追问“机器能多聪明”的通用人工智能并列，AI 增强人类智能（AHI）追问机器能为某个具体的人带来多少智能。实现它需要“认知共生体”：终身、嵌入、实时、私密、低摩擦且主动的伙伴，通过外部设备感知人所感知，跨年保存上下文，建模其处境与心智，在恰当时机参与思考、代为执行日常任务，并持续学习这个人。作者以“认知缺口”为概念内核，将设计空间组织为由个人运行时与信任包裹的共生循环。
items.highlight_zh: 提出 AI 增强人类智能（AHI）与认知共生体范式
items.digest_zh:
① 研究的问题：过去十年，AI 的进步基本用“机器能独立做多少事”来衡量——大模型会写代码、跑多步任务，个人智能体替人办事。但作者指出，人真正的短板往往发生在具体情境里：忘记自己学过的东西、看不见视野之外的信息、话到嘴边想不起词、做重大抉择时用不上自己的过往经验。根源在于机器始终站在情境之外。
② 提出的框架：作者主张 Physical AI 时代不只有“具身机器人”一类智能个体，还有同等重要的“被 AI 增强的人”。他们提出 AI 增强人类智能（AHI），与通用人工智能（AGI）并列：AGI 问机器能多聪明，AHI 问机器能让某个具体的人变多聪明。实现它需要一种新系统——认知共生体：终身陪伴、嵌入生活、实时响应、保护隐私、低摩擦、主动介入；通过外部设备感知人所感知，多年保存上下文，建模人的处境与心智，在恰当时机参与思考、代为执行日常任务，并随人一起成长。
③ 概念内核与设计空间：以“认知缺口”为核心——人本可带入情境的能力与工作记忆实际能保持的内容之间的落差；把设计空间组织成“共生循环”（感知、保存、理解、陪伴、代为行动、共同思考、成长），外层由个人运行时与信任机制包裹。
④ 为何重要：这类系统会改变一个人在他人面前能做什么，因此带来新型风险（如对他人隐蔽的协助等），也意味着 AI 的评测与伦理框架需要从“机器自主”转向“人机共同表现”。

items.title_en: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
items.title_zh: MDSKILL：通过多视角蒸馏学习内化技能记忆，实现高效动态智能体自我演化
items.abstract_en: Skill memories encode past experiences as textual prompts to improve reinforcement learning (RL) for self-evolving agents. Complementing RL, On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) provides dense, fine-grained supervision to internalize knowledge from skill-guided trajectories and accelerate policy learning. However, self-generated memories often contain noisy supervision and functionally entangled, redundant, or conflicting knowledge, making direct distillation difficult. Under limited training budgets, these issues can hinder knowledge internalization and even degrade performance. To address this problem, we propose MDSKILL, a multi-view distillation approach for skill memory internalization. MDSKILL organizes skill memories into three complementary functional views (state grounding, action planning, and execution control) and selects high-quality skills using dynamic metrics to construct view-specific and integrated reasoning branches. OPSD then transfers and consolidates complementary experiential knowledge across these branches into a shared policy, enabling efficient skill internalization and continuous agent self-evolution. We evaluate MDSKILL on three agent benchmarks against RL, skill-augmented, and self-distillation baselines that do not rely on stronger external teacher models. Without additional computational overhead, MDSKILL improves upon SOTA performance by up to 7.1% and 8.1% on ALFWorld and WebShop. Extensive ablations and evolution analyses further validate its effectiveness in knowledge internalization and policy improvement. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MDSKILL-CF53.
items.abstract_zh: 技能记忆把过往经验编码为文本提示，用以改进自演化智能体的强化学习（RL）。On-Policy Self-Distillation（OPSD）作为 RL 的补充，提供稠密细粒度监督，将技能引导轨迹中的知识内化并加速策略学习。但自生成的记忆常含噪声监督，且知识在功能上纠缠、冗余或冲突，直接蒸馏困难，在训练预算有限时甚至损害性能。为此提出 MDSKILL：把技能记忆组织为三个互补功能视角（状态接地、动作规划、执行控制），用动态指标筛选高质量技能，构建视角专属与整合推理分支；再由 OPSD 将各分支的互补经验知识迁移并巩固到共享策略中，实现高效技能内化与持续自我演化。在三个智能体基准上，不依赖更强外部教师模型、不增加额外计算开销，即在 ALFWorld 与 WebShop 上分别超过 SOTA 最多 7.1% 和 8.1%。
items.highlight_zh: 多视角蒸馏内化技能记忆，性能提升 7.1%/8.1%
items.digest_zh:
① 研究的问题：让智能体“越用越强”的一个常见做法是技能记忆——把过去的成功经验写成文本提示，下次遇到类似任务时放进上下文，配合强化学习提升表现。但光靠 RL 信号太稀疏。On-Policy Self-Distillation（OPSD）可以让模型把自己在技能提示引导下产生的轨迹当作监督，把知识“内化”进策略。问题在于：这些记忆是模型自己写的，噪声大、知识点互相纠缠甚至彼此冲突，直接蒸馏会把噪声也学进去；训练预算有限时，性能反而可能下降。
② 方法：MDSKILL 先给技能记忆“分门别类”，拆成三个互补功能视角——状态接地（当前处于什么局面）、动作规划（下一步该做什么）、执行控制（具体怎么执行）。再用动态指标挑出高质量技能，为每个视角构建专属推理分支，并加一个整合分支。随后用 OPSD 把这些分支里互补的经验知识迁移、汇总到一个共享策略中，相当于让多个“专业视角”共同教一个学生。
③ 结果：在三个智能体基准上，与 RL、技能增强、自蒸馏等基线（且不使用更强的外部教师模型）相比，MDSKILL 在 ALFWorld 提升最多 7.1%、WebShop 提升 8.1%，且不增加额外计算开销；消融实验和演化分析进一步验证了它在知识内化与策略改进上的作用。
④ 为何重要：它说明“经验”不能直接塞给模型，需要先清洗、分视角组织再蒸馏，才能让智能体在有限算力下持续自我进化。

items.title_en: Personas Are Not People: Identity as State, Not Attribute
items.title_zh: 人设不是人：身份是状态，而非属性
items.abstract_en: Synthetic populations, large sets of simulated people, are increasingly used in place of real people to pretest surveys, simulate users and communities, and evaluate AI systems. Each simulated person is defined by a persona, a written profile of fixed traits, demographics, and attitudes that a language model is instructed to act out. Every such system assumes that a person's identity is a stable attribute that behaves the same way in every situation the simulation presents. We show that this assumption is not a harmless simplification. Three decades of personality research find the opposite. How a given person behaves varies more across contexts than people vary from one another. Drawing on identity economics, which describes how different situations activate different identities and norms within the same person, we separate behavior into three parts, which are stable traits, the identity a context calls up, and the situation itself. We then prove, under two stated assumptions, that any simulation built on fixed personas, no matter how detailed the personas or how large the underlying model, cannot reproduce the part of a population's behavior that is specific to it and its circumstances. We propose a new evaluation criterion based on this result and a person-in-context design that can meet it in principle. We test one version on a naturalistic Reddit personality corpus and on a published clinical-trial recruitment survey of a community with documented distrust of medical institutions. The design does produce context-dependent behavior when tested directly, but in neither setting does it fully match the real population, and we show where it falls short. The consequence for practice is a risk that synthetic-population evaluations misrepresent the groups whose behavior is most shaped by context, a distortion that richer personas cannot correct.

items.title_en: Beyond Accuracy: What Language-Subspace Interventions Capture, Remove, and Improve
items.title_zh: 超越准确率：语言子空间干预捕获、移除并改进了什么
items.abstract_en: Language-subspace interventions aim to improve multilingual reasoning by suppressing language-related components in mid-layer activations. Using MATH and MGSM across four open-weight LLMs, we ask three questions: do estimated language subspaces capture translation-associated variation? Does projecting them out remove language information? And do they improve accuracy without compromising response language? For the first question, we build subspaces using the existing Mean-SVD construction and our DiffPCA. Both capture substantial translation-associated variation and show similar patterns across model depth. For the second, we project out each subspace and train linear probes to classify language from the projected activations. The probes still identify language almost perfectly, showing that neither subspace exhaustively captures language information. For the third, we evaluate several intervention configurations on Qwen2.5-7B, by varying subspace creation methods and intervention operators. We find that the intervention that most improves MGSM accuracy sacrifices response-language fidelity, with only one intervention improving joint accuracy--answers that are correct and in the target language--slightly, by 1.60 points. Interestingly, subtle changes in the prompt alone can reproduce the accuracy gains albeit with significant damage to language fidelity. We argue that causal interventions must be judged on more than accuracy, to fully account for language substitution trade-offs.

items.title_en: ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals
items.title_zh: ARLoop：具有注意力残差的完全开放预训练循环 Transformer
items.abstract_en: Looped transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared set of transformer layers, offering a parameter-efficient way to scale computation. However, standard residual connections aggregate information across recurrent depth into a single stream, providing limited control over which intermediate representations from preceding layers should be reused. In this paper, we introduce ARLoop, a looped transformer architecture based on attention residuals, where the input of each layer is selectively aggregated through attention over model depth. Distinct from standard transformers, we find that looped transformers do not require access to the full residual history: sliding-window depth attention matches or outperforms full-history attention at larger recurrent depths. Across controlled experiments with multiple parameter scales (140M and 370M) and recurrent depths (R = 1 to 5), ARLoop consistently outperforms prior residual designs for looped transformers. More importantly, we further scale ARLoop to 0.6B and 1.2B parameters under a realistic LLM pretraining recipe, demonstrating that the gains transfer to realistic pretraining, with particularly strong improvements on math and coding tasks. Our 1.2B model, pretrained on only 0.5T tokens with three recurrences, outperforms Huginn-3.5B (the only fully-open looped LLM as of our release date) across all evaluated tasks and is competitive with similar-sized non-looped models such as Qwen3.5-2B despite being trained on substantially less data.

items.title_en: When Self-Verification Hurts: Calibrated Answer Repair for Financial Question Answering
items.title_zh: 当自我验证有害时：面向金融问答的校准答案修复
items.abstract_en: Financial question answering can fail even when a model extracts a plausible number from the supplied evidence: the answer may attach it to the wrong entity, period, unit, or accounting concept. Asking the model to verify and revise its draft can help, but open-ended revision may alter content that was already correct or inspect the wrong relation and reinforce the original error. We formulate repair as a decision that balances the information it may recover against the correct content it may damage. Based on this trade-off, we introduce Calibrated Answer Repair (CAR), which first estimates whether a draft is likely to benefit from repair, then selects a targeted check, localizes the relevant evidence or draft span, and limits the permitted edit. Across FinRank, Fin-RATE, and FinQA with three open-weight models, CAR outperforms generic verification in all dataset-model settings. At the system level, it recovers 14.6% of initially missed answer requirements while damaging 2.1% of initially correct ones. Its post-draft token cost is over 30 percent lower than the iterative revision alternatives. Ablations on two dataset-model settings show that evidence localization and bounded editing are the main contributors to CAR's gains.

items.title_en: GM League Arena: An Interactive Long-Horizon Task Benchmark Based on Professional Sports League Management
items.title_zh: GM League Arena：基于职业体育联盟管理的交互式长时程任务基准
items.abstract_en: Long-horizon decision-making under sustained competition requires large language models (LLMs) to balance immediate investment with future resource needs. However, local success in multi-step interactions can not adequately capture cumulative decision effects or demonstrate long-term goal achievement under resource constraints and sustained competition. To address this gap, we introduce GM Bench, a benchmark for managing professional sports teams across seasons under resource constraints and competition among teams. We build the environment simulators for four sports and add financial constraints, player demands, and market mechanisms to establish a unified task across sports. Diverse rosters of comparable strength are constructed from real-world player data, and each LLM is evaluated as a team general manager to assess its long-term management capabilities. We evaluate competitive performance, cash reserves, and cross-season improvement across four sports. Over five NBA seasons, Claude Opus 5.5 ranks first among 29 LLMs, while GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol combine strong performance with larger cash reserves.

items.title_en: The Right Source Is Not Enough: Understanding History Interference in Speech-LLM Memory
items.title_zh: 正确的来源还不够：理解语音-LLM 记忆中的历史干扰
items.abstract_en: Speech large language models retain audio history to support multi-turn conversations. Yet remembering an event does not ensure that its information is used only when relevant. We investigate why irrelevant historical audio changes answers even when the queried event remains represented. Controlled experiments on MOSS-Audio and MiMo-Audio show that historical values direct errors toward specific competing answers, beyond a generic effect of context length. Causal interventions distinguish two paths. In open-ended question answering, most history-value errors disappear when subsequent computation cannot directly access the irrelevant source. In multiple-choice answering, many errors persist: early historical influence is carried by question-candidate states even after direct source access is blocked. Low-dimensional interventions further separate source-role information from answer-value information. Their effects peak at different depths, and changing the source-role signal does not eliminate the causal influence of competing values. On naturally occurring errors, strengthening the queried role and counteracting the historical value each improve answers; their joint intervention gives the greatest recovery. These findings support a failure of downstream evidence use beyond source identification alone: source-role information can influence a decision without exclusively controlling which historical values affect it. Reliable conversational memory therefore requires not only retention and retrieval, but also control over how retained information enters answer computation.

items.title_en: Whose Effect Is It? How Objectives Inflate Learned Subspace Interventions
items.title_zh: 这是谁的效果？目标如何夸大学习到的子空间干预
items.abstract_en: Interpretability often locates concepts by copying part of a language model's state from one input into another (activation patching). A larger output change counts as stronger evidence that this part carries the concept. Methods that learn which part to copy often change the output more than the whole state does. By that reading, learned parts isolate the concept more cleanly. Yet the whole contains the part. So whose effect is this excess, the network's or the method's? Copying the whole state learns nothing, so it shows what the network produces. We prove that, to first order, the effects of orthogonal parts add up to that of the whole. A part therefore exceeds the whole exactly when the rest moves the output back, which does not require isolating the concept more cleanly. Objectives that reward a larger effect select such parts. Distributed alignment search with cross-entropy, for example, exceeds the whole-state copy just before the output on almost all tasks, and inside the network at most sites. In both, changing only its objective to target what the network produces removes most of the excess. It therefore comes largely from the objective, so a larger learned effect alone is not stronger evidence.

items.title_en: Who is the Pronoun Pro? Comparing LLMs and Humans at Number-Disambiguation of 'they'
items.title_zh: 谁是代词高手？比较 LLM 与人类在“they”的单复数消歧上的表现
items.abstract_en: This study evaluates whether large language models (LLMs) can reliably replace or complement human research assistants in linguistically complex annotation. In a controlled annotation task, 73 human annotators (local students and crowdworkers with and without a background in linguistics) and more than 40 LLM configurations number-disambiguated 174 authentic uses of 'they' from Reddit, including innovative and context-sensitive cases. The best LLM, Kimi K3, reached 94.5% accuracy, above the human majority vote (86.2%) and the mean of the top half of human annotators (78.5%); only the single best human annotator scored higher (95.7%). LLMs also offer substantial practical advantages in cost and speed. However, qualitative error analysis reveals a crucial complementarity: human reasoning in low-agreement cases exposes inconsistencies in the annotation typology and thereby improves the methodological framework itself. The study contributes (i) a benchmark-style human-LLM comparison for a semantically demanding task, (ii) transparent cost and time evidence, and (iii) a methodological argument against a purely replacement-oriented view of automation. LLMs are viable for large-scale annotation support in linguistics, but their responsible use requires human critical oversight. The dataset with its gold-standard labels, all human and LLM annotations, and the fully reproducible code are openly available as a Quarto-based, public repository.

items.title_en: Shuffled OPSD: When Semantic Consistency Hurts On-Policy Self-Distillation?
items.title_zh: Shuffled OPSD：语义一致性何时会损害同策略自蒸馏？
items.abstract_en: Knowledge distillation improves a student model's reasoning ability through supervision from a teacher. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) uses the same model as both teacher and student under different contexts: the student generates reasoning trajectories from the question alone, while the teacher additionally receives a complete worked example and provides token-level supervision along those trajectories. Because the problem statement is shared, its content and ordering shape both student generation and teacher feedback. Preserving its semantic structure therefore seems natural, but does it always improve learning? We introduce Shuffled OPSD, which shuffles the words of the shared problem statement while keeping the teacher-only worked example intact. Across three mathematical reasoning benchmarks and three Qwen3 model scales, the method improves mean accuracy over both an intact-target control and Standard OPSD under matched training configurations. The largest gain over Standard OPSD is 3.52 percentage points on Qwen3-1.7B. Further controls show that preserving larger word blocks offers no advantage over word-level shuffling at the evaluated scales, whereas shuffling the teacher-only worked example reduces accuracy at every scale. Cross-problem mixing and target-removal experiments further distinguish the roles of problem content, word order, and teacher context. These results show that disrupting the shared problem statement can improve learning, while disrupting the teacher-only reference hurts performance. They challenge semantic coherence as a universally beneficial principle for OPSD and motivate closer study of how input structure shapes student generation and teacher supervision.

items.title_en: HERIT: Enabling Global Access to Hanja-to-English Historical Translation by Mitigating Temporal Bias
items.title_zh: HERIT：通过缓解时间偏差实现 Hanja 到英语历史翻译的全球访问
items.abstract_en: Historical archives are invaluable for multidisciplinary research but remain inaccessible globally due to severe language barriers. While manual translation is prohibitively expensive and time-consuming, simply applying existing machine translation models is inadequate due to unique linguistic nuances and the temporal bias inherent in scarce human-labeled corpora. To address these challenges, we propose HERIT, a systematic domain-adaptation pipeline that leverages retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to generate high-quality pseudo-labeled data from abundant Hanja-Korean corpora. This approach substantially expands the training dataset, mitigating both data scarcity and temporal overfitting across different historical periods. Extensive automated and human evaluations demonstrate that HERIT consistently outperforms baselines. Finally, we translate previously untranslated portions of the archives using our model, thereby enabling global access to these resources for researchers.

items.title_en: Residual Attribute Leakage Is an Interface: Auditing Privacy Evaluation After Text De-identification
items.title_zh: 残余属性泄露是一个接口：文本去标识化后隐私评估的审计
items.abstract_en: A privacy evaluation of de-identified text asks a language model (the adversary) to guess a person's protected attribute. We introduce a prior-normalised clipped leakage score of its confidence gain on the true value and audit the conclusions drawn from it. Each verdict depends on an evaluation interface (the queried person, answer options, prior, adversary model and scoring rule), which we vary on fixed releases of three corpora. In a stress test, an editor that writes the opposite-sex form at the same spans a redaction editor would redact misleads the adversary about most people, yet ranks first among editors scored on the same MedQA entries under this score, as under attack accuracy and proper scoring rules read as privacy. A relabelling-invariant reading of AUC ranks that editor sixth of eight, and a rule-aware adversary recovers the attribute from the same text. On ordinary releases most verdict changes are gains or losses of separability; of six choices varied over all pairs, only the adversary reverses comparisons (5 of its 124 changes), and the query can target the wrong person. SACC, a traceable editor we build as the instrument, lets us ablate two editing principles and show where its advantage does not hold.

items.title_en: PROSE: Preservation-Constrained Selective Editing for Guilty Bias in Legal Judgment Prediction
items.title_zh: PROSE：面向法律判决预测中有罪偏差的保留约束选择性编辑
items.abstract_en: Legal judgment prediction models may retain a guilty verdict after a legally decisive condition has been altered such that the specified charge is no longer established. We study this guilty bias via selective repair over matched charge-established and charge-not-established cases, where the unsupported verdict should change while its supported counterpart remains stable. We construct CAIL-MC, a legally reviewed dataset of 11,478 matched pairs covering 261 Chinese criminal charges. Held-out activation interventions show that contrasts learned from correctly resolved pairs transfer to false-guilty cases, but target-reaching interventions can also damage matched supported-guilty decisions. Motivated by this observation, we introduce PROSE, which reconstructs case-specific targets from a training-derived residual geometry, aligns them with a local margin-descent signal, attenuates supported-guilty-sensitive components, and realizes bounded targets through a preservation-regularized low-rank parameter update. Across Qwen3-8B and GLM4-9B, PROSE achieves stronger pairwise safe repair and evidence sensitivity, while preserving standard single-pass inference.

items.title_en: TraceRouter++: Causal Semantic Routing Realignment via Optimal Transport
items.title_zh: TraceRouter++：基于最优传输的因果语义路由重对齐
items.abstract_en: Despite their remarkable capabilities, large foundation models (LFMs) remain susceptible to adversarial manipulation. Current safety intervention methods primarily rely on the \textit{locality hypothesis}, rigidly suppressing isolated neurons or features. However, harmful semantics manifest as distributed, cross-layer circuits, rendering localized ablations both brittle against complex jailbreaks and detrimental to general utility. To bridge this gap, we propose TraceRouter++, a routing-level safety intervention framework that explicitly traces safety-relevant causal routing pathways activated under harmful inputs and realigns their unsafe activation states. Our framework operates in a \textit{Discover-Trace-Realign} paradigm: it first pinpoints a sensitive onset layer via attention divergence and disentangles dense activations into interpretable routing features using sparse autoencoders (SAEs). Subsequently, it maps these features to downstream causal circuits via feature influence scores (FIS). Crucially, departing from rigid suppression paradigms, TraceRouter++ introduces a constrained optimal transport (OT)-based soft routing realignment. By formulating safety intervention as a tractable coordinate-wise marginal optimal transport approximation, our method redirects unsafe activation marginals toward safe-reference marginals within causally identified routing subspaces while preserving non-selected coordinates at the intervention point. This mechanism safely redirects malicious semantic flows while leaving orthogonal computational routes intact. Extensive experiments across representative large language models (LLMs), multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and diffusion models (DMs) show that TraceRouter++ outperforms evaluated baselines, improving adversarial robustness while maintaining a favorable safety-utility trade-off. WARNING: This paper contains unsafe model responses.

items.title_en: One Assistant, Many Memories: Benchmarking Real-World Group Assistance When Recall Is Not Enough
items.title_zh: 一个助手，多重记忆：当召回不足时对真实世界群体协助进行基准评测
items.abstract_en: The value of memory lies not only in recall but in using it to provide appropriate assistance. Recent benchmarks test memory use in personalisation and agentic tasks, but seldom evaluate assistance without fixed answers or integration across multiple participants. Group chats make both challenges more acute: an assistant must integrate information from multiple members, track revisions and conflicts over time, and produce one response for the group. Yet existing group memory benchmarks rely on synthetic conversations and inherit constrained evaluation from general memory benchmarks, focusing on recall against fixed answers or decisions over a closed set. We introduce GroupAssistBench, the first memory benchmark from real-world group conversations with a deployed group assistant, covering 80,299 messages in 50 groups and costing over $53K. Over the same histories, GroupAssistBench evaluates memory recall (L1) with reference answers and memory use (L2) with service requests without fixed answers across single, distributed, and conflicting memories (M1--M3). Requests are verified to require group history, memories are anchored to their sources, and L2 uses tailored rubrics with penalties derived from real user feedback. Across evaluations of frontier models with full context, retrieval methods, and memory systems, the strongest memory system rivals full context on recall but falls far behind on use, especially for distributed and conflicting memories. Together, two additions that relate retrieved memories and bind remembered facts as response constraints bring consistent gains, showing that group memory systems must improve use, not recall alone.

items.title_en: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
items.title_zh: 更少思考，局部进行：面向推理压缩的局部偏好学习
items.abstract_en: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. Existing reasoning compression methods primarily operate on reasoning trajectories, paying less attention to the local decision of whether further reasoning is necessary given the current state. We propose LoCo, a local preference learning method for reasoning compression. LoCo detects candidate overthinking states from the model's own traces, freezes the corresponding reasoning prefixes, regenerates shorter verified continuations from the same states, and trains on the resulting state-conditioned preference pairs with DPO. This formulation teaches the model when to continue reasoning and when to conclude, rather than simply encouraging shorter trajectories overall. We construct training data entirely from self-generated mathematical traces and evaluate LoCo on five mathematical and three code generation benchmarks. LoCo reduces completion length by 41.7\%--45.4\% on mathematics and 23.4\%--36.3\% on code, while maintaining or improving accuracy and achieving the best AUC across all code benchmarks. LoCo consistently improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off on mathematics and transfers effectively to code generation despite math-only training, demonstrating the cross-domain generality of local preference learning for reasoning compression. The code and model will be publicly released at https://github.com/MuyaoYuan/LoCo.

items.title_en: Where Is the Truth When AI Agents Disagree? Dependence-Aware Belief Propagation for Unsupervised Truth Discovery (Extended Version)
items.abstract_en: LLM agents often give conflicting answers to the same question, and many deployed agents are variants of one base model, so their errors are correlated. We study truth discovery among such agents: inferring the true answer and each agent's reliability without labels. Classical truth-discovery and crowdsourcing estimators reward an agreeing bloc and can fall below majority vote. We propose BP-TD, which adds per-agent decorrelation weights to mean-field variational inference on a one-coin Dawid-Skene model, so that agents sharing a base model count together as about one vote. Its first iteration is exactly a weighted vote; later iterations estimate agent reliability. With 13 local agents on MMLU, BP-TD beats majority vote without any labels (0.716 vs. 0.624 on 160 questions; 0.707 vs. 0.674 on 10,000) and ranks agents by their true accuracy, which classical estimators invert. The gain depends on the pool: over 2,852 sub-pools of four benchmarks, decorrelation helps when the largest correlated bloc is weaker than the other agents and hurts when it is the strongest, and we found no label-free statistic that tells the two cases apart. Labels change the picture quickly: with 20 labelled questions, selecting the single best agent is more accurate than every aggregator we tested on MMLU, ARC and TruthfulQA.

items.title_en: ReSI-Math: Exploring Recoverable Capability Frontiers for Efficient Reasoning Improvement
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective approach for improving mathematical reasoning in large language models. However, a fundamental question remains: when a model fails to solve a problem, does it truly lack the underlying capability? In this work, we reveal that direct failure does not necessarily imply inability. Some reasoning failures can be recovered by exploring the model's own trajectories, exposing a recoverable capability frontier: a policy-dependent region where solutions are not reliably generated through direct decoding but can be elicited through trajectory-level search. Based on this observation, we introduce ReSI-Math, a framework that explores recoverable capability frontiers and converts recovered capabilities into data-efficient RLVR supervision. ReSI-Math uses Self-Judge-guided evolutionary search to identify recoverable failures under a fixed policy and adaptively selects frontier problems for sequential RLVR as the policy evolves. On Qwen3-VL-8B, correct-incorrect trajectory crossover produces 272 verifier-confirmed correct offspring from 621 attempts (43.8%). After three sequential one-shot RLVR stages, the MATH500 and WE-MATH average improves from 78.71 to 80.16. Under matched single-problem RLVR, random selection reaches only 53.31 versus 54.16 for frontier-guided Q1.

items.title_en: When Ground Truth Is Not Ground Truth: Automatic Labeling for Hallucination Detection
items.abstract_en: Hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) remain a major challenge, as they can produce misleading, factually incorrect, or unverifiable information, thereby undermining their trustworthiness and reliability. However, reliable ground-truth labels remain a key challenge in evaluating hallucination detectors. Recent studies often construct labels automatically by comparing model generations with reference answers using similarity metrics such as BLEURT. This implicitly treats BLEURT similarity as a proxy for hallucination, despite its English-centric supervision, unbounded score range, and design as a similarity metric rather than a factuality measure, making threshold-based ground-truth construction potentially unreliable. Through comprehensive experiments using 15 automatic supervision judges, seven hallucination detection baselines, two generator models, two QA datasets, and five languages, we demonstrate that detector performance varies substantially with the choice of supervision judge. Human validation reveals substantial differences in labeling reliability, with QGen-9B achieving the lowest overall misclassification rate (12.86%), while BLEURT and BLEURT-n exhibit rates of 47.23% and 47.32%, respectively. Our findings highlight the limitations of automatic similarity-based labeling and the need for more reliable judging methods that better capture semantic and factual correctness.

items.title_en: CardioVascBench:Prioritized Diagnosis Generation from Real-World Chinese Cardiovascular Records
items.title_zh: CardioVascBench：基于真实世界中文心血管病历的优先级诊断生成
items.abstract_en: Identifying the primary diagnosis alone does not fully characterize a model's diagnosis-generation performance. We introduce CardioVascBench, a retrospective benchmark for prioritized diagnosis generation from real-world Chinese cardiovascular inpatient records. It contains 3,262 de-identified cases, with 2,174 for training and 1,088 for evaluation, linking clinical narratives and textual ECG reports to expert-verified, ordered discharge diagnoses standardized to ICD-10. An English translation of the evaluation set supports aligned cross-lingual comparison. Our evaluation protocol combines terminology normalization and rank-aware scoring to separately assess primary-diagnosis identification, reference-diagnosis coverage, and list precision. Evaluation across 36 systems shows that higher primary-diagnosis accuracy does not necessarily imply higher list precision against discharge references. We also provide CardioKG-Agent, a knowledge-enhanced baseline combining entity normalization, constrained graph retrieval, and guideline evidence. In a staged comparison of three baseline models, supervised fine-tuning plus the agent achieves a 73.5% higher mean composite score than fine-tuning alone, representing a system-level gain. These results measure retrospective agreement with recorded diagnoses; agreement between metric rankings and physician judgments remains to be validated. CardioVascBench supports research on diagnosis prioritization and knowledge-enhanced generation.

items.title_en: MIMIC-Note-Extract: A Large-Scale Structured Dataset Extracted from MIMIC-IV-Note Discharge Summaries
items.title_zh: MIMIC-Note-Extract：从MIMIC-IV-Note出院小结中提取的大规模结构化数据集
items.abstract_en: MIMIC is one of the most widely used public hospital datasets for machine learning on electronic health records, yet clinically important information, such as past medical history, allergies, and diagnostic findings, remains confined to free-text discharge summaries. Studies requiring this information must therefore build their own extraction pipelines, duplicating substantial effort across projects. We release MIMIC-Note-Extract (MNE), a large-scale dataset that uses a hybrid extraction pipeline combining deterministic parsing with schema-guided large language model generation to transform 16 sections from 300,720 discharge summaries into structured tables.
